patents.title: ACIDES NUCLÉIQUES CODANT POUR DES PROTÉINES DE FUSION CHIMÉRIQUES MODIFIÉES
patents.abstract: What is disclosed herein are nucleic acids encoding a chimeric fusion protein comprising an extracellular domain that comprises an antigen binding domain, particularly a TROP2 binding domain. patents.title: PARTITIONING ANION EXCHANGE CHROMATOGRAPHY FOR PURIFICATION OF RECOMBINANT ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUS (rAAV)
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present inventions provide methods for purifying adeno-associated viruses (AAV) that comprise gene of interest (GOI). The present inventions provide partitioning anion-exchange chromatography (AEX), leveraging surface charge differences between empty and full capsids to create an environment of on-column competition for binding sites. This results in empty capsids being removed during the column loading phase, allowing the bulk of full capsids to be eluted in a concentrated, highly enriched pool. The inventions also provide methods for conducting partitioning anion-exchange chromatography in rapid cycling mode for AAV purification process intensification.
patents.assignee: REGENERON PHARMA [US]; Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a partitioning anion-exchange chromatography (AEX) method that exploits surface charge differences between empty and full AAV capsids to selectively remove empty capsids during column loading while concentrating full capsids in a single enriched pool. This represents a significant advancement in AAV purification efficiency and process intensification, particularly relevant for in vivo gene therapy applications where empty capsid contamination must be minimized and manufacturing scalability is critical.

patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents a nanoparticle-based approach for extracorporeal transfection of immune effector cells using surface-exposed binding moieties to target and deliver CAR or TCR-encoding nucleic acids directly to cells in blood or blood fractions. This represents a potentially significant advance in ex vivo cell engineering by enabling direct transfection without cell isolation/enrichment steps, which could reduce processing complexity and manufacturing costs for CAR-T and TCR-engineered T cell therapies.

patents.title: MÉTHODES ET COMPOSITION POUR INDUIRE L'ACTIVATION ET L'EXPRESSION D'ADN DANS DES LYMPHOCYTES T
patents.abstract: The disclosure relates to nanoparticles comprising a surface-exposed immune cell binding moiety, a transposable element comprising a gene sequence flanked by inverted terminal repeats (ITRs), a nucleic acid encoding a transposase with specificity for the ITRs, and an mRNA encoding a first chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) or T-cell receptor (TCR). Methods are also described for treating a disease or disorder by administering such nanoparticles to a subject in need thereof.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent presents nanoparticles engineered with surface-binding moieties that deliver transposable elements and mRNA encoding CAR or TCR directly to T lymphocytes, enabling in situ gene expression without ex vivo cell engineering. The integration of transposon-based delivery with mRNA co-delivery in a single nanoparticle platform represents a potentially significant advance for in vivo CAR-T manufacturing, addressing the manufacturing bottleneck and accessibility challenges of current ex vivo approaches.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS ET COMPOSITIONS POUR ADMINISTRER UNE CONSTRUCTION NUCLÉIQUE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure includes a composition including a) one or more nucleic acid constructs, wherein the one or more nucleic acid constructs encode: at least one of Replicase 68 (Rep68) and Replicase 78 (Rep78); and at least one protein of viral origin having nucleic acid replication and/or transgene amplification promotion activity, and b) nucleic acid construct comprising a coding region encoding at least one gene of interest (GOI) and at least one inverted terminal repeat (ITR) sequence on each side of the GOI, and methods of making and using the composition.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a dual-component nucleic acid delivery system combining Rep68/Rep78 replication proteins with ITR-flanked gene-of-interest constructs to enable autonomous plasmid amplification in target cells. This approach potentially offers improved transgene expression kinetics and reduced dosing requirements compared to conventional non-viral delivery, with relevance to in vivo CAR-T applications through enhanced persistence of engineered T cell payloads without integration.

patents.title: MOYENS ET MÉTHODES D'ADMINISTRATION D'AGENTS À DES CELLULES EFFECTRICES IMMUNITAIRES
patents.abstract: The current disclosure relates to targeted delivery of agents to T cells and/or NK cells. Highly suitable targeting domains were meticulously identified that allow for an agent, such as DNA and/or RNA, to be delivered to T cells and/or NK cells. As shown, when lipid nanoparticles were provided with such a targeting domain, nucleic acid comprised in said lipid nanoparticles was highly efficiently and specifically delivered. This allows for engineering of T cells and/or NK cells, highly useful in medical treatments for cancer.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) functionalized with novel targeting domains that achieve high efficiency and specificity for delivery of nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) to T cells and NK cells. This targeted delivery technology is significant for CAR-T and other engineered T cell therapies, as it provides an alternative to viral vectors for in vivo cell engineering while potentially reducing off-target effects and improving clinical efficacy in cancer treatment.

patents.title: VECTEURS VIRAUX À INTÉGRATION ET À AUTO-INACTIVATION ET CONSTRUCTIONS ET UTILISATIONS DE CEUX-CI
patents.abstract: The present disclosure relates to gene delivery systems and methods of producing and using single constructs or viral vectors that carry a transposon and a transposase gene that is functional in target cells and not functional in producer cells.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses viral vectors carrying both a transposon and a transposase gene with cell-type-specific functionality (active in target cells, inactive in producer cells), enabling safer gene delivery with self-inactivating properties. This dual-component approach offers a competitive advantage for in vivo CAR-T by reducing genotoxic risk during manufacturing while maintaining therapeutic transgene integration in target lymphocytes.

patents.title: SYSTÈMES ET PROCÉDÉS DE CONCENTRATION DE POPULATIONS DE CELLULES TRIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are devices, systems, and methods for sorting, concentrating, and dispensing a single particle or a small number of particles from a sample in a continuous, integrated workflow to facilitate downstream particle analysis. Such methods, devices, and systems can be used to identify, sort, change the particle concentration, and dispense a subset of particles or a single particle from a sample into a well in a multi-well plate or strip. Using microfluidics and acoustic field technologies to perform particle sorting, concentrating, and dispensing in a single device or system allows for streamlining the steps into a continuous, integrated process as compared to traditional flow cytometry systems.
patents.assignee: NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL INC [US]; NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL, INC.

patents.title: SYSTEMES MICROFLUIDIQUES ET PROCEDES DE TRI DE PARTICULES
patents.abstract:
[0001]    Provided herein are devices, systems, and methods for particle sorting, including cell sorting, using microfluidics cartridges and microchips and the manufacture of the microfluidics cartridges and microchips by high-throughput approaches. Such methods, devices, and systems can be used to identify, sort, and collect a subset of particles or a single particle from a sample. The capability to manufacture such microfluidic tools in high volume may lower production costs and allow for the microfluidic tools to be used as consumables.
[0002]    L'invention concerne des dispositifs, des systèmes et des procédés de tri de particules, comprenant le tri de cellules, à l'aide de cartouches microfluidiques et de micropuces et la fabrication des cartouches microfluidiques et des micropuces par des approches à haut débit. De tels procédés, dispositifs et systèmes peuvent être utilisés pour identifier, trier et collecter un sous-ensemble de particules ou une particule unique à partir d'un
patents.assignee: NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL INC [US]; NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes high-throughput manufacturing approaches for microfluidic cartridges and microchips enabling cost-effective, consumable-grade cell sorting devices. This is relevant to CAR-T manufacturing as it addresses scalable, automated cell enrichment and isolation—critical steps in clinical-grade CAR-T production where selecting target T cell populations improves therapeutic efficacy and reduces off-target effects.

patents.title: Polysaccharide core Nanocells as well as preparation method and application thereof
patents.abstract: The invention discloses polysaccharide core Nanocells as well as a preparation method and application thereof. Each polysaccharide core Nanocell is of a core-shell structure, a nanoparticle made of a polysaccharide material serve as a core, the outer layer of the nanoparticle is wrapped with a lipid membrane which is formed by a lipid material and similar to a lipidosome capsule membrane, and a medicine is entrapped in the nanoparticle, and/or between the lipid membrane and the nanoparticle core, and/or entrapped on the lipid membrane. According to the polysaccharide core Nanocells, different lipid materials can be adopted, or lipid is modified with different targeting guide molecules, and magnetic particles are wrapped or materials or medicines sensitive to the microenvironment of a corresponding disease site are added, so that the polysaccharide core Nanocell with different targeting functions is obtained; medicines of various mechanisms can be simultaneously entrapped, so that multi
patents.assignee: UNIV JINAN; 暨南大学
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a core-shell nanoparticle with a polysaccharide core surrounded by a lipid membrane, capable of encapsulating therapeutics at multiple locations within the structure. The modular design allowing lipid modification with targeting ligands and incorporation of magnetic particles offers potential advantages for controlled delivery in cell therapy applications, though the patent does not specifically address CAR-T or T cell engineering applications.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS ET MÉTHODES DE MODULATION DE LYMPHOCYTES T
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods for delivering an engineered immune receptor to immune cells, e.g., T cells, in vivo, ex vivo, or in vitro. Provided are recombinant nucleic acids and templates that are useful for immune cell reprogramming with high specificity and efficiency.
patents.assignee: AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IL]; AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses recombinant nucleic acids and templates for delivering engineered immune receptors to T cells across in vivo, ex vivo, and in vitro contexts, with emphasis on high specificity and efficiency in immune cell reprogramming. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as it addresses the delivery challenge—a critical bottleneck—by providing novel nucleic acid compositions and delivery templates that may enable direct in vivo T cell engineering without ex vivo manipulation.

patents.title: Engineered retrotransposable element proteins for gene delivery and insertion
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods for enhancing the integration of a transgene into a genome.
patents.assignee: AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IL]; AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered retrotransposable element proteins designed to enhance transgene integration into host genomes, offering a potentially safer and more efficient alternative to viral vectors for gene delivery. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T applications as it could enable non-viral, integrating delivery of CAR constructs with reduced immunogenicity and off-target integration risks compared to conventional lentiviral or gamma-retroviral approaches.

patents.title: Recombinant proteins comprising non-ltr retrotransposon-derived polypeptides for gene delivery and insertion
patents.assignee: AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IL]; TRUDEAU DEVIN [IL]; BEN SHUSHAN GOLECZKI YARON [IL]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes recombinant proteins containing non-LTR retrotransposon-derived polypeptides as novel gene delivery vehicles. This represents a non-viral delivery approach potentially applicable to CAR-T engineering by enabling integration-capable gene transfer without conventional viral vectors, which could reduce immunogenicity and manufacturing complexity.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS POUR LA TRANSCRIPTION INVERSE AMORCÉE PAR LA CIBLE
patents.abstract: Provided herein are nucleic acid constructs and systems for target primed reverse transcription gene insertion. The constructs and systems may comprise a non-naturally occurring nucleic acid molecule comprising a 3' UTR sequence comprising a mutation relative to a wild-type R2 3' UTR sequence.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ADDITION THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered nucleic acid constructs with mutated 3' UTR sequences derived from R2 retrotransposons for target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT)-mediated gene insertion. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T lies in potentially enabling non-viral, integration-competent gene delivery that could circumvent limitations of conventional viral vectors (immunogenicity, manufacturing constraints) while achieving genomic integration without double-strand break requirements.

patents.title: QUEUES D'ARN POUR TRANSCRIPTION INVERSE AMORCÉE CIBLE
patents.abstract: Provided herein are nucleic acid constructs and systems for target primed reverse transcription gene insertion.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ADDITION THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes nucleic acid constructs and systems designed specifically for target primed reverse transcription (TPRT)-mediated gene insertion, a mechanism distinct from traditional viral integration. This represents a potentially advantageous gene delivery approach for in vivo applications where precise genomic integration without viral scaffolding could reduce immunogenicity and improve safety/efficacy profiles for CAR-T and other cell therapies.

patents.title: INSERTION D'ACIDE NUCLÉIQUE CHEZ DES JEUNES MAMMIFÈRES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods and systems for modifying a target nucleic acid in a cell of a subject. The methods and systems may comprise providing the cell with a first nucleic acid comprising (i) a 5' untranslated region (UTR) sequence and a 3' untranslated region (UTR) sequence, and (ii) a template sequence. The methods and systems may further comprise providing the cell with an R2 retroelement polypeptide or a second nucleic acid encoding the R2 retroelement polypeptide. The R2 retroelement polypeptide may insert the template sequence or a reverse complement thereof into the target nucleic acid. The subject may be a mammal less than 6 weeks of age.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; GREGOIRE FRANCINE M [US]; UPTON HEATHER [US]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a novel approach to in vivo nucleic acid insertion in young mammals using R2 retroelement polypeptides to precisely insert template sequences into target genomic loci. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T therapy lies in enabling direct genetic modification of T cells in neonatal/juvenile subjects without ex vivo cell engineering, potentially simplifying manufacturing and allowing therapeutic intervention at developmental windows when T cell function may be more plastic.

patents.title: SYSTÈMES À COMPOSANTS MULTIPLES POUR MODIFICATIONS GÉNOMIQUES SPÉCIFIQUES À UN SITE
patents.abstract: Provided herein are genome editing systems comprising a reverse transcriptase and a template RNA with a translation-incapable 5' cap (TI-CAP) encoding a payload. The genome editing systems can be used to target, edit, modify, or manipulate a DNA sequence at one or more locations in a safe harbor site of the genome of a cell.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ADDITION THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: Novel genome editing systems combining reverse transcriptase with translation-incapable 5' cap (TI-CAP) RNA templates for targeted genomic integration into safe harbor sites. This approach enables payload delivery with reduced immunogenicity and off-target effects, providing a potentially safer platform for engineering T cells and other therapeutics by directing modifications to predefined genomic loci rather than random integration.

patents.title: MÉTHODES DE TRAITEMENT D'UNE MALADIE À L'AIDE D'ANTICORPS ANTI-CD47 X ANTI-MÉSOTHÉLINE EN COMBINAISON AVEC UNE CHIMIOTHÉRAPIE
patents.abstract: The invention relates method of treatment of cancer using novel bispecific antibodies carrying a different specificity for each binding site of the immunoglobulin molecule, where one of the binding sites is specific for CD47 and the second is specific for mesothelin (MSLN). In addition, the disclosure contains methods of combination treatment using novel bispecific antibodies in combination with paclitaxel.
patents.assignee: NOVIMMUNE SA [CH]; NOVIMMUNE SA
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses bispecific antibodies with dual specificity for CD47 (immune checkpoint) and mesothelin (tumor antigen), designed to block the "don't eat me" signal while targeting mesothelin-expressing cancers. Competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is indirect but potentially complementary: CD47 blocking can enhance CAR-T cell infiltration and effector function against mesothelin+ tumors, making this a synergistic combination approach rather than a direct CAR-T technology.

patents.title: ANTIGENBINDENDE POLYPEPTIDE GEGEN CD229
patents.abstract: The invention relates to antigen-binding polypeptides comprising the CDR1, CDR2 and CDR3 region of a VHH domain of a camelid heavy chain antibody. The polypeptides bind specifically to CD229 and are therefore suitable for the diagnosis as well as for the therapeutic and prophylactic treatment of diseases characterised by increased CD229 expression. Fusion proteins, conjugates and pharmaceutical compositions comprising the antigen-binding polypeptides are also disclosed. In addition, the invention relates to the use of such antigen-binding polypeptides in methods for detecting CD229 or CD229-expressing cells in a biological sample. Methods for purifying and concentrating CD229 or CD229-expressing cells using the antigen-binding polypeptides are also described.
patents.assignee: UNIV HAMBURG EPPENDORF [DE]; Universitätsklinikum Hamburg-Eppendorf
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes novel VHH domain-based antigen-binding polypeptides (nanobodies) that specifically target CD229, with applications in diagnosis and therapeutic/prophylactic treatment of CD229-overexpressing diseases. This is potentially significant for CAR-T engineering as CD229 is an activating receptor on T cells; nanobody-based targeting agents could enable selective T cell engagement, enrichment, or modulation in manufacturing or therapeutic contexts.

patents.title: VIRUS FONCTIONNALISÉS, COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to functionalized viruses (non-recombinant or recombinant) comprising a plurality of capsid-displayed drug molecules (e.g., chemotherapeutic agents), where the displayed drug molecules are attached to the capsid by a linker comprising a biocompatible polymer (e.g., PEG). In some embodiments the linker comprises a cleavable spacer, which enables release of the attached drug within and/or in close proximity to a transduced cell. In some embodiments a functionalized virus is a recombinant virus that, in addition to capsid-linked drug molecules also encodes a therapeutic agent (e.g., a protein or polynucleotide) for expression in a target cell to be transduced. Also provided are pharmaceutical compositions comprising such functionalized viruses. Also provided are methods for generating such functionalized viruses, as well as methods for their use in treatment of diseases, e.g., cancers. The present invention also relates to drug conjugates of CBL0137 and at le
patents.assignee: STAMFORD PHARMACEUTICALS INC [US]; STAMFORD PHARMACEUTICALS INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention provides functionalized viral vectors displaying multiple drug molecules on capsid surfaces via biocompatible polymer linkers with cleavable spacers, enabling dual delivery of chemotherapeutic agents and encoded therapeutic payloads (proteins/polynucleotides) to target cells. This represents a novel viral engineering approach for simultaneous cytotoxic and gene therapy delivery, potentially enabling enhanced anti-tumor efficacy in cell therapy applications through combination modality mechanisms.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ ET APPAREIL DE TRI ET DE CULTURE DE CELLULES, DISPOSITIF INFORMATIQUE ET SUPPORT DE STOCKAGE
patents.abstract: The present application relates to the technical field of biomedicine. Provided are a cell sorting and culturing method and apparatus, a computer device, and a storage medium. The cell sorting and culturing method comprises separating a sample solution by means of a density gradient centrifugation method to obtain a cell solution to be cultured; conveying said cell solution to a culturing device by means of a first pipeline switching operation, and culturing said cell solution to obtain a cultured cell solution; and acquiring the cultured cell solution by means of a second pipeline switching operation, and concentrating and washing the cultured cell solution to obtain a target cell solution. The cell sorting and culturing method can ensure a fully enclosed one-stop sterile operating environment, avoid the risk of contamination during cell operation site changing, and improve the cell treatment stability. In addition, continuous operation between cell solution sorting and culturing trea
patents.assignee: BEIJING CELLBRI FUTURE BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 北京赛桥未来生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes an automated, fully enclosed pipeline system for cell sorting via density gradient centrifugation, culturing, and concentration/washing in a sterile environment. The novelty lies in the integrated apparatus design and automated pipeline switching operations that maintain sterility throughout the process, which could reduce manual handling contamination risk and improve consistency in cell therapy manufacturing.

patents.title: ADDITIFS POUR LA PRODUCTION DE VECTEURS VIRAUX
patents.abstract: Among other things, the present disclosure provides methods, systems, and compositions for production of viral vectors, e.g., recombinant viral vectors, e.g., recombinant adeno-associated viruses (rAAVs). In some embodiments, a method comprises addition of one or more additives to a medium comprising host cells. In some embodiments, an addition of an additive to a medium can provide increased titer of produced recombinant viral vector particles, e.g., rAAV particles. In some embodiments, an additive comprises momelotinib or a salt or derivative thereof.
patents.assignee: BIOGEN MA INC [US]; BIOGEN MA INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses additives (notably momelotinib and derivatives) added to cell culture media to increase titer of recombinant viral vector production, particularly rAAV. This addresses a critical manufacturing bottleneck in viral vector production for gene therapy, offering potential cost and efficiency advantages for scaling CAR-T and other cell therapy manufacturing pipelines that rely on viral transduction.

patents.title: DOSAGE RÉPÉTÉ DE RÉTROTRANSPOSONS
patents.abstract: The present disclosure demonstrates that earlier editing of cells with ribosomal non-LTR retrotransposons (R elements) still allowed sufficient editing from subsequent dosing of R elements, without significant interference therebetween, whether they are the same R elements or different. Provided are compositions and methods for integrating one or more exogenous sequence(s) to the genome of a mammalian cell, comprising (a) introducing to the cell a first amount of one or more polynucleotide(s) comprising a first ribosomal non-long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposon (R element) which comprises a first exogenous sequence, and, (b) introducing to the cell a second amount of one or more polynucleotide(s) comprising a second R element.
patents.assignee: TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; UNIV TOKYO [JP]; TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent demonstrates that sequential dosing of non-LTR retrotransposons (R elements) for genome editing can be performed without significant mutual interference, enabling multiple rounds of precise genomic integration in mammalian cells. This is significant for CAR-T and gene therapy applications as it enables iterative, multi-step genetic modifications of therapeutic cells, potentially allowing stacked integration of multiple therapeutic transgenes or correction sequences in a single cell population.

patents.title: NOUVEAUX RÉTROTRANSPOSONS R2 POUR L'ÉCRITURE GÉNIQUE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure describes numerous new R2 retrotransposons discovered from various species. These R2 retrotransposons exhibited good retrotransposition activities in human cells. These new retrotransposons, as well as engineered versions thereof, can be suitably used for targeted gene delivery.
patents.assignee: TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: Novel R2 retrotransposons from diverse species with demonstrated retrotransposition activity in human cells, engineered for targeted gene delivery applications. Competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T: represents an alternative non-viral delivery mechanism potentially applicable to CAR-T cell engineering, with potential advantages in avoiding immunogenicity associated with viral vectors and enabling precise genomic integration.

patents.title: RÉTROTRANSPOSONS R2 POUR L'ÉCRITURE GÉNIQUE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure describes new R2 retrotransposons discovered from bird species. Two of them, from Corvus moneduloides (New Caledonian crow) and Accipiter gentilis (Eurasian goshawk) and referred to as R2Cm and R2Ag, respectively, exhibited excellent retrotransposition activities in human cells. These new retrotransposons, as well as engineered versions thereof, can be suitably used for targeted gene delivery.
patents.assignee: TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; UNIV TOKYO [JP]; TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: Novel R2 retrotransposons (R2Cm from New Caledonian crow and R2Ag from Eurasian goshawk) with high retrotransposition activity in human cells, engineered for targeted gene delivery applications. This represents a new class of non-viral gene delivery vectors with potential advantages for in vivo CAR-T engineering through chromosomal integration without viral immunogenicity concerns.

patents.title: PROTÉINE DE FUSION DESTINÉE À ÊTRE UTILISÉE EN TANT QU'ENGAGEUR DE CELLULES IMMUNITAIRES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are immune cell engagers. The immune cell engager may include a cell binding domain, an immune cell adhesion molecule, an immune cell costimulatory molecule, or a combination thereof. Methods of use and production are further provided.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses fusion proteins functioning as immune cell engagers with modular architecture combining cell-binding domains with immune cell adhesion and/or costimulatory molecules. This represents a novel approach to redirecting and activating T cells without requiring genetic modification, offering potential advantages in manufacturing simplicity and off-the-shelf therapeutic deployment compared to traditional CAR-T platforms.

patents.title: ACTIVATEUR MULTISPÉCIFIQUE DES CELLULES IMMUNITAIRES ET SES UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: Provided here are immune cell engagers and multispecific immune cell engagers. Some such embodiments include an adhesion molecule linked to a costimulatory molecule or an immune cell binding domain and a target cell binding domain. The disclosure also includes vectors such as lentiviral vectors, cells, and methods that may relate to or include such engagers. The multispecific immune cell engagers may incorporate a fusion molecule comprising a CD58 extracellular domain, an anti-CD3 antibody, a CD80 or CD86 extracellular domain, and a target cell binding domain.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses multispecific immune cell engagers incorporating adhesion molecules (CD58), costimulatory domains (CD80/CD86), anti-CD3 antibodies, and target cell binding domains in fusion constructs, delivered via lentiviral vectors for in vivo T cell activation. This represents a novel architecture for dual costimulation and engagement that could enhance CAR-T potency by combining adhesion-mediated signaling with traditional costimulatory signals, offering potential advantages in tumor penetration and persistence.

patents.title: FABRICATION DE PARTICULES VIRALES
patents.abstract: Provided are methods for large scale production of viral particles, and compositions and methods for using said viral particles.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses methods for large-scale production of viral particles with potential applications in cell and gene therapy. Given Umoja Biopharma's focus on in vivo CAR-T therapies, this likely covers manufacturing innovations for viral vectors used in T cell engineering, offering competitive advantages in scalable GMP production and cost reduction for therapeutic viral particle delivery systems.

patents.title: ADMINISTRATION LENTIVIRALE DE RÉCEPTEURS ANTIGÉNIQUES CHIMÉRIQUES ANTI-CD22
patents.abstract: Provided herein are particles comprising polynucleotide constructs for generating cells expressing anti-CD22 chimeric antigen receptor, as well as vectors, such as lentiviral vectors, comprising same, cells comprising same, and methods of using same. Some embodiments include a surface-engineered lentiviral vector. In some embodiments, the lentiviral vector further encodes a synthetic receptor protein.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS USA LTD [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent covers lentiviral vector-based delivery of anti-CD22 CAR-T constructs with surface-engineering modifications and optional synthetic receptor co-expression. Competitive significance lies in optimizing lentiviral transduction efficiency and potentially enhancing CAR-T cell functionality through engineered vector surfaces and dual transgene expression, addressing manufacturing scalability and in vivo persistence for CD22+ malignancies (particularly B-cell lymphomas and leukemias).

patents.title: CELLULES MYÉLOÏDES DÉRIVÉES DE CELLULES SOUCHES INDUITES MODIFIÉES ET PROCÉDÉS DE DIFFÉRENCIATION ET MÉTHODES D'UTILISATION DE CELLES-CI
patents.abstract: Provided are compositions and methods for a cell population comprising macrophage cells comprising a synthetic cytokine receptor for a non-physiological ligand. The non- physiological ligand activates the synthetic cytokine receptor in the engineered stem cells to induce differentiation of the stem cells and, expansion and/or activation of resulting cytotoxic macrophage cells.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents engineered myeloid cells derived from modified induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) expressing synthetic cytokine receptors responsive to non-physiological ligands, enabling controlled differentiation and activation of cytotoxic macrophages. This synthetic receptor system provides a novel approach to engineer innate immune effector cells with programmable activation, offering competitive differentiation from natural CAR-T approaches by targeting macrophage-based cell therapies with enhanced control mechanisms.

patents.title: PARTICLES DISPLAYING ADHESION-MOLECULE FUSIONS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are particles comprising a fusion molecule comprising an adhesion molecule linked to a costimulatory molecule or an activation molecule, as well as vectors, such as lentiviral vectors, comprising the same, cells comprising the same, and methods of using the same. The particle may be a lentiviral particle that displays on the surface of the particle a fusion molecule comprising: a) a CD58 extracellular domain, or a functional fragment thereof, b) an antigen-binding fragment of an anti-CD3 antibody, and c) a CD80 or CD86 extracellular domain, or a functional fragment thereof, and a viral glycoprotein (G protein).
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes lentiviral particles displaying engineered surface fusion molecules that combine adhesion molecules (CD58), T cell activation signals (anti-CD3 scFv), and costimulatory domains (CD80/CD86) on a single polypeptide. This represents a novel approach to ex vivo T cell activation and engineering by providing multiple activation signals simultaneously during lentiviral transduction, potentially enhancing CAR-T cell manufacturing efficiency and reducing the need for external costimulatory ligands.

patents.title: ADMINISTRATION LENTIVIRALE DE RÉCEPTEURS ANTIGÉNIQUES CHIMÉRIQUES ANTI-CD20
patents.abstract: Provided herein are particles comprising polynucleotide constructs for generating cells expressing anti-CD20 chimeric antigen receptor, as well as vectors, such as lentiviral vectors, comprising same, cells comprising same, and methods of using same.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent covers lentiviral vector-based delivery of anti-CD20 CAR constructs to generate CAR-T cells, with novelty in the specific polynucleotide constructs, vector formulations, and resulting engineered cells. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as lentiviral integration offers stable, long-term transgene expression compared to non-integrating alternatives, particularly relevant for CD20+ B-cell malignancies where durable CAR persistence is clinically valuable.

patents.title: PARTICULES PRÉSENTANT DES FUSIONS DE MOLÉCULES D'ADHÉSION
patents.abstract: Provided herein are particles comprising a fusion molecule comprising an adhesion molecule linked to a costimulatory molecule or an activation molecule, as well as vectors, such as lentiviral vectors, comprising the same, cells comprising the same, and methods of using the same. The particle may be a lentiviral particle that displays on the surface of the particle a fusion molecule comprising: a) a CD58 extracellular domain, or a functional fragment thereof, b) an antigen-binding fragment of an anti-CD3 antibody, and c) a CD80 or CD86 extracellular domain, or a functional fragment thereof, and a viral glycoprotein (G protein).
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: Novel lentiviral particles displaying surface-engineered fusion molecules that combine adhesion molecules (CD58), T cell activation domains (anti-CD3), and costimulatory molecules (CD80/CD86) in a single polypeptide. This addresses a key limitation in CAR-T manufacturing by enabling simplified, single-vector production of functionally enhanced T cells without requiring separate costimulatory ligands, potentially improving transduction efficiency and T cell activation during ex vivo expansion.

patents.title: LENTIVIRAL PARTICLES DISPLAYING FUSION MOLECULES AND USES THEREOF
patents.abstract: Provided herein are particles comprising polynucleotide constructs for generating cells expressing anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor, as well as vectors, such as lentiviral vectors, comprising same, cells comprising same, and methods of using same.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses lentiviral particles displaying fusion molecules that deliver polynucleotide constructs encoding anti-CD19 CAR-T cells, with potential novelty in the vector design and fusion molecule display strategy for improved transduction efficiency. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as optimized lentiviral delivery systems can enhance transduction of primary T cells and potentially enable direct in vivo engineering approaches, reducing manufacturing complexity.

patents.title: CONSTRUCTION POLYNUCLÉOTIDIQUE ET VECTEURS VIRAUX ET PROCÉDÉS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are polycistronic constructs for coexpression of a synthetic cytokine receptor complex and a chimeric antigen receptor system, as well as vectors, such as viral vectors, comprising same, cells comprising same, and methods of using same.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses polycistronic constructs enabling simultaneous coexpression of synthetic cytokine receptor complexes with CAR systems in a single vector, addressing coordination of CAR-T signaling with engineered cytokine responsiveness. This approach offers competitive advantage by potentially improving CAR-T cell persistence, proliferation, and therapeutic efficacy through integrated receptor signaling without requiring separate transduction events.

patents.title: CELLULE LYMPHOIDE INNEE CYTOTOXIQUE ET SES UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: Provided are compositions and methods for a cell population comprising engineered cytotoxic innate lymphoid cells engineered for controlled expansion and/or activity, the engineered cytotoxic innate lymphoid cells comprising a synthetic cytokine receptor for a non-physiological ligand. The cytokine receptor may comprise a synthetic gamma chain polypeptide as a first dimerization domain, a first transmembrane domain, and an interleukin-2 receptor subunit gamma (IL-2RG) intracellular domain and a synthetic beta chain polypeptide as a second dimerization domain, a second transmembrane domain, and an intracellular domain selected from an interleukin-2 receptor subunit beta (IL-2RB) intracellular domain, an interleukin-7 receptor subunit beta (IL-7RB) intracellular domain, and/or an interleukin-21 receptor subunit beta (IL-21RB) intracellular domain. The non-physiological ligand activates the synthetic cytokine receptor in the cytotoxic innate lymphoid cells to induce expansion and/or activ
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents engineered cytotoxic innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) with synthetic cytokine receptors responsive to non-physiological ligands, enabling controlled expansion and activity independent of natural cytokine signaling. This orthogonal control mechanism offers competitive advantage for in vivo CAR-T and cell therapy by allowing precise temporal and spatial activation while minimizing off-target cytokine cross-reactivity.

patents.title: LENTIVIRUS PERMETTANT DE GENERER DES CELLULES EXPRIMANT UN RECEPTEUR ANTIGENIQUE CHIMERIQUE ANTI-CD19
patents.abstract:
[0001]    Provided are compositions and methods for transducing immune cells in vivo where a viral particle comprising a polynucleotide encoding a chimeric antigen receptor and a multipartite cell-surface receptor is administered to a subject.
[0002]    L'invention concerne des compositions et des procédés permettant la transduction de cellules immunitaires in vivo, une particule virale comprenant un polynucléotide codant pour un récepteur d'antigène chimère et un récepteur de surface cellulaire multipartite étant administrée à un sujet.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes lentiviral vectors encoding both a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) targeting CD19 and a multipartite cell-surface receptor for in vivo transduction of immune cells. The novelty lies in the dual-component approach combining CAR expression with a multipartite receptor in a single viral particle, enabling direct in vivo T cell engineering without ex vivo manipulation—a significant advancement toward non-manufacturing-intensive CAR-T therapies.

patents.title: SYSTEMES DE VECTEURS POUR L'ADMINISTRATION DE MULTIPLES POLYNUCLEOTIDES ET UTILISATIONS ASSOCIEES
patents.abstract:
[0001]    The present disclosure relates to a vector system comprising at least two polynucleotides, each polynucleotide may comprise a polynucleotide sequence encoding a polypeptide component of a macromolecular complex. Assembly of the macromolecular complex in a cell transduced with the polynucleotides may promote growth and/or survival of a cell.
[0002]    La présente divulgation concerne un système de vecteurs comprenant au moins deux polynucléotides, chaque polynucléotide pouvant comprendre une séquence polynucléotidique codant pour un composant polypeptidique d'un complexe macromoléculaire. L'assemblage du complexe macromoléculaire dans une cellule transduite avec les polynucléotides peut favoriser la croissance et/ou la survie d'une cellule.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a multi-polynucleotide vector system where each vector encodes separate polypeptide components that self-assemble into a functional macromolecular complex upon transduction, thereby enhancing cell growth and survival. This approach is significant for CAR-T as it enables delivery of multi-component therapeutic proteins (e.g., CAR receptors, co-stimulatory molecules, or signaling complexes) through separate, coordinated vectors, potentially improving safety, efficacy, and tunability compared to single-vector approaches.

patents.title: RÉCEPTEUR CIBLANT UN ADAPTATEUR COMMANDÉ PAR UNE PORTE
patents.abstract: Provided are compositions and methods for polynucleotides and vectors encoding novel chimeric receptor systems. The Gated Adaptor Targeting Receptor (GATR) system employs a dual adaptor system: a first, targeting adaptor and a second, gating adaptor. The targeting adaptor bispecifically binds both the target cell and the gating adaptor, while an engineered cell expressing the chimeric receptor binds the gating adaptor. This targets the engineered cells to an antigen recognized by the targeting adaptor thereby activating the engineered cells and leading to the desired physiological effect.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The GATR (Gated Adaptor Targeting Receptor) system introduces a dual-adaptor architecture where targeting and gating adaptors work in concert to redirect engineered cell specificity and activation, providing an alternative to single-chain CAR approaches with potential advantages in modularity, safety, and therapeutic flexibility. This represents a novel architectural innovation for CAR-T cell engineering with significant competitive implications for multi-antigen targeting and safety-gated cell therapies.

patents.title: ACTIVATEUR DE TRANSDUCTION BISPECIFIQUE
patents.abstract: Provided are compositions and methods for transducing immune cells in vivo where a multispecific antibody (e.g. a bispecific T-cell engager) is administered to render immune cells in the subject more transducible by a vector, such as a lentiviral vector.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a novel approach to enhance in vivo transduction of immune cells by co-administering a multispecific antibody (e.g., bispecific T-cell engager) alongside a viral vector to increase cellular transducibility. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as it addresses a major limitation in direct in vivo genetic modification—poor transduction efficiency—by using antibody-mediated immune cell activation to prime cells for improved vector uptake, potentially enabling off-the-shelf CAR-T generation without ex vivo manufacturing.

patents.title: VECTEUR RETROVIRAL POUR THERAPIE DU RECEPTEUR UNIVERSEL
patents.abstract:
[0001]    The present disclosure relates to retroviral vectors comprising polynucleotides encoding hapten-binding receptors and T cell activating receptors. The retroviral vectors may also comprise transduction enhancers. Also disclosed are adaptor molecules and their use in conjunction with the retroviral vectors and T cells transduced with the retroviral vectors.
[0002]    La présente invention concerne des vecteurs rétroviraux comprenant des polynucléotides codant des récepteurs de liaison d'haptène et des récepteurs d'activation de lymphocytes T. Les vecteurs rétroviraux peuvent également comprendre des amplificateurs de transduction. L'invention concerne également des molécules adaptatrices et leur utilisation en conjonction avec les vecteurs rétroviraux et les lymphocytes T transduits avec les vecteurs rétroviraux.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent discloses retroviral vectors encoding hapten-binding receptors coupled with T cell activating receptors, along with adaptor molecules that enable universal antigen targeting through a hapten-bridge strategy. The competitive significance lies in potentially circumventing traditional CAR-T single-antigen specificity limitations by enabling rapid retargeting to multiple antigens without re-engineering, a platform approach developed by Umoja Biopharma.

patents.title: MULTICISTRONISCHER VEKTOR ZUM OBERFLÄCHEN-ENGINEERING VON LENTIVIRALEN TEILCHEN
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; Umoja Biopharma, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a multicistronric lentiviral vector for surface engineering of lentiviral particles, enabling improved display of multiple proteins on viral surfaces for enhanced transduction efficiency. This is significant for CAR-T cell engineering as optimized lentiviral vectors are critical delivery platforms for introducing CAR constructs into primary T cells with improved manufacturing efficiency and transduction kinetics.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS DE PURIFICATION DE PARTICULES VIRALES ET FORMULATIONS ASSOCIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are pharmaceutical compositions comprising a virus, such as lentiviruses, including pseudotyped lentiviruses and uses thereof. Also provided for herein are methods of purifying and/or concentrating viral vectors and methods of producing sterile compositions, such as, sterile pharmaceutical compositions, wherein the methods can perform steps after passing the viral vector through a protein coated sterile filter. Also provided for herein are methods of using the pharmaceutical compositions.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims novel methods for purifying and concentrating lentiviral vectors (including pseudotyped variants) using protein-coated sterile filters, with subsequent processing steps to generate sterile pharmaceutical compositions. This is significant for CAR-T gene therapy as it addresses a critical manufacturing bottleneck—scalable, GMP-compatible lentiviral vector purification—which directly impacts production efficiency and cost of lentiviral-transduced CAR-T cell therapies.

patents.title: DOSAGE DU TITRAGE INFECTIEUX
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are methods of determining infectious titers of viral vectors, such as lentiviruses that are in a pharmaceutical composition including a sterile-filtered pharmaceutical composition.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes methods for determining infectious titers of viral vectors (specifically lentiviruses) in sterile-filtered pharmaceutical compositions. This is relevant to CAR-T manufacturing and gene therapy as accurate titer quantification is critical for quality control and dosing consistency of lentiviral vector-based CAR-T cell therapies, addressing a manufacturing challenge in ensuring product potency and safety.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS DE DÉTECTION D'ADN RÉSIDUEL DANS DES PRÉPARATIONS VIRALES
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are methods of purifying and/or concentrating viral vectors, methods of using the same to treat diseases, such as cancer or autoimmune diseases, and methods of producing sterile compositions, such as, sterile pharmaceutical compositions, wherein the methods can perform steps after passing the viral vector through a protein coated sterile filter.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.

patents.title: MOLÉCULES DE CIBLAGE D'HÉPATOCYTES ET LEURS PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are viral particles comprising a heterologous viral glycoprotein and a targeting moiety, wherein the targeting moiety comprises a polypeptide comprising a formula of T-S1, wherein T is a target binding domain that targets the viral particle to the liver and S1 is a stalk portion. The stalk portion may comprise a variant Fc domain. The stalk portion may comprise a flexible polypeptide domain. The targeting moiety comprising the formula T-S1 may be incorporated into a viral particle to assist with targeting such particles to a specific cell type. Also provided for herein are compositions comprising the same, and methods of using the same.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents engineered viral particles with modular targeting moieties (T-S1 formula) combining hepatocyte-specific binding domains with flexible stalk regions and variant Fc domains to enable liver-directed viral delivery. The innovation addresses cell-type specific targeting of viral vectors, which is relevant to in vivo CAR-T and gene therapy delivery where precise organ/tissue tropism is critical for reducing off-target effects and improving therapeutic efficacy.

patents.title: ACTIVATION OF T-CELLS WITH MUTANT G-CSFR
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are particles or compositions comprising one or more nucleic acid molecules encoding for a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) and/or a polypeptide comprising i) a ligand binding extracellular domain (ECD), ii) an immune cell activating intracellular domain (ICD); and iii) a transmembrane domain linking the ECD and ICD, polypeptides comprising the same, and nucleic acid molecules encoding for the same. Also provided for herein are compositions comprising the same, and methods of using the same. Also provided for herein are viral particles comprising the same.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes viral particles and compositions encoding CAR constructs with mutant G-CSFR signaling domains as an alternative intracellular activation mechanism. The novelty centers on using G-CSFR (granulocyte-colony stimulating factor receptor) mutations—typically associated with myeloid differentiation—to replace or supplement conventional CAR costimulatory domains, potentially offering a distinct T-cell activation profile with competitive advantage in terms of reduced exhaustion or altered persistence kinetics in in vivo CAR-T applications.

patents.title: PSEUDOTYPED VIRAL PARTICLES, COMPOSITIONS COMPRISING THE SAME, AND USES THEREOF
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are variant VSV-G polypeptides comprising one or more mutations as compared to wild type VSV-G polypeptides, compositions comprising the same, and methods of using the same.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses variant VSV-G polypeptides with specific mutations that enhance pseudotyped viral particle production and transduction efficiency. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery as VSV-G pseudotyping is a key technology for lentiviral and other viral vector systems used to engineer T cells ex vivo or enable in vivo transduction, potentially improving CAR-T manufacturing efficiency and reducing manufacturing costs.

patents.title: PARTICULES VIRALES PSEUDOTYPÉES COMPRENANT DES PROTÉINES RÉCEPTRICES CHIMÉRIQUES MODIFIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are viral particles comprising a heterologous viral glycoprotein and a targeting moiety, wherein the targeting moiety comprises a polypeptide comprising a formula of T-S1, wherein T is a target binding domain and S1 is a stalk portion. As provided for herein, the viral particles further comprises a nucleic acid molecule encoding for a heterologous molecule of interest. As provided for herein, the heterologous molecule of interest may be a tandem CAR. Also provided for herein are compositions comprising the same, and methods of using the same.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses pseudotyped viral particles engineered with modular targeting moieties (T-S1 architecture) capable of delivering heterologous payloads including tandem CAR constructs. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T lies in the potential for improved cellular targeting and delivery efficiency through rational design of the stalk domain (S1), enabling targeted transduction of CAR-T constructs without reliance on native viral tropism.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS D'ÉDITION DE GÈNES DE POLYPEPTIDES ET D'ACIDES NUCLÉIQUES, ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are viral particles comprising a heterologous viral structural protein, targeting moiety, and at least one nucleic acid molecule encoding for a gene editing system, compositions comprising the same, and methods of using the same.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes viral particles engineered with heterologous structural proteins and targeting moieties that deliver gene editing systems (likely CRISPR-based) as nucleic acid cargo. This represents a novel approach to pseudotyped viral vector technology for in vivo gene editing delivery, potentially offering improved cell tropism and safety profiles compared to conventional viral vectors, with significant implications for targeted T cell engineering and CAR-T manufacturing via ex vivo or in vivo gene correction.

patents.title: PURIFICATION DE VIRUS ET DE PARTICULES DE TYPE VIRAL
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are pseudotyped viral constructs comprising affinity binding polypeptides fused with glycoproteins, targeting moieties, or a combination thereof. Also provided for herein are methods of purifying and using the viral constructs provided for herein.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes pseudotyped viral constructs with affinity binding polypeptides fused to glycoproteins and/or targeting moieties, along with purification methods. For in vivo CAR-T applications, this is significant as pseudotyped viral vectors with enhanced targeting capabilities could improve selective transduction of T cells and reduce off-target effects, while affinity-based purification methods could increase manufacturing efficiency and product purity for viral gene delivery vehicles.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS PHARMACEUTIQUES COMPRENANT DES PARTICULES VIRALES ET LEURS MÉTHODES D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are pharmaceutical compositions comprising a virus, such as lentiviruses, including pseudotyped lentiviruses and uses thereof. Also provided for herein are methods of using the pharmaceutical compositions.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent covers pharmaceutical compositions based on lentiviruses (including pseudotyped variants) and their therapeutic uses. For in vivo CAR-T applications, pseudotyped lentiviruses represent a potentially significant delivery vector for CAR transgenes, offering broader tropism and reduced immunogenicity compared to wild-type lentiviruses, though the abstract provides limited specificity on CAR-T targeting or in vivo efficacy innovations.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS DE FILTRATION OU DE PURIFICATION DE PARTICULES VIRALES
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are methods of purifying and/or concentrating viral vectors, methods of using the same to treat diseases, such as cancer or autoimmune diseases, and methods of producing sterile compositions, such as, sterile pharmaceutical compositions, wherein the methods can perform steps after passing the viral vector through a protein coated sterile filter.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes methods for purifying and concentrating viral vectors using protein-coated sterile filters, with application to treating cancer and autoimmune diseases. The competitive significance lies in improving viral vector manufacturing efficiency and sterility assurance, which is critical for clinical-grade CAR-T and gene therapy production where vector purity and titer directly impact therapeutic efficacy and safety.

patents.title: PARTICULES VIRALES MODIFIÉES ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are compositions and methods that can be used to transduce cells and deliver genetic information that can then be expressed in the transduced cell. Also provided herein are methods of treating a disease in a subject using the compositions and methods provided.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses modified viral particles designed for cell transduction and delivery of genetic information with subsequent expression in target cells, applicable to disease treatment. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T involves potential use of these modified viral vectors as delivery vehicles for CAR constructs, though the abstract lacks specificity regarding CAR-T engineering, integration mechanisms, or T cell-specific modifications that would differentiate this from broader gene delivery platforms.

patents.title: PSEUDOTYPED VIRAL PARTICLES, COMPOSITIONS COMPRISNG THE SAME, AND USES THEREOF
patents.abstract: Provided for herein are mutant VSV-G polypeptides, compositions comprising the same, and methods of using the same. Also provided for herein are polypeptides and compositions that bind to CD7 and uses thereof. Also provided for herein are polypeptides and compositions that bind to CD8 and uses thereof.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses mutant VSV-G polypeptides for pseudotyping viral particles, along with CD7- and CD8-binding polypeptides for targeted transduction. This is significant for CAR-T manufacturing as improved VSV-G variants and targeted envelope proteins could enhance lentiviral or other viral vector transduction efficiency and selectivity in T cell engineering, potentially reducing off-target effects and improving manufacturing yield.

patents.title: VECTEURS PSEUDOTYPES D'EBOLA ET LEURS METHODES D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present embodiments provide methods and compositions for pseudotyping viral vectors. Also provided are methods and compositions for creating targeting moiety fused viral glycoproteins. Also provided herein are methods of treating a disease in a subject in need thereof using the compositions provided for herein. Also provided are methods of delivering a molecule of interest to a target cell using the compositions provided for herein.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent covers pseudotyped Ebola viral vectors with targeting moieties fused to viral glycoproteins, enabling selective delivery of molecules of interest to target cells. This technology is relevant to gene therapy delivery systems, particularly for directing therapeutic payloads to specific cell populations, which could enhance specificity and reduce off-target effects in cell and gene therapy applications.

patents.title: MOLÉCULES D'ACIDES NUCLÉIQUES ET LEURS PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Nucleic acid molecules are provided herein that can be used, for example, to produce viruses that can be used, for example to treat cancer or infections, or to induce an immune response in a subject, or to deliver or express a target molecule in or from a cell.
patents.assignee: INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; INTERIUS BIOTHERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses nucleic acid molecules designed for viral vector production to treat cancer, infections, or induce immune responses through target molecule delivery/expression in cells. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is moderate—while viral vector-based delivery is relevant to T cell engineering, the abstract does not specifically claim CAR-T constructs, engineered T cells, or CAR-specific innovations, limiting direct application to the CAR-T space.

patents.title: LIPIDES CATIONIQUES IONISABLES ET NANOPARTICULES LIPIDIQUES
patents.abstract: Ionizable cationic lipids, methods for synthesizing the same, intermediates useful in synthesis of the ionizable cationic lipids, and methods of synthesizing the intermediates are disclosed. The ionizable cationic lipids are useful as a component of lipid nanoparticles (LNP), which in turn can be used for delivering nucleic acids into cells in vivo or ex vivo. LNP compositions are also disclosed, including LNP comprising a functionalized lipid to enable conjugation of a binding moiety, and targeted LNP (tLNP), that is an LNP in which a binding moiety has been conjugated to the functionalized lipid and can serve as a targeting moiety to direct the tLNP to a desired tissue or cell type.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses ionizable cationic lipids and their synthetic methods, with application to lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for in vivo nucleic acid delivery. Novel aspects include functionalized lipids enabling targeted LNP (tLNP) conjugation with binding moieties for cell-type specific delivery, which is highly relevant for directing CAR-T engineering payloads to T cells or enabling ex vivo T cell transduction with improved efficiency and reduced off-target effects.

patents.title: LIPIDES CATIONIQUES IONISABLES CONTRAINTS ET NANOPARTICULES LIPIDIQUES
patents.abstract: Ionizable cationic lipids, methods for synthesizing the same, intermediates useful in synthesis of the ionizable cationic lipids, and methods of synthesizing the intermediates are disclosed. The ionizable cationic lipids are useful as a component of lipid nanoparticles (LNP), which in turn can be used for delivering nucleic acids into cells in vivo or ex vivo. LNP compositions are also disclosed, including LNPs comprising a functionalized lipid to enable conjugation of a binding moiety, and targeted LNPs (tLNPs), that is, LNPs in which a binding moiety has been conjugated to the functionalized lipid and can serve as a targeting moiety to direct the tLNPs to a desired tissue or cell type.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel ionizable cationic lipids with constrained structures and their incorporation into lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) with enhanced targeting capabilities through functionalized lipids and conjugated binding moieties. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery as targeted LNPs enable cell-type specific delivery of nucleic acids encoding CAR constructs, potentially improving therapeutic efficacy and reducing off-target effects compared to non-targeted delivery systems.

patents.title: AMPLIFICATION D'INGÉNIERIE IMMUNITAIRE
patents.abstract: This disclosure provides methods of increasing in vivo transfection efficiency and pharmacologic activity of T cells, by administering multiple small doses within a compact time period of T cell-targeted lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA encoding an antigen receptor that recognizes an antigen of a cell against which immune activity is to be directed. Also provided are methods of depleting B cells, and methods of treating B cell-mediated diseases and disorders by depleting B cells and achieving immunological reset, entailing administration of immune cell-targeted lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA encoding an antigen receptor recognizing a B cell marker as multiple small doses within a compact time period. The antigen receptor can be a T cell receptor or a chimeric antigen receptor.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims novelty in the dosing regimen of mRNA-LNP delivering CAR/TCR constructs to T cells via multiple small doses within compact timeframes to enhance in vivo transfection efficiency and pharmacologic activity. Additionally, the invention extends to B cell depletion and immunological reset through similar LNP-mRNA delivery targeting B cell markers, representing a novel application of fractional dosing strategy in cell-targeted gene therapy.

patents.title: HUMANIZED ANTI-CD8 ANTIBODIES AND USES THEREOF
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides humanized antibodies and antigen binding domains thereof that bind CD8α and other antibody formats comprising these antigen binding domains, their use as a targeting moiety on lipid nanoparticles (tLNP) to deliver a therapeutic payload (such as a nucleic acid molecule) or other types of payloads. The present disclosure further relates to pharmaceutical compositions comprising the humanized anti-CD8α antibodies and CD8-targeted tLNP encapsulating a payload.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; Capstan Therapeutics, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents humanized anti-CD8α antibodies engineered as targeting moieties on targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNP) for selective CD8+ T cell delivery of therapeutic payloads (nucleic acids and other cargo). This is significant for in vivo CAR-T applications as it enables non-viral, antibody-directed delivery of genetic material directly to CD8+ T cells, potentially allowing ex vivo-free CAR-T manufacturing or in vivo reprogramming of endogenous T cells.

patents.title: RNA for In vivo Transfection with Increased Expression
patents.abstract: This disclosure provides improved RNA molecules, including mRNA molecules that can be produced by in vitro transcription and are suitable for in vivo transfection using an appropriate delivery vehicle, such as a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) or targeted lipid nanoparticle (tLNP). The improved RNA include particular combinations of 5′ untranslated region (UTR) and 3′ UTR, particular 3′ UTRs, or particular open reading frame sequences. Also provided herein are compositions of the LNP, or tLNP with an antibody as a targeting moiety, such as anti-CD8 antibodies that are used as targeting moiety.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; Capstan Therapeutics Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses optimized mRNA molecules with specific 5′ UTR, 3′ UTR, and open reading frame combinations designed for enhanced in vivo expression via LNP/tLNP delivery, including targeted formulations with antibodies (e.g., anti-CD8) as targeting moieties. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as it addresses improved mRNA delivery efficiency and cell-type targeting, potentially enabling more effective CAR-T cell engineering with reduced off-target effects and enhanced transduction of desired T cell populations.

patents.title: LIPIDES CATIONIQUES IONISABLES CONTRAINTS ET NANOPARTICULES LIPIDIQUES
patents.abstract: Ionizable cationic lipids, methods for synthesizing the same, intermediates useful in synthesis of the ionizable cationic lipids and methods of synthesizing the intermediates are disclosed. The ionizable cationic lipids are useful as a component of lipid nanoparticles (LNP), which in turn can be used for the delivery of nucleic acids into cells in vivo or ex vivo. LNP compositions are also disclosed, including LNP comprising a functionalized lipid to enable conjugation of a binding moiety, and targeted LNP (tLNP), that is an LNP in which a binding moiety has been conjugated to the functionalized lipid and can serve as a targeting moiety to direct the tLNP to a desired tissue or cell type.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel ionizable cationic lipids with constrained structures and their synthetic intermediates, optimized for lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations with improved in vivo nucleic acid delivery properties. The inclusion of functionalized lipids enabling targeted LNP (tLNP) with cell-type or tissue-specific binding moieties represents a significant advancement for directing therapeutic nucleic acids to desired cellular targets, particularly relevant for directing gene therapy and CAR-T engineering payloads to immune cells or tumor microenvironments.

patents.title: LIPIDES CATIONIQUES IONISABLES À ESPACEMENT CONSERVÉ ET NANOPARTICULES LIPIDIQUES
patents.abstract: Ionizable cationic lipids, methods for synthesizing the same, intermediates useful in synthesis of the ionizable cationic lipids, and methods of synthesizing the intermediates are disclosed. The ionizable cationic lipids are useful as a component of lipid nanoparticles (LNP), which in turn can be used for delivering nucleic acids into cells in vivo or ex vivo. LNP compositions are also disclosed, including LNP comprising a functionalized lipid to enable conjugation of a binding moiety, and targeted LNP (tLNP), that is a LNP in which a binding moiety has been conjugated to the functionalized lipid and can serve as a targeting moiety to direct the tLNP to a desired tissue or cell type.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses ionizable cationic lipids with conserved spacing architecture and their incorporation into lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for in vivo/ex vivo nucleic acid delivery, with particular innovation in targeted LNPs (tLNPs) bearing conjugated binding moieties for cell-type-specific delivery. This is significant for CAR-T applications as it enables precise in vivo delivery of CAR-encoding nucleic acids to lymphoid tissues, potentially improving transduction efficiency and reducing off-target effects compared to conventional LNP formulations.

patents.title: INGÉNIERIE EXTRACORPORELLE ET EX VIVO DE POPULATIONS DE CELLULES SÉLECTIONNÉES ISSUES DE SANG PÉRIPHÉRIQUE
patents.abstract: Disclosed are methods for producing a population of autologous engineered cells to be reinfused into a subject comprising extracorporeally transfecting an internal payload into a population of target cells from a sample obtained from the subject by incubating the population of cells with a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) and/or targeting lipid nanoparticle (tLNP) in an incubation component of an extracorporeal system for no more than 6 hours.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; LI XIANGHONG [US]; AGHAJANIAN HAIG [US]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses an ex vivo cell engineering approach using lipid nanoparticles (LNPs/tLNPs) to transfect autologous cells from peripheral blood within an extracorporeal system, with a key innovation being the rapid incubation window of ≤6 hours. This offers competitive significance for CAR-T manufacturing by potentially enabling faster, closed-system cell engineering that reduces ex vivo culture time while maintaining cell viability and therapeutic potential.

patents.title: LIPID NANOPARTICLE FORMULATIONS AND COMPOSITIONS
patents.abstract: [0000]    Disclosed are compositions of lipid nanoparticles (LNP) comprising an ionizable cationic lipid, a phospholipid, a sterol, and a PEG-lipid (non-functionalized and optionally functionalized). The functionalized PEG-lipid can be conjugated with a binding moiety to create a targeted LNP (tLNP). The disclosed tLNP preferentially deliver a nucleic acid molecule or other negatively charged payload to cells expressing a cell surface antigen recognized by the binding moiety of the tLNP, and are better tolerated, as compared to LNPs and tLNPs comprising ionizable cationic lipids found in marketed pharmaceuticals comprising LNPs.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses targeted lipid nanoparticle (tLNP) formulations with functionalized PEG-lipids conjugated to binding moieties for cell-surface antigen-directed delivery, claiming improved tolerability compared to marketed LNP formulations. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as it addresses a key delivery bottleneck—efficient and safe systemic delivery of nucleic acids (mRNA, DNA) encoding CAR-T constructs to target tissues while reducing off-target toxicity.

patents.title: CONDITIONNEMENT POUR L'INGÉNIERIE DE CELLULES IMMUNITAIRES IN VIVO
patents.abstract: Disclosed are methods of conditioning subjects who receive, are receiving, or have received an agent for in vivo reprogramming of immune cells in order to improve the efficiency of the in vivo reprogramming and/or the overall therapeutic effect of the treatment. Also disclosed are nanoparticle compositions for providing the conditioning agent(s). The conditioning agent can be provided prior to, concurrently with, or after administration of the in vivo reprogramming agent depending on the conditioning agent. The conditioning regimens are useful in combination with in vivo reprogramming of immune cells to treat hematologic cancers and solid tumor, fibrotic disorders, and B cell or T cell mediated autoimmunity, chronic infection. Some conditioning regimens are also useful in combination with other cancer treatments.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; UNIV PENNSYLVANIA [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses conditioning regimens administered before, during, or after in vivo immune cell reprogramming to enhance therapeutic efficacy, along with nanoparticle delivery compositions for conditioning agents. The competitive significance lies in optimizing in vivo T cell engineering approaches (as alternative to ex vivo CAR-T) by strategically timing immunomodulatory conditioning to improve cell reprogramming efficiency and clinical outcomes across hematologic and solid tumors.

patents.title: LIPIDES PEG ET NANOPARTICULES LIPIDIQUES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are polyethylene glycol (PEG)-lipids, functionalized PEG-lipids, and functionalized PEG-lipids that are conjugated to a binding moiety which can comprise an antibody antigen binding domain. Also disclosed are methods for synthesizing and functionalizing the PEG-lipids. The PEG-lipids are useful components lipid nanoparticles (LNP) used for the delivery of nucleic acids into living cells, in vivo or ex vivo. LNP comprising functionalized PEG-lipids that are conjugated to a binding moiety are useful as targeted LNP for delivering nucleic acids into cells or tissues expressing the ligand of the binding moiety.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel PEG-lipid conjugates functionalized with antibody antigen binding domains for targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery. The key innovation is the integration of targeting moieties into LNP formulations, enabling cell- or tissue-specific nucleic acid delivery—particularly significant for in vivo CAR-T applications where targeted delivery of therapeutic nucleic acids (e.g., CAR constructs) to immune cells or tumor microenvironments could improve efficacy and reduce off-target effects.

patents.title: IONIZABLE CATIONIC LIPIDS AND LIPID NANOPARTICLES
patents.abstract: [0000]    Ionizable cationic lipids, methods for synthesizing them, as well as intermediates useful in synthesis of these lipids and methods of synthesizing the intermediates are disclosed. The ionizable cationic lipids are useful as a component of lipid nanoparticles (LNP), which in turn can be used for the delivery of nucleic acids into cells in vivo or ex vivo. LNP compositions are also disclosed, including LNP comprising a functionalized lipid to enable conjugation of a binding moiety, and targeted LNP (tLNP), that is a LNP in which a binding moiety has been conjugated to the functionalized lipid and can serve as a targeting moiety to direct the tLNP to a desired tissue or cell type.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses ionizable cationic lipids and lipid nanoparticle formulations with functionalized lipids enabling targeted delivery via conjugated binding moieties. For in vivo CAR-T applications, targeted LNPs represent significant competitive advantage by enabling direct T cell targeting and potentially improving transfection efficiency and reducing off-target effects compared to non-targeted delivery systems.

patents.title: CONDITIONNEMENT POUR L'INGÉNIERIE DE CELLULES IMMUNITAIRES IN VIVO
patents.abstract: Disclosed are methods of conditioning subjects who receive, are receiving, or have received an agent for in vivo reprogramming of immune cells in order to improve the efficiency of the in vivo reprogramming and/or the overall therapeutic effect of the treatment. Also disclosed are nanoparticle compositions for providing the conditioning agent(s). The conditioning agent can be provided prior to, concurrently with, or after administration of the in vivo reprogramming agent depending on the conditioning agent. The conditioning regimens are useful in combination with in vivo reprogramming of immune cells to treat hematologic cancers and solid tumor, fibrotic disorders, and B cell or T cell mediated autoimmunity, chronic infection.
