Some conditioning regimens are also useful in combination with other cancer treatments.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses conditioning regimens (including nanoparticle compositions) administered before, during, or after in vivo immune cell reprogramming to enhance reprogramming efficiency and therapeutic efficacy. This represents a novel approach to optimizing in vivo CAR-T and related cell engineering by combining preparatory conditioning with non-viral in vivo reprogramming agents, potentially expanding applicability across hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, fibrotic disorders, and autoimmune conditions.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS DE PRODUCTION D'ARN CIRCULAIRE
patents.abstract: The present invention provides nucleic acids and methods for making circular RNAs (circRNAs), compositions comprising circular RNAs, and methods of use thereof. The present invention uses optimized self-splicing T4 bacteriophage td gene (T4td) intron sequences to produce circular RNAs. The optimized T4td intron sequences described herein mediate efficient circularization of a linear RNA sequence.
patents.assignee: ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses optimized T4 bacteriophage td gene intron sequences that enable efficient circularization of linear RNA into circular RNA (circRNA). This is significant for in vivo CAR-T applications as circRNAs offer improved stability, reduced immunogenicity, and prolonged expression compared to linear mRNA, potentially enabling more durable CAR-T cell engineering through non-viral RNA delivery platforms.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS DE CIRCULARISATION D'ARN
patents.abstract: The present invention provides nucleic acids and methods for making circular RNAs (circRNAs), and circular RNAs, compositions and methods of use thereof. The present invention uses selected self-splicing intron sequences (e.g., intronic sequences derived from self-splicing Group I or Group II introns) to produce circular RNAs. These self-splicing intron sequences described herein mediate efficient circularization of a linear RNA sequence.
patents.assignee: ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention provides a novel platform for efficient circularization of RNA using self-splicing intron sequences (Group I/II introns), enabling production of circular RNAs with potential advantages in stability and immunogenicity. This circRNA technology is relevant to in vivo CAR-T delivery as circRNAs offer improved mRNA stability, reduced innate immune activation, and enhanced protein translation compared to linear mRNA, making them attractive vehicles for delivering CAR constructs and other therapeutic transgenes.

patents.title: RIBONUCLÉASE R THERMOSTABLE POUR PURIFICATION D'ARN CIRCULAIRE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides, among other things, methods for removing linear ribonucleic acid molecules from a sample by contacting the sample with ribonuclease R (RNase R) from a thermophilic organism, for example, Geobacillus stearothermophilus, Fervidobacterium pennivorans or Thermus thermophilus expressed and purified in E.coli. Also provided herein are methods of producing circular RNA and removing uncircularized linear RNA molecules, linear RNA byproducts, or linear RNA side products using an RNase R expressed or purified from a thermophilic organism. The present disclosure also provides methods of purifying RNase R from a thermophilic organism in E. coll, wherein the method comprises heat treatment at high temperatures, and compositions and kits comprising the same.
patents.assignee: ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses thermostable RNase R from thermophilic organisms (e.g., Geobacillus stearothermophilus) for selective removal of linear RNA while preserving circular RNA, along with purification methods in E. coli via heat treatment. This is significant for circular RNA (circRNA) therapeutics as it enables cost-effective, scalable production and purification of circRNA for vaccine and gene therapy applications, addressing a key manufacturing bottleneck in circRNA-based immunotherapies.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS AMÉLIORÉS DE FABRICATION DE L'ARN PAR LIGATURE À PONT ET COMPOSITIONS ASSOCIÉES
patents.abstract: The present invention provides, among other things, a method of making circular RNA by annealing a DNA splint having regions of homology to the 5' and 3' ends of linear RNA with an RNA ligase and subsequently removing the DNA splint. Also provided is a method of joining two linear RNA molecules by ligation using a DNA splint having regions of homology to the 3' end of a first linear RNA and the 5' end of a second linear RNA with a RNA ligase, and subsequently removing the DNA splints. The present invention provides a method of making circular RNA by joining two linear RNA molecules with an RNA ligase and two DNA splints, each comprising regions of homology to the 5' end.
patents.assignee: ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent describes improved methods for manufacturing circular RNA and joining linear RNA molecules using DNA splint-mediated ligation with RNA ligase, followed by splint removal. The circular RNA production approach is relevant to gene therapy as circular RNA constructs offer improved stability and reduced immunogenicity compared to linear RNA, making them potentially valuable for CAR-T and other T cell engineering applications requiring robust mRNA delivery.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS SE RAPPORTANT À L'EXPRESSION DE PROTÉINE DANS DE L'ARNM SYNTHÉTIQUE ADMINISTRÉ PAR INJECTION
patents.abstract: The present disclosure relates to use of an oligosaccharide or a glucosidase to enhance protein expression from synthetic RNA delivered by injection. In particular, the present disclosure relates to use of chitosan or hyaluronidase to transfect skeletal muscle or skin cells. Other cells that can be effectively transfected with synthetic RNA/chitosan mixtures include bone marrow cells, peritoneal cavity cells, and retro-orbital sinus cells.
patents.assignee: ELIXIRGEN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ELIXIRGEN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses enhancement of protein expression from synthetic mRNA via co-delivery with oligosaccharides (chitosan) or glucosidases (hyaluronidase), enabling efficient transfection of multiple cell types including skeletal muscle and bone marrow cells. This is relevant to in vivo gene therapy as it provides a non-viral delivery approach that could facilitate mRNA-based therapeutic protein expression, though the direct application to CAR-T cell engineering is not explicitly addressed.

patents.title: VIRALER VEKTOR UND PRODUKTIONSZELLE
patents.abstract: [0001]    There is provided a viral vector having a lipid bilayer envelope comprising an antibody binding domain displayed on the exterior of the envelope that is cell-type specific; a viral envelope protein displayed on the exterior of the envelope that is able to facilitate infection of the same cell type; and a nucleic acid molecule comprising a promoter expressible in the same cell type. Further provided are methods of making the viral vector and methods of using the viral vector to modify cells and treat diseases / conditions.
patents.assignee: ESOBIOTEC [BE]; ESOBIOTEC SA [BE]; EsoBiotec
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a viral vector with a lipid bilayer envelope displaying cell-type-specific antibody binding domains and matching envelope proteins for targeted infection of specific cell types, combined with cell-type-specific promoters for regulated transgene expression. This targeting approach could enhance specificity and safety in T cell engineering applications by restricting viral transduction and transgene expression to target cell populations.

patents.title: COMPOSICIONES PARA MODIFICAR CÉLULAS
patents.abstract: La presente divulgación proporciona composiciones y métodos que comprenden partículas recombinantes adecuadas para suministrar de manera específica uno o más receptores diseñados a células efectoras inmunitarias in vivo.  Reivindicación 1: Una partícula recombinante que comprende: (a) una superficie que comprende (i) una o más glicoproteínas de envoltura viral mutadas que retienen la actividad fusogénica y que carecen de actividad de unión de receptor afín y (ii) un polipéptido de tropismo no viral unido a la membrana que comprende un anticuerpo o su fragmento de unión a antígeno que se une a un antígeno expresado sobre una célula efectora inmunitaria, un polipéptido espaciador, un dominio transmembrana, y opcionalmente, un dominio intracelular que comprende no más de 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 o 10 aminoácidos; y (b) una carga útil terapéutica. Reivindicación 81: Una célula transducida con la partícula de cualquiera de las reivindicaciones 1 a 80. Reivindicación 84: Una composición que
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents recombinant particles with engineered viral envelope glycoproteins that retain fusogenic activity while lacking native receptor-binding capacity, coupled with non-viral tropism polypeptides (antibody-based) to redirect delivery specifically to immune effector cells in vivo. This represents a novel dual-targeting approach for CAR-T and T cell engineering, potentially improving specificity and reducing off-target transduction compared to conventional viral vectors.

patents.title: POLYPEPTIDES DE LIAISON À UN ANTIGÈNE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions comprising antigen binding polypeptides. More particularly, the disclosure relates to polypeptides comprising antibodies or antigen binding fragments thereof, nucleic acids encoding the polypeptides, and vectors for expressing the same.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses antigen-binding polypeptides including antibodies or antigen-binding fragments, along with nucleic acids and expression vectors for their production. While the abstract provides limited detail, this is potentially relevant to CAR-T engineering if these polypeptides are intended as single-chain variable fragments (scFvs) or similar binding domains for CAR constructs, which would represent a composition enabling improved targeting specificity in adoptive cell therapy.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS POUR LE TRAITEMENT DU CANCER
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods comprising recombinant particles suitable for specifically delivering one or more chimeric antigen receptors to immune effector cells in vivo.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses recombinant particles engineered for in vivo delivery of chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) directly to immune effector cells, representing a novel delivery platform that circumvents ex vivo cell manipulation. This approach addresses a key limitation in current CAR-T therapeutics by enabling systemic administration and targeted CAR expression, potentially reducing manufacturing costs and improving scalability compared to conventional ex vivo transduction methods.

patents.title: ANTIGEN BINDING POLYPEPTIDES
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present disclosure provides compositions comprising antigen binding polypeptides. More particularly, the disclosure relates to polypeptides comprising antibodies or antigen binding fragments thereof, nucleic acids encoding the polypeptides, and vectors for expressing the same.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; Kelonia Therapeutics, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses antigen binding polypeptides (antibodies or fragments), their encoding nucleic acids, and expression vectors. While foundational to therapeutic applications, the abstract lacks specificity regarding novel binding mechanisms, targeting strategies, or delivery innovations that would differentiate this from established antibody technologies relevant to CAR-T engineering.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS FOR TREATING CANCER
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods comprising recombinant particles suitable for specifically delivering one or more chimeric antigen receptors to immune effector cells in vivo.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; Kelonia Therapeutics, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes recombinant particles engineered for in vivo delivery of chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) directly to immune effector cells, offering a potential alternative to ex vivo manufacturing approaches. This is significant for CAR-T because it targets the key manufacturing bottleneck by enabling intracellular CAR expression without prior cell isolation and ex vivo transduction, potentially reducing cost and time-to-treatment.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS DE MODIFICATION CELLULAIRE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods comprising recombinant particles suitable for specifically delivering one or more engineered receptors to immune effector cells in vivo.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses recombinant particles designed for in vivo delivery of engineered receptors to immune effector cells, enabling direct cellular modification without ex vivo manipulation. This approach is significant for CAR-T therapy as it potentially eliminates the need for patient cell extraction, ex vivo engineering, and re-infusion, reducing manufacturing costs and time-to-treatment while improving accessibility.

patents.title: MODÈLES D'ANIMAUX LENTIVIRAUX IN VIVO
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods for decreasing B cells in non-human primates using recombinant lentiviral vectors.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes methods for in vivo B cell depletion in non-human primates using recombinant lentiviral vectors. This is relevant to CAR-T therapy development as B cell targeting and understanding CAR-T efficacy in primate models with lentiviral delivery represents a potential advance in preclinical validation approaches for cellular immunotherapy.

patents.title: RÉTROVIRUS RECOMBINANTS MODIFIÉS
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides recombinant retroviruses engineered to transduce immune effector cells in vivo.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered recombinant retroviruses designed for in vivo transduction of immune effector cells, representing a modified viral vector platform for direct cellular engineering without ex vivo manipulation. This addresses a key technical challenge in cell therapy by enabling in situ CAR-T generation or immune cell modification, potentially reducing manufacturing complexity and improving clinical scalability compared to traditional ex vivo approaches.

patents.title: DARIC IN VIVO
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods effective for transducing cells in vivo with a recombinant retrovirus comprising a polynucleotide encoding a dimerizing agent regulated immunoreceptor complex (DARIC).
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses in vivo transduction of cells using recombinant retroviruses encoding DARIC (dimerizing agent regulated immunoreceptor complex), a novel immunoreceptor architecture that enables regulated T cell activation through synthetic dimerization. This approach offers competitive advantages for in vivo CAR-T by enabling activity control without genetic modification of the target antigen receptor, potentially reducing off-target effects and providing superior safety/efficacy profiles compared to conventional CAR-T designs.

patents.title: THÉRAPIE GÉNIQUE À DOUBLE CIBLAGE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods effective for transducing cells in vivo with a recombinant retrovirus comprising a polynucleotide encoding a chimeric antigen receptor and a chimeric costimulatory receptor.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a dual-targeting approach using recombinant retroviruses to co-deliver both a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) and a chimeric costimulatory receptor in a single vector for in vivo cell transduction. This represents a significant advancement for CAR-T therapy by combining antigen recognition with integrated costimulatory signaling in one construct, potentially improving therapeutic efficacy and reducing the need for separate transduction steps or ex vivo cell engineering.

patents.title: RÉTROVIRUS RECOMBINANT, COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods for transducing immune effector cells in vivo with a recombinant retrovirus comprising a polynucleotide encoding a chimeric antigen receptor and a multipartite cell surface receptor.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a recombinant retrovirus vector designed for in vivo transduction of immune effector cells with CAR constructs incorporating a multipartite cell surface receptor architecture. The competitive significance lies in enabling direct in vivo CAR-T cell engineering via retroviral delivery, potentially eliminating the need for ex vivo cell extraction and manufacturing, which could substantially reduce cost and improve accessibility of CAR-T therapies.

patents.title: RÉTROVIRUS RECOMBINANTS, COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides recombinant retroviruses, retroviral vectors, packaging cell lines, and in vivo methods of use for expansion of immune effector cell populations for treatment of a disease, disorder, or condition.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses recombinant retroviruses and retroviral vectors designed for in vivo expansion of immune effector cell populations, representing a delivery platform for therapeutic cell therapy. The competitive significance lies in enabling direct in vivo expansion of engineered T cells without ex vivo manufacturing bottlenecks, potentially addressing scalability and manufacturing costs that constrain current CAR-T therapeutics.

patents.title: RÉTROVIRUS RECOMBINANT, COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides recombinant retrovirus or retroviral particles comprising fusogens and tropism polypeptides and polynucleotides encoding hapten-binding receptors and optionally transduction enhancers and one or more T cell activating proteins. The present disclosure further provides adaptor molecules and methods of using the same with the recombinant retrovirus or retroviral particles and T cells transduced with the recombinant retrovirus or retroviral particles.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes recombinant retroviral vectors engineered with dual functional components: hapten-binding receptors for targeted recognition and T cell activating proteins for enhanced T cell engagement. This represents a novel approach to ex vivo T cell engineering that combines receptor specificity with integrated co-stimulatory signaling, potentially reducing the need for external activation and improving CAR-T manufacturing efficiency and potency.

patents.title: RÉTROVIRUS RECOMBINANTS, COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides a recombinant retrovirus comprising retroviral vectors encoding components of a macromolecular complex, which when expressed in a cell and in the presence of a ligand may promote growth and/or survival of the cell.
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KELONIA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes recombinant retroviruses encoding components of macromolecular complexes that promote cell growth/survival in the presence of ligands. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is moderate—retroviral vectors remain relevant for T cell transduction, but the ligand-dependent survival mechanism may offer an engineered safety switch or proliferation control system, though the abstract lacks specificity on CAR or TCR targeting sequences.

patents.title: AUF LYMPHOZYTEN ZIELGERICHTETE LENTIVIRALE VEKTOREN
patents.assignee: KELONIA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; Kelonia Therapeutics, Inc.

patents.title: PROTÉINE CHIMÉRIQUE ET CELLULE IMMUNITAIRE MODIFIÉE, AINSI QUE LEUR PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉPARATION ET LEUR UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided are a chimeric protein and an engineered immune cell. The chimeric protein contains an Fc-binding domain of an Fcγ receptor, can bind to the Fc fragment of an IgG antibody, and does not contain a protease-cleavable site in the Fc-binding domain of the Fcγ receptor, thereby effectively promoting continuous killing of a target cell when the engineered immune cell expressing the chimeric protein is used in combination with IgG.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a chimeric protein featuring an Fc-binding domain of Fcγ receptor lacking protease-cleavable sites, enabling sustained antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) when expressed on engineered immune cells combined with IgG antibodies. This design addresses proteolytic degradation of Fc-binding interfaces, offering improved persistence and efficacy in antibody-redirected cell therapy platforms.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉPARATION DE CELLULES CAR-T ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Disclosed are a method of preparing CAR-T cells, and a composition used in said method. The method comprises: S1, administering, as a pretreatment, lymphocyte depletion therapy to a subject having cancer; and S2, administering to the subject (a) a cell population comprising T cells collected from a haploidentical donor thereof and (b) a viral vector. The method allows for effective preparation of CAR-T cells in a subject.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses an in vivo CAR-T cell preparation method combining lymphodepleting pretreatment with haploidentical donor T cells and viral vector administration directly to the subject, rather than ex vivo manufacturing. This approach offers potential advantages in accessibility and speed by shifting CAR-T generation from centralized manufacturing to patient bedside, with competitive significance for allogeneic CAR-T cell therapy platforms.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉPARATION D'UN LYMPHOCYTE T EXPRIMANT UN CAR ET UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to the field of cell therapy, and specifically relates to a method for preparing a CAR-expressing T cell and a use. Disclosed in the present invention is a method for preparing a CAR-T cell, comprising the following steps: S1, collecting a T cell-containing cell population of an autologous or allogeneic donor of a subject; S2, administering lymphodepletion therapy to the subject for pretreatment; and S3, administering the T cell-containing cell population and a viral vector to the subject.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention presents a CAR-T cell preparation method that integrates lymphodepletion pretreatment (S2) with concurrent administration of T cells and viral vector (S3), potentially optimizing in vivo transduction and CAR-T cell engraftment. The competitive significance lies in the simplified ex vivo manufacturing footprint and potential cost reduction by shifting transduction to the patient's body, though clinical efficacy compared to conventional ex vivo approaches remains unclear.

patents.title: VECTEUR COMPRENANT DE MULTIPLES MOLÉCULES DE CIBLAGE ET PROCÉDÉ D'AMÉLIORATION DE L'EFFICACITÉ DE TRANSDUCTION D'UN VECTEUR
patents.abstract: Provided are a vector comprising multiple targeting molecules, and a method for improving transduction efficiency of a vector. Provided is a vector comprising multiple targeting molecules. The efficiency of transducing non-activated T cells by the vector is improved. Also provided is a method for improving transduction efficiency of a vector. The method can effectively improve the efficiency of transducing non-activated T cells by the vector.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a vector with multiple targeting molecules designed to improve transduction efficiency specifically in non-activated T cells, addressing a key challenge in ex vivo CAR-T manufacturing where primary T cells often remain quiescent. The multi-targeting approach represents a competitive innovation for enhancing lentiviral or similar vector-based CAR-T production by reducing the need for T cell activation prior to genetic modification.

patents.title: UTILISATION D'UN ANTAGONISTE DE CYTOKINE DANS LA PRÉPARATION D'UN MÉDICAMENT POUR LA PRÉVENTION ET/OU LE TRAITEMENT DU SLC
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to the field of cell therapies, and in particular to use of a cytokine antagonist in the preparation of a drug for preventing and/or treating death from CRS. Disclosed is use of a cytokine antagonist in the preparation of a drug for preventing and/or treating death from CRS, the cytokine antagonist being a TNFα antagonist.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims use of TNFα antagonists specifically for preventing/treating cytokine release syndrome (CRS)-related mortality in cell therapy contexts. This addresses a significant clinical challenge in CAR-T and adoptive T cell therapies where CRS is a dose-limiting toxicity; the selective targeting of TNFα for CRS mitigation represents a targeted approach to managing therapy-related cytotoxicity rather than broad immunosuppression.

patents.title: NANOCORPS CIBLANT CD7 ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to the field of nanobodies, and specifically relates to a CD7-targeting nanobody and a use thereof. Disclosed is a CD7-targeting nanobody. The nanobody has a small molecular weight and low immunogenicity, and is more suitable for clinical applications such as cell therapy and gene therapy.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: A CD7-targeting nanobody with claimed advantages of small molecular weight and low immunogenicity designed for cell therapy and gene therapy applications. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is moderate—CD7 targeting is relevant for T-cell malignancies, but nanobodies as standalone therapeutics differ mechanistically from CAR-T cell engineering; however, nanobodies could potentially be incorporated into CAR designs or used as adjunctive targeting agents.

patents.title: VÉSICULE EXTRACELLULAIRE, PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉPARATION S'Y RAPPORTANT ET UTILISATION ASSOCIÉE
patents.abstract: An extracellular vesicle. The surface of the extracellular vesicle comprises at least part of a viral envelope glycoprotein or a variant thereof; the at least part of the viral envelope glycoprotein or the variant thereof does not bind to a receptor or the binding to a receptor is inhibited; and the extracellular vesicle is difficult to infect a cell by binding to a glycoprotein receptor. When the extracellular vesicle is used for delivering a target protein, the targeting performance of the extracellular vesicle is significantly improved. When an extracellular vesicle membrane expresses a hydrophobic protein, the expression and purification of the hydrophobic protein are facilitated.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes extracellular vesicles (EVs) engineered with modified viral envelope glycoproteins that have ablated or inhibited receptor-binding capacity, enabling improved targeting performance and facilitating expression/purification of hydrophobic cargo proteins. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery as it addresses EV-mediated delivery of therapeutic payloads with enhanced specificity and reduced off-target binding, potentially improving biodistribution and reducing immune clearance through pseudo-infection pathways.

patents.title: SYSTÈME D'ENCAPSIDATION DE VECTEUR VIRAL ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided are a packaging system for packaging a lentiviral vector or a retroviral vector, and a use of the packaging system. Specifically, the provided packaging system comprises a polynucleotide encoding a CAR binding molecule, wherein the CAR binding molecule can bind to a CAR. Pseudotransduction is reduced when a host cell is transduced by the lentiviral vector or the retroviral vector packaged by the provided packaging system, and the ability to transduce a target cell expressing an antigen decreases, thereby significantly improving the targeting performance of the lentiviral vector or the retroviral vector in the transduction of immune cells such as T cells.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention provides a lentiviral/retroviral packaging system encoding a CAR-binding molecule that reduces pseudotransduction while maintaining target cell transduction capability, thereby improving targeting specificity for T cell transduction in CAR-T manufacturing. This addresses a key manufacturing challenge by reducing off-target transduction and improving the purity and efficacy of CAR-T cell products.

patents.title: POLYPEPTIDE ET VECTEUR VIRAL CONTENANT UN GÈNE CODANT POUR UN POLYPEPTIDE
patents.abstract: Provided in the present invention are a TCP polypeptide and a viral vector containing a gene encoding the TCP polypeptide. The viral vector further contains a T cell-activation signaling molecule, and can effectively target, activate and transduce T cells.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention combines a TCP (T cell-targeting) polypeptide with a viral vector encoding this polypeptide alongside a T cell-activation signaling molecule, enabling efficient targeting and transduction of T cells. This dual-component approach (targeting polypeptide + activation signaling integrated into a single vector) is potentially significant for CAR-T manufacturing as it could streamline vector design and improve T cell engineering efficiency by co-delivering both targeting/activation signals and therapeutic genes.

patents.title: PARTICULE VIRALE, SON PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉPARATION ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: A viral particle. The surface of the viral particle comprises a T cell activation primary signaling molecule and a T cell activation secondary signaling molecule; the envelope glycoprotein of the viral particle is subjected to a first mutation, so that the receptor binding ability of the viral glycoprotein is weakened or lost with respect to its receptor binding ability before the first mutation; and the envelope glycoprotein of the viral particle can also be subjected to a second mutation, so that the viral particle has enhanced resistance to complement-mediated inactivation or is not subjected to complement-mediated inactivation. The viral particle has improved specificity for targeted activation, stimulation and transduction of non-activated T cells, and is thus more applicable for the preparation of CAR-T cells in subjects.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes engineered viral particles with surface-displayed T cell activation signals (primary and secondary) combined with mutations that ablate or weaken natural receptor binding while enhancing complement resistance. This combination aims to achieve targeted T cell activation and transduction with improved specificity, potentially enabling more controlled CAR-T cell manufacturing and activation without off-target viral tropism.

patents.title: ANTICORPS À DOMAINE UNIQUE CIBLANT CD79B, RÉCEPTEUR ANTIGÉNIQUE CHIMÉRIQUE ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: A single-domain antibody targeting CD79B, a chimeric antigen receptor, and a use thereof. Provided are an anti-CD79B single-domain antibody, a chimeric antigen receptor constructed using the single-domain antibody, and an engineered immune effector cell. Also provided is a use of the single-domain antibody, the chimeric antigen receptor, and the engineered immune effector cell in the preparation of a drug for the treatment of CD79B and/or B cell-related diseases.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims a single-domain antibody (sdAb) targeting CD79B integrated into a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) architecture, along with engineered immune effector cells expressing this CAR construct. The novelty centers on using sdAb-based CARs (potentially offering improved manufacturing, reduced immunogenicity, and faster tissue penetration compared to scFv-based CARs) to target CD79B on B-cell malignancies and B-cell disorders—a clinically relevant target given CD79B's role in B-cell receptor signaling.

patents.title: VECTEUR VIRAL ET SON UTILISATION DANS L'INFECTION DE LYMPHOCYTES B
patents.abstract: A lentiviral vector or retroviral vector, and a use thereof in infecting B cells, establishing acquired immunity in a subject, and preparing a broadly neutralizing antibody. The viral envelope of the lentiviral vector or retroviral vector comprises targeting molecules targeting B cells and carries a broadly neutralizing antibody gene; the viral glycoprotein of the lentiviral vector or retroviral vector may further comprise a first mutation that attenuates the receptor binding ability thereof and a second mutation that enhances the ability thereof to antagonize complement inactivation, and further enhances the ability of the lentiviral vector or retroviral vector to target and transduce B cells in a subject and prepare a broadly neutralizing antibody.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention combines engineered lentiviral/retroviral vectors with B cell-targeting envelope modifications and broadly neutralizing antibody (bNAb) gene cargo for in vivo B cell transduction and therapeutic antibody production. Novelty lies in the dual glycoprotein mutations (attenuated receptor binding + enhanced complement antagonism) optimizing B cell targeting and transduction efficiency, positioning this as a platform for HIV/infectious disease immunotherapy distinct from conventional CAR-T approaches.

patents.title: VECTEUR VIRAL ET UTILISATION DE LA SOUS-UNITÉ TCR
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to the field of genetic engineering, and in particular to a viral vector and a use of a TCR subunit. Provided is a lentiviral vector or a retroviral vector. The ability to infect a target cell by the lentiviral vector or the retroviral vector is reduced. Also disclosed is a use of a TCR subunit or a functional fragment thereof in the preparation of the lentiviral vector or the retroviral vector.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes lentiviral or retroviral vectors with reduced ability to infect target cells, incorporating TCR subunits or functional fragments for vector engineering. The novelty lies in using TCR subunits as components in viral vector construction, potentially enabling safer or more controlled transduction profiles for cell engineering applications, with competitive significance for reducing off-target transduction in CAR-T manufacturing.

patents.title: VECTEUR ET PROCÉDÉ DE TRANSFECTION IN VITRO DE LYMPHOCYTES T NON ACTIVÉS
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to the field of genetic engineering, and specifically relates to a vector and a method for transfecting non-activated T cells in vitro. Disclosed in the present invention are a vector and a method of using the vector to come into contact with non-activated T cells and transfect the non-activated T cells. The surface of the vector comprises one or more antibodies or antigen-binding fragments thereof and/or ligands or receptor binding fragments thereof that specifically bind to endocytic receptors of non-activated T cells; and the vector can carry a nucleic acid encoding a CAR, enters the non-activated T cells by means of endocytosis initiated by the specific binding of the endocytic receptors of the non-activated T cells, and then effectively transfects the non-activated T cells. Therefore, the technical problem whereby it is difficult to effectively transfect non-activated T cells in the process of preparing CAR-T cells in vitro is effectively solved, ther
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a vector with surface-displayed antibodies or ligands that specifically target endocytic receptors on non-activated T cells to enable receptor-mediated endocytosis and CAR gene delivery without requiring T cell activation. This approach is significant for CAR-T manufacturing because it eliminates the need for pre-activation steps, potentially reducing production time, cost, and improving transduction efficiency in primary T cells.

patents.title: VSVG MUTANT ET VECTEUR DE CIBLAGE
patents.abstract: Provided are a mutant VSVG and a targeting vector, belonging to the field of vector delivery. An envelope glycoprotein of vesicular stomatitis virus having a first mutation and a second mutation is provided, the first mutation causes the envelope glycoprotein to be unable to mediate complement inactivation; and the second mutation weakens the ability of the envelope glycoprotein to be recognized by a receptor. A targeting vector is also provided, which comprises: a first molecule that binds to an endocytic receptor of a target cell and a second molecule that is non-complement inactivated and promotes the release of a substance carried by the targeting vector into the cytoplasm; the second molecule promotes the endosomal escape or lysosomal escape of the targeting vector and prevents the targeting vector from being inactivated by a complement.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a dual-mutant VSVG envelope glycoprotein with ablated complement inactivation and weakened native receptor recognition, combined with a targeting vector system that incorporates endocytic receptor-binding molecules and fusogenic moieties for enhanced intracellular delivery. This addresses immunogenicity and off-target transduction challenges in pseudotyped viral vector systems used for cell and gene therapy.

patents.title: VECTEUR ET UTILISATION CORRESPONDANTE
patents.abstract: A vector and the use thereof in the field of gene delivery. The vector is a virus vector having a viral envelope, wherein (a) the surface of the virus vector having the viral envelope contains one or more ligands specifically binding to a lymphocyte endocytic receptor; (b) the envelope glycoprotein of the virus vector having the viral envelope has a first mutation, so that the ability of the envelope glycoprotein to specifically bind to a receptor is weakened or lost; and (c) the envelope glycoprotein of the virus vector having the viral envelope can also have a second mutation, so that the ability of the virus vector having the viral envelope to antagonize the inactivation by the complement is enhanced or the virus vector having the viral envelope is not inactivated by the complement.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered viral vectors with lymphocyte-targeting ligands on the viral envelope surface, combined with mutations that ablate native receptor binding (first mutation) and optionally enhance complement resistance (second mutation). This targeted approach enables selective transduction of lymphocytes while reducing off-target infection, which is significant for in vivo CAR-T applications as it could improve safety and efficacy of T cell engineering by minimizing systemic viral exposure and enhancing lymphocyte-specific gene delivery.

patents.title: VECTEUR DE CIBLAGE, SON PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉPARATION ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided are a targeting vector and a method for targeting same to a host cell. The vector comprises a first molecule that binds to an endocytosis receptor of the target cell and a second molecule that promotes the release of a substance carried by the targeting vector into a cytoplasm. When the targeting vector is a viral vector, the first molecule is not part of a viral envelope protein, and the second molecule promotes endosomal escape or lysosomal escape of the targeting vector. The first molecule is designed according to the endocytosis receptor of the cell to be targeted, different types of cells can be targeted, and after a reasonable mutation is carried out on the vector, infection of cells that do not need to be targeted can be avoided, thereby improving the accuracy of the vector.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a targeting vector with modular components: a first molecule binding to cell-specific endocytosis receptors and a second molecule promoting endosomal/lysosomal escape, designed to improve targeting specificity and reduce off-target transduction. This approach is relevant to in vivo CAR-T delivery as it addresses the critical challenge of directing viral vectors to T cells while minimizing toxicity to non-target tissues, potentially improving efficacy and safety of adoptive T cell therapy.

patents.title: MÉDICAMENT, MÉTHODE ET UTILISATION POUR TRAITER DES MALADIES PROVOQUÉES PAR LA PRODUCTION D'AUTOANTICORPS RÉSULTANT D'UNE PROLIFÉRATION EXCESSIVE DE LYMPHOCYTES B
patents.abstract: Provided are a drug, a method, and use for treating diseases caused by autoantibody production resulting from excessive proliferation of B cells. The drug for treating diseases caused by autoantibody production resulting from excessive proliferation of B cells comprises: an mRNA encoding a chimeric antigen receptor molecule and a T cell targeting lipid nanoparticle. The drug can produce a chimeric antigen receptor T cell in vivo. The lipid nanoparticle comprises: a cationic lipid, a phospholipid, cholesterol, a PEG lipid, and a targeting molecule. The targeting molecule mediates T cell targeting. The lipid nanoparticle encapsulating the mRNA of the chimeric antigen receptor molecule (mRNA-LNP) is used to deliver the mRNA into a T cell in vivo to produce the chimeric antigen receptor T cell, and pathological autoreactive B cells are eliminated to achieve the treatment of diseases caused by autoantibody production resulting from excessive proliferation of B cells.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN MAGICRNA BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 深圳虹信生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents an in vivo CAR-T cell therapy using mRNA-LNP (lipid nanoparticle) technology with T cell-targeting capability, designed to treat autoimmune diseases driven by excessive B cell proliferation and autoantibody production. The key innovation is the LNP formulation incorporating a targeting molecule that mediates direct T cell targeting to enable CAR-T cell generation in vivo rather than ex vivo manufacturing. This addresses manufacturing complexity and scalability challenges inherent in traditional CAR-T therapies, positioning it as a potential competitive advantage for treating autoimmune rather than oncologic indications.

patents.title: AMINO LIPID, AND LIPID NANOPARTICLES AND USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: The present invention provides an amino lipid, and lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and a use thereof, the amino lipid having a structure represented by general formula (I), or an isomer, pharmaceutically acceptable salt, prodrug or solvate of the amino lipid. The present invention further provides LNPs containing the amino lipid. According to the present invention, the amino lipid having a structure represented by general formula (I) is used as an ionizable lipid compound, and the LNPs are obtained by means of self-assembly of the ionizable lipid compound, a steroid, a neutral lipid, and a polymer-bonded lipid. The LNPs can further improve the translation expression level of a nucleic acid load in cells, improve the effect of a nucleic acid-LNP preparation, and enable the nucleic acid-LNP preparation to provide a theoretical basis for personalized treatment.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN MAGICRNA BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHENZHEN MAGICRNA BIOTECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a novel amino lipid with ionizable properties designed as a component of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), formulated with steroids, neutral lipids, and polymer-bonded lipids to enhance nucleic acid translation and expression in cells. This addresses a key challenge in gene therapy delivery by improving LNP-mediated cellular uptake and transgene expression, which is directly applicable to CAR-T engineering where efficient mRNA or DNA delivery is critical for generating functional engineered T cells.

patents.title: AMINOLIPID, HERSTELLUNGSVERFAHREN UND ANWENDUNG DAVON
patents.abstract: The disclosure belongs to the technical field of medical chemistry, particularly relates to an amino lipid and their preparation method as well as an application thereof, and provides the ionizable amino lipids with a general formula as shown in Formula (I), or pharmaceutically acceptable salts thereof. The amino lipids of the disclosure can be used for delivering nucleic acids and small molecule drugs. The amino lipid compounds have two ester bonds, which obviously enhance the lysosome escape capability of the ionizable amino lipids, and are favorable for the release of delivery targets of a targeted drug or gene, etc., thus improving the delivery efficiency, and showing the good capability of delivering nucleic acids into cells in the in-vitro and in-vivo delivery study.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN MAGICRNA BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; Shenzhen MagicRNA Biotechnology Co., Ltd.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses ionizable amino lipids with a dual ester bond architecture designed to enhance lysosomal escape capability and improve nucleic acid delivery efficiency. For in vivo CAR-T applications, these lipids could offer competitive advantages in mRNA delivery by providing superior intracellular release kinetics and reduced off-target effects compared to single ester bond lipid nanoparticles, potentially enabling more efficient CAR-T mRNA transfection.

patents.title: AMINOLIPIDE ET SON APPLICATION
patents.abstract: An amino lipid and an application thereof: using ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF), a dual-function electrophile, to build an amine head group and a hydrophobic chain into an amino lipid, fully utilizing the click chemical reaction properties of ESF; in the process of constructing the amino lipid, reaction conditions are mild, protection and deprotection are not needed, and atom economy is high. In vitro and in vivo delivery studies show an excellent ability to deliver nucleic acid into cells. The amino lipid compound is provided with two sulfonamides, and the introduction of the group significantly enhances the stability of lipid nanoparticles and improves the in-vivo cycle time, thereby improving in-vivo delivery efficiency. The preparation method of the amino lipid compound has the advantages of readily available raw materials, mild reaction conditions, good reaction selectivity, high reaction yield, low requirements for instruments and equipment, and simple operations.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN MAGICRNA BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 深圳虹信生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: Novel amino lipid synthesized using ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a dual-function electrophile with mild reaction conditions and high atom economy. The lipid incorporates sulfonamide groups that enhance lipid nanoparticle (LNP) stability and in vivo circulation time, improving nucleic acid delivery efficiency.

patents.title: CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) library screening method of lipid metabolism related genes for targeted tumor immunotherapy
patents.abstract: The invention provides a CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) library screening method of lipid metabolism related genes for targeted tumor therapy. Specifically, the invention develops a lipid metabolism related gene design specific sgRNA for targeted tumor treatment for the first time, and constructs a CRISPR library screening method, so as to realize high-throughput screening of functional genes for targeted tumor treatment.
patents.assignee: BIG HEALTH RES INSTITUTE OF HEFEI INTEGRATED SCIENCES CENTER; 合肥综合性国家科学中心大健康研究院
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a novel CRISPR library screening approach specifically targeting lipid metabolism genes to identify functional genes for tumor immunotherapy. The competitive significance lies in the systematic high-throughput identification of lipid metabolism modulators that enhance anti-tumor immune responses, potentially enabling next-generation CAR-T cell engineering through metabolic reprogramming to improve efficacy and persistence.

patents.title: New tumor immune intervention target SIDT1, inhibitor thereof and application of new tumor immune intervention target SIDT1 in tumor resistance
patents.abstract: According to the invention, a novel immune checkpoint molecule SIDT1 is found. The SIDT1 is a powerful T cell inhibition factor mainly expressed on CD8 < + > T cells. A series of SIDT1 inhibitors are identified in the invention. The SIDT1 inhibitor can enhance the anti-tumor CD8T cell reaction and limit tumor progression, so that a new thought is provided for treatment and prevention of related tumor patients with PD-1 treatment resistance.
patents.assignee: BIG HEALTH RES INSTITUTE OF HEFEI INTEGRATED SCIENCES CENTER; UNIV SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY CHINA; 合肥综合性国家科学中心大健康研究院
patents.novelty_summary: The patent identifies SIDT1 as a novel immune checkpoint molecule expressed on CD8+ T cells that functions as a T cell inhibition factor, and discloses SIDT1 inhibitors that enhance anti-tumor CD8+ T cell responses. This represents a new immunosuppressive mechanism distinct from PD-1/PD-L1 axis, with potential therapeutic application in patients resistant to anti-PD-1 therapy, offering a complementary checkpoint target for T cell-based immunotherapy.

patents.title: CRISPR-Cas12m system and application thereof
patents.abstract: The invention discloses a CRISPR-Cas12m (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) system and application thereof, and relates to the technical field of biological medicines. The CRISPR-Cas system is a CRISPR-Cas12m system and comprises a Cas12m polypeptide, and the amino acid sequence of the Cas12m polypeptide is as follows: (1) the amino acid sequence of the Cas12m polypeptide is shown as any one of SEQ ID NO.1-21; and (2) compared with the sequence as shown in SEQ ID NO.1-21, the sequence has 70% of sequence identity. The molecular weight of the Cas12m protein is small, in-vivo delivery is facilitated, and the protein has DNA binding activity and does not have DNA cleavage activity. The protein can be combined with an adenosine deaminase structural domain to form a base editor, and can also be combined with a transcriptional regulation structural domain to form an epigenetic editor.
patents.assignee: BIG HEALTH RES INSTITUTE OF HEFEI INTEGRATED SCIENCES CENTER; 合肥综合性国家科学中心大健康研究院
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses Cas12m nuclease variants with small molecular weight optimized for in vivo delivery, featuring DNA-binding capability without cleavage activity, enabling fusion with adenosine deaminase for base editing applications. This addresses a key bottleneck in delivering CRISPR machinery to T cells in vivo, potentially enabling direct CAR-T engineering without ex vivo manipulation.

patents.title: Antibody specifically binding to CD48-1 protein or antigen binding fragment thereof and application thereof
patents.abstract: The invention discloses an antibody specifically binding to CD48-1 protein or an antigen binding fragment thereof and application thereof, and belongs to the technical field of biological medicine. The invention further discloses application of the antigen binding fragment specifically binding to the CD48-1 protein, the antibody, polynucleotide, an expression vector, a host cell and the conjugate. The invention also discloses a pharmaceutical composition which comprises one of the antigen binding fragment specifically binding to the CD48-1 protein, an antibody, polynucleotide, an expression vector, a host cell and a conjugate. The antibody or the antigen binding fragment thereof has the beneficial effects that immunological rejection caused by species difference does not exist, and the antibody or the antigen binding fragment thereof has specific binding performance to human CD48-1 full-length protein, can be used for detecting the CD48-1 protein and diagnosing diseases related to the
patents.assignee: BIG HEALTH RES INSTITUTE OF HEFEI INTEGRATED SCIENCES CENTER; UNIV SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY CHINA; 合肥综合性国家科学中心大健康研究院
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses monoclonal antibodies or antigen-binding fragments (scFv, Fab, etc.) specifically targeting CD48-1 protein, with claimed advantages including reduced immunological rejection from species differences. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is limited; this appears to be a target-binding reagent rather than a CAR construct or T-cell engineering technology, though CD48-1 antibodies could potentially serve as checkpoint modulators or target identification tools in CAR-T development.

patents.title: NOUVELLES TRANSPOSASES ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to highly efficient PiggyBac transposases identified through language-model guided correction of genome mined transposons.
patents.assignee: INTEGRA THERAPEUTICS [ES]; INTEGRA THERAPEUTICS
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes engineered PiggyBac transposases optimized through computational language-model guided correction of naturally mined transposon sequences, improving transposition efficiency. This is significant for CAR-T cell engineering as PiggyBac transposases enable non-viral, integrating gene delivery to enable robust CAR construct insertion with potentially higher efficiency than wild-type transposases, reducing viral vector dependence and manufacturing complexity.

patents.title: Nucleic acid vectors and methods of use
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to nucleic acid vectors (e.g., circular DNA vectors) and compositions thereof. Also provided are methods of administering nucleic acid vectors (e.g., circular DNA vectors) and compositions thereof, e.g., in combination with pulsed electric field therapy. Also provided are methods and compositions for treating cancer (e.g., cancer characterized by the presence of a solid tumor) by administering a nucleic acid vector carrying a heterologous gene to modulate the tumor microenvironment.
patents.assignee: INTEGRA THERAPEUTICS INC; 英特格拉治疗公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes circular DNA vectors administered with pulsed electric field (PEF) therapy for cancer treatment, particularly targeting solid tumors by modulating the tumor microenvironment through heterologous gene delivery. The combination of circular DNA vectors with PEF-mediated delivery represents a potentially novel approach to overcome barriers in solid tumor treatment, though the competitive significance depends on the specific genes delivered and efficacy data relative to viral vectors and established CAR-T platforms.

patents.title: UTILISATION DE TRANSPOSASES POUR AMÉLIORER L’EXPRESSION TRANSGÉNIQUE ET LA LOCALISATION NUCLÉAIRE
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to methods of increasing expression of a transgene of interest in a cell population and/or of increasing nuclear localization of a transgene of interest in a cell population, using a transposase.
patents.assignee: INTEGRA THERAPEUTICS [ES]; UNIV POMPEU FABRA [ES]; INTEGRA THERAPEUTICS
patents.novelty_summary: This invention uses transposases to enhance transgene expression and nuclear localization in cell populations. For in vivo CAR-T applications, this could improve CAR construct integration efficiency and expression levels, potentially enhancing therapeutic efficacy by achieving higher or more stable CAR protein production in engineered T cells.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ DE PRODUCTION D'UNE GRANDE RECOMBINASE À SÉRINE SPÉCIFIQUE D'UNE CIBLE
patents.abstract: The present invention pertains to a method for generating a target-specific large serine recombinase (LSR), the method comprising the steps of: a) generating a plurality of first variants of an LSR by introducing one or more mutations into a sequence encoding the LSR; b) generating a library of expression vectors, wherein each expression vector comprises a first region encoding one of the first variants of an LSR, and a second region comprising at least two first target sites of the LSR, wherein the two first target sites are different from each other; c) introducing the library of expression vectors into host cells; d) culturing the host cells and expressing the first variant LSR; e) isolating plasmid DNA from the culture of host cells; f) determining whether a portion of the second region of the expression vector between the two first target sites has been excised by the variant LSR; g) generating a plurality of second LSR variants by introducing one or more mutations into the sequen
patents.assignee: SEAMLESS THERAPEUTICS GMBH [DE]; SEAMLESS THERAPEUTICS GMBH
patents.novelty_summary: This patent describes a directed evolution approach to generate target-specific large serine recombinases (LSRs) through iterative mutagenesis and selection. LSRs are site-specific recombinases that can be engineered for precise genomic integration, offering potential advantages over currently used integration systems in CAR-T manufacturing by enabling safer, more controllable transgene insertion with reduced genotoxicity risk.

patents.title: Electrotransfection module for organ conformal, bioelectronic patch and preparation method and application of bioelectronic patch
patents.abstract: The invention discloses an electrotransfection module for organ conformal, a bioelectronic patch and a preparation method and application of the bioelectronic patch, an electrotransfection module body is of a paper-cut structure and comprises a substrate layer, an electrode layer, a medicine storage layer and a nanopore layer, and the substrate layer, the electrode layer, the medicine storage layer and the nanopore layer are sequentially stacked together from bottom to top; cutting according to a paper-cut pattern conformal with the target organ to form inlaid paper-cut units connected through hinges; and integrating a wireless communication module to obtain the bioelectronic patch. A paper-cut conformal theory is adopted, a paper-cut structure electrotransfection module and a bioelectronic patch for organ conformal are designed and prepared on the basis of the characteristic slope of a target organ, seamless covering of the target organ is achieved, and meanwhile safe, controllable an
patents.assignee: UNIV BEIHANG; 北京航空航天大学
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a novel organ-conformal bioelectronic patch with an electrotransfection module using paper-cut architecture for localized drug/molecule delivery via electrical stimulation. While the electrotransfection concept is established, the organ-conformal paper-cut design and integration with wireless communication represents a differentiated delivery platform that could enhance in vivo transfection efficiency and tissue conformability compared to rigid electrode systems.

patents.title: Recombinant chimpanzee oncolytic adenovirus Adsimian-delta24-IL21 as well as construction method and application thereof
patents.abstract: The invention discloses a recombinant chimpanzee oncolytic adenovirus Adsimian-delta24-IL21 and a construction method and application thereof, the vector is based on serotype 25 chimpanzee adenovirus, the immunogenicity is reduced by deleting an E3 region, and the integrin targeting is enhanced by inserting an RGD peptide fragment; a skeleton plasmid pAdsimian-deltaE3 is in seamless cloning connection with a shuttle plasmid pSRK17-delta24-CMV carrying delta24 mutation E1A, a recombinant oncolytic adenovirus Adsimian-delta24-IL21 and a control virus Adsimian-delta24-EGFP are constructed, the delta24 mutation enables the virus specificity to be copied in Rb defect tumor cells, the IL-21 gene remodels a tumor immune microenvironment by activating CD3 +/CD8 + T cells, and the tumor immune microenvironment of the Rb defect tumor cells is improved. The invention provides an efficient carrier and a method for oncolytic-immune combined treatment of colorectal cancer.
patents.assignee: UNIV ZHEJIANG SCIENCE & TECH; ZHEJIANG SCI TECH UNIV SHAOXING ACADEMY OF BIOMEDICINE CO LTD; 浙江理工大学
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a chimpanzee oncolytic adenovirus (Adsimian-delta24-IL21) engineered with reduced immunogenicity (E3 deletion), enhanced tumor targeting (RGD insertion), tumor-specific replication (delta24 mutation in E1A), and IL-21 transgene for T cell activation. The significance lies in combining oncolytic virotherapy with immunogene therapy to remodel the tumor microenvironment by activating CD8+ T cells, potentially offering a synergistic approach to overcome CAR-T limitations in solid tumors.

patents.title: DNA library screening method of intracellular mRNA sensor switch and application
patents.abstract: The invention provides a DNA library screening method and application of an intracellular mRNA sensor switch. The DNA library screening method comprises the following steps: designing a DNA library containing a switch sequence of a degenerate basic group; preparing a circular expression vector library; preparing a minimum linear expression vector library; performing seamless cloning; carrying out RCA rolling circle amplification; carrying out telomerase digestion; carrying out cell transfection; extracting RNA (Ribonucleic Acid) and carrying out reverse transcription; carrying out library building of next-generation sequencing by taking the cDNA as a template; carrying out next-generation sequencing; analyzing data and comparing to obtain the DNA library of the mRNA sensor switch. According to the DNA library screening method provided by the invention, more sensor switch sequences can be provided for a single site on mRNA in cells, and more selection possibilities are further provided
patents.assignee: BEIJING CANCER HOSPITAL BEIJING CANCER HOSPITAL; 北京肿瘤医院（北京大学肿瘤医院）
patents.novelty_summary: This invention presents a DNA library screening methodology for identifying and optimizing intracellular mRNA sensor switches through iterative cycles of in vitro amplification, cell transfection, and next-generation sequencing-based selection. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T lies in enabling rational design of synthetic mRNA sensors that could improve CAR-T activation specificity and reduce off-target effects by incorporating intelligent genetic switches responsive to tumor-associated mRNA signatures.

patents.title: Recombinant oncolytic vaccinia virus VV-dTVA-CD55-alpha PDL1 as well as construction method and application thereof
patents.abstract: The invention discloses a recombinant oncolytic vaccinia virus VV-dTVA-CD55-alphaPDL1 as well as a construction method and application thereof, three key sites of vaccinia virus genome TK, VGF and A56R are systematically knocked out through a CRISPR/Cas9 technology, a human CD55 gene and an alphaPD-L1 antibody gene are directionally inserted into the A56R site, accurate assembly of gene elements is completed through technologies such as PCR amplification, homologous recombination and seamless cloning, and the recombinant oncolytic vaccinia virus VV-dTVA-CD55-alphaPDL1 is obtained. Through verification, the recombinant virus can stably express CD55 and alphaPDL1 proteins, meanwhile, the genome stability is kept, and a research direction is provided for providing a novel biological preparation with high targeting property and high safety for treatment of malignant tumors such as colorectal cancer.
patents.assignee: ZHEJIANG SCI TECH UNIV SHAOXING ACADEMY OF BIOMEDICINE CO LTD; UNIV ZHEJIANG SCIENCE & TECH; 浙江理工大学绍兴生物医药研究院有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a recombinant oncolytic vaccinia virus engineered to express both CD55 (complement regulatory protein) and an anti-PD-L1 antibody through systematic CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletions (TK, VGF, A56R) and directed gene insertion. This dual immunomodulatory approach is potentially significant for overcoming PD-L1-mediated immune suppression and complement-mediated viral clearance, offering a novel oncolytic virus platform for cancer immunotherapy that could complement CAR-T strategies by pre-conditioning the tumor microenvironment.

patents.title: Editing guidance system
patents.abstract: The invention relates to a guided editing system, in particular to pegRNA, a pegRNA combination, a vector for expressing the pegRNA or the pegRNA combination, a vector for expressing PE protein, a tool cell, a guided editing system, a guided editing method, a kit and application of the pegRNA, the pegRNA combination, the vector, the tool cell, the guided editing system, the guided editing method and the kit in preparation of drugs for treating genetic diseases. The pegRNA comprises a first Csy4 endo ribonuclease recognition site and a second Csy4 endo ribonuclease recognition site, and the first Csy4 endo ribonuclease recognition site and the second Csy4 endo ribonuclease recognition site are subjected to enzyme digestion by Csy4 endo ribonuclease. According to the invention, high editing efficiency can be maintained between different target sites and cell types, and large-fragment DNA can be inserted and/or seamless editing can be realized.
patents.assignee: UNIV TSINGHUA; 清华大学
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a prime editing (PE) guidance system utilizing pegRNA with dual Csy4 endonuclease recognition sites that enable enzymatic maturation and improved editing efficiency for genetic disease treatment. This modular pegRNA architecture with Csy4-mediated processing could enhance the precision and control of prime editing outcomes in therapeutic applications, including potential T cell engineering for CAR-T therapies.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ DE PRODUCTION DE LEUCOCYTES EXPRIMANT DES RÉCEPTEURS D'ANTIGÈNES CHIMÉRIQUES
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) suitable for transfecting a leukocyte, which nanoparticle comprises an mRNA encoding for a transposase enzyme, and a DNA encoding for an antigen receptor.
patents.assignee: T CURX GMBH [DE]; T-CURX GMBH
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) co-delivering mRNA-encoded transposase and DNA encoding chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) for ex vivo leukocyte engineering. The approach is significant for CAR-T manufacturing as it combines non-viral transfection with transposon-mediated genomic integration, potentially offering a faster, simpler, and GMP-scalable alternative to viral vector-based CAR-T production without requiring electroporation.

patents.title: VERBESSERTES TRANSPOSON-SYSTEM ZUR GENVERABREICHUNG
patents.abstract: Described is a transposon system comprising (a) a transposon unit containing inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) or direct terminal repeats (DTRs) that flank a sequence of interest to be inserted into the genome of a target cell; and (b) an RNA encoding a transposase capable of recognizing said ITRs and transposing said sequence of interest into said genome; wherein said RNA encoding said transposase is characterized in that it contains a combination of unmodified and modified nucleotides, wherein 5 to 50% of the uridine nucleotides and 5 to 50% of the cytidine nucleotides are respectively modified uridine nucleotides and modified cytidine nucleotides. Moreover, described is the use of a said transposon system for the ex vivo gene delivery into a target cell. Further, described is an ex vivo method for gene delivery into a target cell comprising the following steps: (a) bringing into contact the transposon system according to any one of claims 1 to 4 with a cell; (b) culturing said cell u
patents.assignee: T CURX GMBH [DE]; T-CURX GmbH
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes an improved transposon system for gene delivery featuring a transposase RNA with strategically modified nucleotides (5-50% modified uridines and cytidines), designed to enhance translational efficiency and reduce immunogenicity during ex vivo cell engineering. This addresses key challenges in non-viral genetic modification of primary T cells, enabling more efficient CAR-T manufacturing while potentially improving safety by reducing innate immune activation.

patents.title: CONSTRUCTIONS POUR L'EXPRESSION MULTI-LIGNÉE D'AGENTS THÉRAPEUTIQUES
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides nucleic acid constructs engineered to express therapeutic expression products from regulatory sequences that drive expression in hematopoietic cell populations. For example, the present disclosure includes nucleic acid constructs in which a first regulatory sequence drives expression of a first therapeutic expression product and a second regulatory sequence drives expression of a second therapeutic expression product. Nucleic acid constructs can be delivered to cells or subjects by viral vectors, including adenoviral vectors, e.g., for the treatment of cancer.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes dual-regulatory sequence constructs engineered for lineage-specific expression of multiple therapeutic products in hematopoietic cells, delivered via viral vectors (particularly adenoviral) for cancer treatment. The competitive significance lies in enabling simultaneous expression of complementary therapeutic agents (potentially including CAR constructs) in target immune cell populations through independent, lineage-controlled promoters, which could improve efficacy and reduce off-target effects compared to single-agent approaches.

patents.title: VECTEURS AUXILIAIRES ADÉNOVIRAUX
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides, among other things, helper genomes and vectors useful in gene therapy, e.g., for production of helper-dependent donor vectors. Helper genomes of the present disclosure include a conditionally defective packaging sequence.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses helper adenoviral genomes with conditionally defective packaging sequences designed to improve helper-dependent adenoviral vector production for gene therapy applications. The conditional defectiveness provides enhanced safety and manufacturability advantages for therapeutic vector production, with potential relevance to ex vivo cell engineering workflows.

patents.title: VECTORES AUXILIARES ADENOVIRALES DEL SEROTIPO 35
patents.abstract: La presente divulgación proporciona, entre otras cosas, genomas auxiliares Ad35 y vectores útiles en la terapia génica, por ejemplo, para la producción de vectores donantes Ad35 dependientes de los auxiliares. Los genomas auxiliares de la presente divulgación incluyen una secuencia de empaquetamiento condicionalmente defectuosa.  Reivindicación 1: Un genoma auxiliar adenoviral recombinante que comprende: una repetición de terminal invertida (ITR) Ad35 5; una ITR Ad35 3; y repeticiones directas de recombinasa que flanquean una secuencia de empaquetamiento de Ad35, donde las repeticiones directas de recombinasa comprenden una primera repetición directa de recombinasa entre las posiciones de nucleótidos correspondientes a 155 y 171, 161 y 181, 185 y 205 o 214 y 234 del nº de registro de GenBank AY128640 y una segunda repetición directa de recombinasa entre las posiciones de nucleótidos correspondientes a 377 y 504 o 3175 y 3225 del nº de registro de GenBank AY128640. Reivindicación 16: Un
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses Ad35 helper genome constructs with conditionally defective packaging sequences flanked by recombinase-recognition sites, enabling controlled production of helper-dependent Ad35 vectors for gene therapy applications. This represents a technical advance in adenoviral vector engineering by providing conditional control over helper virus replication, which is significant for safer and more efficient gene delivery in therapeutic contexts.

patents.title: MODIFICATIONS DE MGMT RÉSISTANTE AUX INHIBITEURS ET MODIFICATION D'ACIDES NUCLÉIQUES CODANT MGMT
patents.abstract: The present disclosure includes MGMT modifications that cause MGMT resistance to MGMT inhibitors. The present disclosure also includes in vivo, in vitro, and ex vivo modification of MGMT -encoding nucleic acids to encode and express an MGMT variant that is resistant to MGMT inhibitors. Inhibitor-resistant MGMT modifications and modification of an MGMT- encoding nucleic can occur or be used in conjunction with a therapeutic modification, e.g., in a single cell. Expression of inhibitor-resistant MGMT can selectively protect modified cells from a selection regimen, such as a selection regimen including an MGMT inhibitor and an alkylating agent. Accordingly, in vivo, in vitro, and ex vivo modification of MGMT -encoding nucleic acids can be used in gene therapy to select for modified cells.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; FRED HUTCHINSON CANCER CENTER [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses MGMT variants engineered to resist MGMT inhibitors, enabling selective enrichment of gene-modified cells through a dual-selection strategy (MGMT inhibitor + alkylating agent). This addresses a key bottleneck in ex vivo and in vivo gene therapy by allowing positive selection of therapeutically-modified cells without requiring physical sorting, with potential applications to CAR-T and other cell therapies requiring robust cell expansion and safety control.

patents.title: VARIANTS D’ENDONUCLÉASE CAS12A ET MÉTHODES D’UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides endonuclease variants having improved properties, such as hyperactivity and/or low indiscriminate single strand DNase activity, relative to the corresponding wild-type endonucleases.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA APS [DK]; ENSOMA APS
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered Cas12a endonuclease variants with improved hyperactivity and reduced off-target single-strand DNase activity compared to wild-type. This is relevant to CAR-T and gene therapy as optimized CRISPR-Cas12a variants could enhance precision of ex vivo T cell editing with reduced collateral DNA damage, improving safety and efficacy of engineered cell therapies.

patents.title: VECTEURS ADENOVIRAUX DE THERAPIE GENIQUE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure includes adenoviral vectors characterized by efficient transduction of hematopoietic cells (e.g., one or more particular types of hematopoietic cells), e.g., for in vivo or ex vivo gene therapy. The present disclosure includes, among other things, Ad3, Ad5, Ad7, Ad11, Ad14, Ad16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad35, Ad37, and Ad50 vectors and genomes. Ad3, Ad5, Ad7, Ad11, Ad14, Ad16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad35, Ad37, and Ad50 vectors and genomes of the present disclosure can include therapeutic payloads.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses adenoviral vectors (Ad3, Ad5, Ad7, Ad11, Ad14, Ad16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad35, Ad37, Ad50) engineered for efficient transduction of hematopoietic cells in both in vivo and ex vivo gene therapy contexts. The competitive significance lies in providing alternative adenoviral serotypes with improved hematopoietic cell tropism and therapeutic payload delivery, potentially offering better in vivo gene transfer compared to conventional Ad5-based approaches for ex vivo T cell engineering or in vivo lymphocyte targeting.

patents.title: MODIFICATION D'ACIDES NUCLÉIQUES CODANT POUR EPOR
patents.abstract: Gene therapy typically modifies some, but not all, cells of a population of target cells. One approach to increasing the prevalence of modified cells includes delivering to the modified cells a gene that provides a competitive advantage (e.g., a proliferative advantage) and therefore results in enrichment of modified cells. The present disclosure including, among other things, methods and compositions for providing a competitive advantage to one or more cells by providing to the cells a nucleic acid encoding a signaling-enhanced EpoR polypeptide (e.g., a truncated EpoR or gain-of-function EpoR).
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses use of signaling-enhanced erythropoietin receptor (EpoR) polypeptides—including truncated or gain-of-function variants—as selectable markers to confer proliferative advantage to genetically modified cells in vivo, enabling enrichment of therapeutically modified cell populations. This approach is significant for CAR-T and other cell therapies by providing a non-immunogenic enrichment strategy that could increase the frequency of successfully engineered cells without requiring cytotoxic selection or immunodominant markers.

patents.title: VECTEURS ADENOVIRAUX DE THERAPIE GENIQUE
patents.abstract:
[0001]    The present disclosure includes adenoviral vectors characterized by efficient transduction of HSCs, e.g., for in vivo gene therapy. The present disclosure includes, among other things, Ad3, Ad7, Ad11, Ad14, Ad16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad37, and Ad50 vectors and genomes. Ad3, Ad7, Ad11, Ad14, Ad16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad37, and Ad50 vectors and genomes of the present disclosure can include therapeutic payloads.
