La présente invention comprend, entre autres, les vecteurs et génomes Ad3, Ad7, Ad11, Ad 14, Ad 16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad37, et Ad50. Les vecteurs et génomes Ad3, Ad7, Ad11, Ad 14, Ad 16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad37, et Ad50 de la présente invention peuvent comprendre des charges thérapeutiques.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses adenoviral vectors (Ad3, Ad7, Ad11, Ad14, Ad16, Ad21, Ad34, Ad37, Ad50) engineered for efficient transduction of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) in in vivo gene therapy applications. The competitive significance lies in enabling direct in vivo HSC modification without ex vivo manipulation, potentially reducing manufacturing complexity and improving therapeutic accessibility for blood and immune cell disorders.

patents.title: VECTEURS ADENOVIRAUX DE SEROTYPE 35 AUXILIAIRES
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides, among other things, Ad35 helper genomes and vectors useful in gene therapy, e.g., for production of helper-dependent Ad35 donor vectors. Helper genomes of the present disclosure include a conditionally defective packaging sequence.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses Ad35 helper genomes with conditionally defective packaging sequences for generating helper-dependent adenoviral vectors in gene therapy applications. The conditional defectiveness represents a refinement over conventional helper systems, potentially enabling safer and more efficient production of therapeutic Ad35 vectors for ex vivo and in vivo gene delivery.

patents.title: Methods and compositions for transducing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in vivo
patents.abstract: The invention relates to the
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; UNIV WASHINGTON [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent addresses in vivo transduction of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), enabling direct genetic modification without ex vivo cell manipulation. This approach is highly significant for CAR-T and gene therapy as it eliminates manufacturing bottlenecks, reduces costs, and potentially improves therapeutic outcomes by preserving cell function during engineering.

patents.title: DOSING REGIMENS FOR THE MOBILIZATION OF HEMATOPOIETIC STEM AND PROGENITOR CELLS
patents.abstract: [0000]    The invention provides compositions and methods useful for mobilizing populations of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells within a donor, as well as for determining whether samples of mobilized cells are suitable for release for ex vivo expansion and/or therapeutic use. In accordance with the compositions and methods described herein, mobilized hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells can be withdrawn from a donor and administered to a patient for the treatment of various stem cell disorders, including hematopoietic diseases, metabolic disorders, cancers, and autoimmune diseases, among others. In certain embodiments, the compositions and methods described herein lead to the mobilization of a population of CD34<dim >cells that have immunosuppressive effects and that can reduce the incidence of graft vs. host disease.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; Ensoma, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes dosing regimens for mobilizing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), particularly CD34dim cells with immunosuppressive properties, and methods for their release qualification. This is relevant to CAR-T as mobilized HSPCs can serve as source material for ex vivo expansion and therapeutic applications, potentially including engineered cell therapies, though the patent does not explicitly focus on CAR-T engineering or antigen-specific modifications.

patents.title: DOSING REGIMENS FOR THE MOBILIZATION OF HEMATOPOIETIC STEM AND PROGENITOR CELLS.
patents.abstract: The invention provides compositions and methods useful for mobilizing populations of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells within a donor, as well as for determining whether samples of mobilized cells are suitable for release for ex vivo expansion and/or therapeutic use. In accordance with the compositions and methods described herein, mobilized hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells can be withdrawn from a donor and administered to a patient for the treatment of various stem cell disorders, including hematopoietic diseases, metabolic disorders, cancers, and autoimmune diseases, among others. In certain embodiments, the compositions and methods described herein lead to the mobilization of a population of CD34<sup>dim</sup> cells that have immunosuppressive effects and that can reduce the incidence of graft vs. host disease.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; ENSOMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes dosing regimens for mobilizing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), with particular focus on mobilizing CD34dim cells with immunosuppressive properties. The competitive significance for CAR-T lies in the potential to generate or co-mobilize regulatory cell populations that could modulate immune responses, though the direct application to CAR-T engineering and manufacturing is indirect and primarily relevant to source material preparation rather than CAR-T cell creation itself.

patents.title: DOSING REGIMENS FOR THE MOBILIZATION OF HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS
patents.abstract: Described herein are compositions and methods useful for mobilizing populations of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells within a subject, as well as for determining whether samples of mobilized cells are suitable for release for ex vivo expansion and/or therapeutic use. In accordance with the composition and methods described herein, mobilized hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells can be withdrawn from a donor and administered to a patient for the treatment of various disorders, including hematopoietic diseases, metabolic disorders, cancers, and autoimmune diseases, among others.
patents.assignee: ENSOMA INC [US]; Ensoma, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes novel dosing regimens for mobilizing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) and criteria for determining suitability of mobilized cell populations for therapeutic use. The competitive significance for cell therapy lies in optimizing HSPC mobilization and release criteria, which could improve the efficiency and quality of cell products for ex vivo expansion and downstream therapeutic applications including CAR-T and other cell-based therapies derived from mobilized progenitor populations.

patents.title: PARTICULES VIRALES À PRÉSENTATION FUSOGÈNE ET COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles containing a viral envelope attachment protein, such as derived from paramyxovirus or baboon endogenous virus (BaEV). In some embodiments, the lipid particles also contain a codisplay protein, such as a transduction adjuvant or an immune stimulating protein. Also provided are such lipid particles that are viral vectors, such as lentiviral vectors or lentiviral-like particles. Also provided are producer cells and compositions containing such lipid particles and methods of making and using the lipid particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents lipid particles displaying viral envelope attachment proteins (paramyxovirus, BaEV) with optional codisplay of transduction adjuvants or immune-stimulating proteins, enabling enhanced cell targeting and transduction. This is significant for CAR-T delivery as it addresses a key bottleneck in in vivo T cell engineering—efficient, targeted delivery of lentiviral vectors to T cells while potentially reducing off-target immunogenicity through tunable fusogenic and immune properties.

patents.title: SAFETY SWITCHES TO CONTROL IN VITRO AND IN VIVO PROLIFERATION OF CELL THERAPY PRODUCTS
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides modified cells comprising a nucleic acid encoding an agent (e.g., a detection agent, a selection agent, or a detection agent and a selection agent) inserted at an endogenous proliferation gene or off-target cell marker gene, as well as compositions, methods, uses, and kits related thereto.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; Sana Biotechnology, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses modified cells with nucleic acids encoding detection/selection agents inserted at endogenous proliferation or off-target marker genes to control in vitro and in vivo proliferation. This represents a novel safety switch architecture using gene disruption-based controls for cell therapy products, offering competitive advantage for CAR-T by enabling kill-switch functionality and selective expansion control without external transgenes.

patents.title: GPRC5D-SPECIFIC ANTIBODY CONSTRUCTS AND COMPOSITIONS THEREOF
patents.abstract: [0000]    Disclosed herein are antibodies or antigen binding fragments that specifically bind human GPRC5D. Also disclosed are chimeric antigen receptors and chimeric antigen receptor transgenes comprising an antigen binding domain that specifically binds human GPRC5D and fusion proteins comprising a Henipavirus glycoprotein G and a GPRC5D antibody, or an antigen binding fragment thereof. Viral vectors and other compositions containing the antibodies or antigen binding fragments thereof, chimeric antigen receptors and chimeric antigen receptor transgenes, and fusion proteins are disclosed. The present disclosure additionally relates to cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors, as well as methods of delivering the various antibodies and chimeric antigen receptors and methods of using cells expressing the chimeric antigen receptors.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; Sana Biotechnology, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses GPRC5D-specific antibody constructs integrated into CAR-T architectures, along with novel Henipavirus glycoprotein G fusion proteins for enhanced cellular delivery. This represents competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T therapies by combining validated tumor-targeting (GPRC5D is expressed on multiple myeloma and other hematologic malignancies) with Sana's proprietary cell engineering and delivery platform, potentially improving CAR-T persistence and trafficking.

patents.title: LYMPHOCYTES T CAR CIBLANT CD22 HYPOIMMUNOGÈNES POUR LE TRAITEMENT DE LYMPHOMES À LYMPHOCYTES B RÉCIDIVANT ET/OU RÉFRACTAIRE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods of treating a subject having or suspected of having a B cell malignancy or a B cell mediated disorder by administering hypoimmune allogenic CD22-directed CAR T cells. Also disclosed are pharmaceutical compositions comprising hypoimmune allogenic CD22-directed CAR T cells, for use in treating a subject having or suspected of having a B cell malignancy or a B cell mediated disorder.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses hypoimmune allogeneic CD22-directed CAR T cells for treating B cell malignancies and B cell-mediated disorders. The competitive significance lies in the use of hypoimmune (reduced immunogenicity) allogeneic CAR-T cells targeting CD22, enabling off-the-shelf cell therapy products that avoid graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and rejection while maintaining anti-tumor efficacy—a key advantage over autologous CAR-T approaches for scalability and accessibility.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ DE CRIBLAGE D'UN ÉCHANTILLON CONTENANT UN TRANSGÈNE À L'AIDE D'UN CODE À BARRES UNIQUE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods to detect a barcode sequence(s), wherein the barcode sequence indicates the presence of a transgene inserted into a cell or population of cells, methods of screening a sample for said barcode sequence(s), cells or populations of cells comprising one or more vectors encoding said transgene(s) and barcode(s), compositions thereof, and therapeutic uses and kits related thereto.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses methods for detecting transgene integration using unique barcode sequences as molecular markers, enabling high-throughput screening and tracking of engineered cells. This is significant for CAR-T and cell therapy manufacturing as it provides a scalable quality control and cell selection approach to identify successfully transduced cells and monitor clonal composition in therapeutic populations.

patents.title: PROTÉINES CD47 MODIFIÉES ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides engineered CD47 proteins and uses thereof. Also disclosed are polynucleotides encoding the engineered CD47 protein, vectors comprising the polynucleotides, cells comprising the engineered proteins and/or the vectors, and compositions comprising the engineered CD47 protein.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered CD47 proteins with modifications that enhance immune evasion properties, delivered via vectors into cells—a strategy highly relevant to CAR-T immunotherapy to reduce host rejection and improve in vivo persistence. The competitive significance lies in addressing a major failure mode of allogeneic CAR-T therapy by engineering the innate immune checkpoint CD47 to protect therapeutic cells from macrophage-mediated killing and complement-dependent cytotoxicity.

patents.title: FUSOGÈNES EN TANDEM ET PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES ASSOCIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles containing at least two attachment proteins derived from a paramyxovirus envelope attachment protein and at least one paramyxovirus fusion (F) protein. Also provided are lipid particles are viral vectors, such as lentiviral vectors or lentiviral-like particles. Also provided are producer cells and compositions containing such lipid particles and methods of making and using the lipid particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses lipid particles incorporating tandem paramyxovirus attachment and fusion proteins to enhance cellular uptake and transduction efficiency. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery as improved lipid nanoparticle (LNP) engineering with optimized envelope proteins could increase transduction rates of primary T cells while reducing off-target effects and immunogenicity compared to conventional LNP formulations.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS DE DOSAGE ET D'ADMINISTRATION DE CELLULES D'ÎLOTS MODIFIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of dosing engineered islet cells that include functional modified beta cell containing one or more modifications, such as genetic modifications. In some embodiments, the engineered islets are hypoimmunogenic cells. In some embodiments, the one or more modifications reduce or eliminate expression of one or more MHC class I and/or MHC class II human leukocyte antigens and also increase expression of one or more tolerogenic factors, such as CD47. In some embodiments, the subject has a beta cell related disorder, such as diabetes (e.g. Type I diabetes).
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents engineered islet cells with dual immunomodulatory modifications—MHC downregulation combined with tolerogenic factor upregulation (e.g., CD47)—along with dosing/administration methods for treating beta cell disorders. The competitive significance for cell therapy lies in the hypoimmunogenic cell engineering approach, which parallels CAR-T strategies for evading immune rejection, though applied to allogeneic islet transplantation rather than adoptive T cell therapy.

patents.title: LYMPHOCYTES T CAR ANTI-CD19 POUR LE TRAITEMENT DE MALIGNITÉS DE LYMPHOCYTES B ET DE MALADIES AUTO-IMMUNES
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods of treating a subject having or suspected of having a B cell malignancy or a B cell mediated disorder by administering hypoimmune allogenic CD19-directed CAR T cells. Also disclosed are pharmaceutical compositions comprising hypoimmune allogenic CD19-directed CAR T cells, for use in treating a subject having or suspected of having a B cell malignancy or a B cell mediated disorder.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents hypoimmune allogeneic CD19-directed CAR-T cells for treating B cell malignancies and autoimmune disorders. The competitive significance lies in the use of allogeneic (off-the-shelf) rather than autologous CAR-T cells with engineered immune tolerance, potentially enabling faster manufacturing timelines, reduced patient-specific manufacturing costs, and broader accessibility compared to standard autologous CAR-T approaches.

patents.title: DOSAGE NUMÉRIQUE UTILISANT DES GOUTTELETTES POUR DÉTECTER UN VECTEUR LENTIVIRAL COMPÉTENT POUR LA RÉPLICATION
patents.abstract: Among other things, the present disclosure provides methods for the detection of replication competent lentiviral vectors.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent discloses digital dosage methods using droplets to detect replication-competent lentiviral (RCL) vectors. The approach is significant for CAR-T and gene therapy manufacturing quality control, as RCL contamination is a critical safety concern in lentiviral-mediated T cell transduction and engineering.

patents.title: FUSOGÈNES DE PROTÉINE G UNIVERSELLE ET SYSTÈMES ADAPTATEURS DE CEUX-CI ET PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES ET UTILISATIONS ASSOCIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles, such as lenti viral particles, that incorporate or are pseudotyped with paramyxovirus envelope attachment glycoproteins as fused to at least one component of a universal adapter system, and in some aspects also a fusion (F) protein such as a NiV-F protein or a biologically active portion or variant thereof. The present disclosure also provides for preparation of the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, comprising at least one component of the universal adapter system, as well as methods for preparing and using the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents engineered lentiviral particles pseudotyped with paramyxovirus envelope glycoproteins fused to universal adapter system components, enabling modular and flexible targeting of diverse cell types. This represents a significant advance for CAR-T delivery by decoupling targeting ligands from viral particles through adapter technology, potentially improving manufacturing scalability and enabling rapid retargeting without regenerating new viral vectors.

patents.title: FUSOGÈNES DE PROTÉINE G MODIFIÉS ET PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES ASSOCIÉES ET PROCÉDÉS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles, such as lenti viral particles, that incorporate or are pseudotyped with a retargeted paramyxovirus envelope attachment protein fused to a targeting moiety inserted within a peptide loop of the paramyxovirus envelope attachment protein, and in some aspects also a fusion (F) protein such as a NiV-F protein or a biologically active portion or variant thereof. The present disclosure also provides for preparation of the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, comprising a retargeted paramyxovirus envelope attachment protein fused to a targeting moiety inserted within a peptide loop of the paramyxovirus envelope attachment protein, as well as methods for preparing and using the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents modified paramyxovirus envelope proteins (attachment/G proteins) with inserted targeting moieties within peptide loops, pseudotyped onto lentiviral particles for enhanced cell-specific transduction. This retargeting approach offers competitive advantage for in vivo CAR-T delivery by enabling tissue-specific or cell-type-specific targeting of therapeutic genetic cargo while maintaining fusogenic capacity through co-incorporation of F proteins.

patents.title: VECTEURS LENTIVIRAUX À DEUX GÉNOMES OU PLUS
patents.abstract: Among other things, provided are an engineered lentiviral vector comprising a first genome and a second genome. A first genome can comprise a first transgene. A second genome can comprise a second transgene. In some embodiments, a first and a second transgene are different. Further provided are engineered lentiviral vector systems for producing such an engineered lentiviral vector. Also, provided are methods of making engineered lentiviral vectors and compositions comprising engineered lentiviral vectors.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses lentiviral vectors engineered to carry two or more independent genomes, each capable of expressing distinct transgenes within a single viral particle. This multi-genome architecture enables simultaneous delivery of multiple therapeutic genes to target cells, addressing a key limitation in CAR-T and gene therapy where sequential transduction or dual-vector systems are typically required, thereby potentially improving co-expression efficiency and reducing manufacturing complexity.

patents.title: IDENTIFICATION DE NOUVEAUX SITES DE ZONES DE SÉCURITÉ POUR L'EXPRESSION STABLE D'UN VECTEUR LENTIVIRAL FUSOGÈNE
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides cells modified by insertion of one or more exogenous sequences into a genomic safe harbor site, as well as compositions, methods, uses and kits related thereto.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent identifies novel genomic safe harbor sites for stable integration of fusogenic lentiviral vectors into cell genomes, enabling improved transgene expression without disrupting critical endogenous genes. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T therapy as safe harbor sites facilitate durable, stable expression of CAR constructs while minimizing genotoxicity risks and off-target integration events that could compromise therapeutic efficacy or safety.

patents.title: SOURIS AUTO-IMMUNE PRÉSENTANT UN DIABÈTE DE TYPE 1
patents.abstract: Among other things, provided are non-human animals comprising immune cells (e.g., peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs)) from a human patient with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and islet cells derived from the human patient with type 1 diabetes (T1D), wherein the immune cells (e.g., PBMCs) and the islet cells are autologous. Methods for use of such non-human animals are also described.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes humanized non-human animals containing autologous human immune cells (PBMCs) and islet cells from T1D patients, creating an in vivo disease model that preserves patient-specific autoimmune pathology. This is significant for CAR-T and cell therapy development as it enables personalized testing of engineered T cell therapies against patient-derived autoantigens in a physiologically relevant microenvironment.

patents.title: CONSTRUCTIONS D'ANTICORPS SPÉCIFIQUES DE CD19 ET COMPOSITIONS ASSOCIÉES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are antibodies or antigen binding fragments thereof that specifically bind human CD19. Also disclosed are chimeric antigen receptors and chimeric antigen receptor transgenes comprising an antigen binding domain that specifically binds human CD19. Also described herein are immune cells, viral vectors, and other compositions containing the antibodies, antigen binding fragments, chimeric antigen receptors, and/or chimeric antigen receptor transgenes.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses CD19-specific antibodies and antigen binding fragments integrated into chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) and CAR transgenes, along with immune cell compositions containing these constructs. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T lies in providing engineered T cell compositions with defined CD19-targeting scFv domains that can be delivered via viral vectors, potentially offering improved specificity and manufacturing consistency for CD19+ B-cell malignancy treatment.

patents.title: PROCESSUS DE PRODUCTION DE VECTEURS VIRAUX
patents.abstract: Among other things, provided are compositions and methods for producing viral vectors. Provided herein are methods of producing a composition comprising viral vectors, the method comprising culturing producer cells that comprise one or more nucleic acids for the production of the viral vector under conditions sufficient to produce the viral vectors. In some embodiments, the viral vectors comprise a lipid bilayer, and the one or more nucleic acids comprise at least one nucleic acid that encodes one or more fusogens. In some embodiments, the one or more fusogens are present in the lipid bilayer. Methods herein are characterized by (i) a 10-fold increase in the number of active vector particles, (ii) a 10-fold reduction in host cell protein, and/or (iii) a 3000- fold reduction in host cell DNA, relative to an alternative process.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes viral vector production methods achieving 10-fold increases in active particle yield with simultaneous 10-fold reductions in host cell protein contamination and significant reductions in host cell DNA, representing substantial process optimization for vector manufacturing. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery as improved vector production efficiency, purity, and safety profile directly enhance the viability and regulatory pathway for ex vivo CAR-T manufacturing and potential in vivo T cell engineering applications requiring high-titer, clean vector preparations.

patents.title: CONSTRUCTIONS D'ANTICORPS SPÉCIFIQUES DE BCMA ET COMPOSITIONS ASSOCIÉES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are antibodies or antigen binding fragments thereof that specifically bind human BCMA. Also disclosed are chimeric antigen receptors and chimeric antigen receptor transgenes comprising an antigen binding domain that specifically binds human BCMA. Also described herein are immune cells, viral vectors, and other compositions containing the antibodies, antibody binding fragments, chimeric antigen receptors and/or chimeric antigen receptor transgenes.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses BCMA-specific antibodies and their integration into chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), along with CAR-transgenic immune cells and viral delivery vectors. This is directly relevant to CAR-T cell therapy as BCMA is a validated target for multiple myeloma and light chain disease; the novelty lies in the specific antibody constructs and their delivery via viral vectors in engineered T cells, representing a complete therapeutic platform rather than isolated components.

patents.title: PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES AVEC COFUSOGÈNES ET LEURS PROCÉDÉS DE PRODUCTION ET D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles containing at least two attachment proteins derived from a paramyxovirus envelope attachment protein and at least one paramyxovirus fusion (F) protein. Also provided are lipid particles are viral vectors, such as lentiviral vectors or lentiviral-like particles. Also provided are producer cells and compositions containing such lipid particles and methods of making and using the lipid particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes lipid particles incorporating dual paramyxovirus attachment proteins and fusion proteins, potentially enabling improved cellular targeting and membrane fusion for viral vector delivery. This represents a novel engineering approach to enhance transduction efficiency and specificity for lentiviral and lentiviral-like vectors, which could improve CAR-T cell manufacturing by enabling more efficient gene delivery into primary T cells with reduced off-target effects.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS ET SYSTÈMES POUR DÉTERMINER DES CARACTÉRISTIQUES DE CELLULES DONATRICES ET FORMULER DES PRODUITS DE THÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE SUR LA BASE DE CARACTÉRISTIQUES DE CELLULES
patents.abstract: Methods of profiling cells for donor capability with a recipient subject are provided. In particular, methods relating to identifying cells, such as T cells, suitable for making a cell therapy product and administration to a patient (e.g., as CAR T cell therapy). Methods are also provided of profiling the donor capability of a cell or population of cells for cell therapy, such methods comprising evaluating the cell or the population of cells for predicted function. A predicted cell function may be evaluated by assaying one or more cell parameters. Further, cells and cell therapy products manufactured according to such methods are provided.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents methods for profiling donor T cells and other cell types to predict their functional capability for CAR-T therapy manufacturing, enabling rational selection of donor cells and formulation of cell therapy products based on measurable cell parameters. This approach offers competitive significance by potentially improving CAR-T product quality, potency, and consistency through donor-matched manufacturing decisions rather than post-manufacture screening alone.

patents.title: PARTICULES VIRALES CIBLANT DES CELLULES SOUCHES HÉMATOPOÏÉTIQUES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are targeted lipid particles, such as targeted lentiviral particles, having a targeting agent that binds to a target molecule selected from the group consisting of ASCT1, ASCT2, CD105, CD110, CD117, CD133, CD146, CD164, CD34, CD46, CD49f, CD90, EPCR, and ITGA3, and related polynucleotides, cells, and methods for preparation and use of the targeted lipid particles, such as lenti viral particles. Also provided herein are methods involving mobilizing bone marrow cells in combination with administering targeted or non-targeted lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, for treatment of a disease or condition in a subject.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents targeted lentiviral particles with surface-engineered targeting agents directed at hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) markers (CD34, CD117, CD133, CD146, etc.), enabling selective transduction of primitive bone marrow populations. This addresses a significant in vivo CAR-T challenge: improving gene delivery specificity to HSCs for ex vivo or in vivo cell engineering while reducing off-target transduction, with competitive advantage in mobilization-combination regimens for therapeutic applications.

patents.title: 저면역원성 RHD 음성 1차 T 세포
patents.abstract: 환자에게 투여하기 위한 감소된 RhD 항원의 발현을 갖는 저면역원성 T 세포가 본 명세서에 개시된다. 일부 구현예에서, 세포는 1차 T 세포 또는 그 자손으로부터 증식되거나, 유도 다능성 줄기 세포(iPSC)로부터 유래된다. 일부 구현예에서, 세포는 외인성으로 CD47 단백질을 발현하고, MHC I형 단백질, MHC II형 단백질, 또는 둘 다의 감소된 발현을 나타낸다. 일부 구현예에서, 세포는 외인성으로 하나 이상의 키메라 항원 수용체를 발현한다.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; 사나 바이오테크놀로지, 인크.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses low-immunogenic T cells with reduced RhD antigen expression, engineered to express exogenous CD47 and optionally reduced MHC-I/II expression, enabling allogeneic CAR-T cell therapy with reduced immune rejection. This addresses a key challenge in off-the-shelf cellular therapy by combining multiple immune-evasion modifications (CD47, HLA downregulation, RhD reduction) to enable universal donor T cells for in vivo therapeutic applications.

patents.title: PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES COMPRENANT DES GLYCOPROTÉINES FIXANT DES PARAMYXOVIRUS VARIANTS ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles, including viral-based particles, comprising Paramyxovirus glycoproteins having reduced glycosylation, and in some aspects, comprise variant G/H proteins. Also provided are methods for producing and modifying lipid particles, including viral-based particles, wherein the particle has reduced glycosylation of the G/H protein, as well as methods for using the particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes lipid particles (including viral-based particles) engineered with variant paramyxovirus glycoproteins (G/H proteins) featuring reduced glycosylation. This represents a novel modification strategy for enhancing lipid particle properties, potentially improving cellular targeting, immunogenicity modulation, or biodistribution—characteristics that could be significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery by enabling more efficient T cell transduction and reduced innate immune activation.

patents.title: ADMINISTRATION DE PROTÉINES HÉTÉROLOGUES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles and compositions thereof for delivery of heterologous proteins, including genome-modifying agents, to cells.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes lipid particles for intracellular delivery of heterologous proteins, including genome-modifying agents. This is relevant to CAR-T cell engineering as lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) represent a non-viral delivery platform for introducing genetic modifications and therapeutic proteins into T cells, offering potential advantages over viral vectors in terms of manufacturing scale-up, immunogenicity profile, and manufacturing control.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS DE TRANSDUCTION UTILISANT UN VECTEUR VIRAL ET DES INHIBITEURS DE FACTEURS DE RESTRICTION ANTIVIRAUX
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of transducing or delivering an exogenous agent to a cell using a viral vector pseudotyped with a paramyxovirus and an inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR). In some embodiments, the methods can further include the administration of an antiviral restriction factor inhibitor and/or a cytokine.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes methods of viral vector transduction using paramyxovirus pseudotyped vectors combined with mTOR inhibitors and optionally antiviral restriction factor inhibitors to enhance cell transduction efficiency. This approach is potentially significant for in vivo CAR-T applications by improving lentiviral or other viral vector-mediated T cell engineering while reducing innate immune activation through restriction factor inhibition.

patents.title: POLYTHÉRAPIES D'AGONISTE DE RÉCEPTEUR DE CYTOKINE ET DE VECTEUR VIRAL
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of transducing or delivering a transgene to a T cell using T tell-targeted viral vectors and a cytokine receptor agonist.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes combined use of T cell-targeted viral vectors with cytokine receptor agonists to enhance transgene delivery and T cell transduction efficiency. This combination approach is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T therapies as it addresses key challenges in achieving effective T cell engineering by synergizing targeted viral delivery with immune stimulation to improve transduction rates and potentially expand engineered T cell populations.

patents.title: CELLULES D'INGÉNIERIE AVEC UN TRANSGÈNE DANS UN LOCUS B2M OU CIITA ET COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods for generating immune evasive cells by inserting one or more transgenes encoding one or more tolerogenic factors such as CD47 into one or more endogenous gene loci such as B2M locus and CHIA locus. The methods may further include reducing expression of one or more MHC I and/or one or more MHC II molecules. Also disclosed are therapeutic cells and compositions derived from these methods.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a novel approach to engineering immune-evasive cells by simultaneously knocking out immunogenic loci (B2M and CIITA for MHC I/II suppression) while inserting tolerogenic transgenes (e.g., CD47) into these same endogenous loci. This dual strategy of targeted gene disruption combined with therapeutic transgene insertion at immunologically relevant loci represents a significant advance in allogeneic cell therapy by reducing rejection risk while enhancing transplant acceptance—particularly valuable for off-the-shelf CAR-T and other engineered cell therapies.

patents.title: PROTÉINES CD47 MODIFIÉES ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses modified CD47 proteins and their uses, likely as immunoevasion agents to prevent phagocytosis of engineered cells. For in vivo CAR-T applications, enhanced CD47 expression or modified CD47 variants could improve persistence and efficacy by protecting CAR-T cells from innate immune clearance, representing a significant competitive advantage in cell therapy durability.

patents.title: MÉTHODES DE TRAITEMENT DE PATIENTS PRÉSENTANT UNE THÉRAPIE PRÉALABLE AYANT ÉCHOUÉ AVEC DES CELLULES HYPOIMMUNOGÈNES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are engineered cells comprising one or more CARs directed to a first therapeutic target and one or more CARs directed to a second therapeutic target, as well as methods of using such engineered cells. Also provided herein are methods of treating a disease or disorder in a patient that has previously been administered one or more targeted therapies, the method comprising administering a population of engineered CAR-T cells to the patient. In some embodiments, one or more targeted therapies comprised administration of a first therapeutic agent, wherein the first therapeutic agent is directed to a first therapeutic target. In some embodiments, engineered CAR-T cells of the population comprise one or more chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), wherein at least one CAR encoded by the one or more exogenous polynucleotides is directed to a second therapeutic target, wherein the first therapeutic target and the second therapeutic target are different.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered CAR-T cells expressing multiple CARs targeting distinct therapeutic targets, combined with methods for treating patients who have failed prior targeted therapies. The competitive significance lies in addressing therapy-resistant disease through dual-targeting CAR-T cells and potentially leveraging hypoimmunogenic cell engineering (Sana's platform) to reduce immunogenicity and enable repeat dosing in pre-treated patients.

patents.title: VECTEURS LENTIVIRAUX CIBLANT CD3 ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of transducing T cells using CD3-targeted viral vectors.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes CD3-targeted lentiviral vectors for efficient T cell transduction, representing a selective delivery approach that could improve CAR-T manufacturing by enhancing transduction specificity and reducing off-target effects. This is competitively significant as it addresses a key manufacturing bottleneck in CAR-T cell production by enabling targeted genetic modification of T cells while minimizing exposure of non-T cell populations.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS D'ADMINISTRATION ET DE DOSAGE RÉPÉTÉS DE PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES OU DE VECTEURS VIRAUX ET SYSTÈMES ET UTILISATIONS CONNEXES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of repeated administration of a lipid particle or viral vector, such as for delivery of a payload gene, to a subject.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent addresses repeated administration regimens of lipid particles or viral vectors for payload gene delivery, which is clinically relevant for overcoming immunogenicity and dosing limitations in in vivo CAR-T applications where repeated dosing may be necessary for sustained therapeutic effect or re-dosing strategies in engineered cell therapies.

patents.title: MÉTHODES DE DOSAGE ET D'ADMINISTRATION EX VIVO DE PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES OU DE VECTEURS VIRAUX AINSI QUE SYSTÈMES ET UTILISATIONS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of ex vivo administration of a lipid particle or a payload gene, to a subject. In some embodiments, the methods are in-line methods of administration of a lipid particle or payload gene that are performed in a closed fluid circuit. Also provided are related compositions, containers, and systems in connection with the provided methods.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents ex vivo administration methods for lipid particles or viral vectors in closed-circuit systems, with potential application to cell engineering. This addresses manufacturing automation and sterility control in cell therapy manufacturing, which is significant for CAR-T scalability and GMP compliance, though the patent does not explicitly focus on CAR-T or T cell engineering.

patents.title: LYMPHOCYTES T A RECEPTEUR ANTIGENIQUE CHIMERIQUE (CAR) POUR LE TRAITEMENT D'UNE MALADIE AUTO-IMMUNE ET METHODES ASSOCIEES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic cells including engineered and/or hypoimmunogenic stem cells, engineered and/or hypoimmunogenic cells differentiated therefrom, engineered and/or hypoimmunogenic CAR-T cells (primary or differentiated from engineered and/or hypoimmunogenic stem cells) and related methods of their use and generation for use in the treatment of autoimmune diseases/disorders and/or inflammatory diseases/disorders. Provided herein are engineered and/or hypoimmunogenic cells exhibiting reduced expression of MHC class I and/or MHC class II human leukocyte antigens and T-cell receptors for use in the treatment of autoimmune diseases/disorders and/or inflammatory diseases/disorders. In some embodiments, such cells also exogenously express one or more tolerogenic factors such as CD47 and one or more chimeric antigen receptors (CARS).
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses hypoimmunogenic engineered CAR-T cells with reduced MHC class I/II and TCR expression for treating autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, representing a novel application of CAR-T technology beyond oncology. The competitive significance lies in enabling allogeneic CAR-T cell therapy for autoimmune indications with reduced rejection risk and potential off-the-shelf manufacturing advantages.

patents.title: GLYCOPROTÉINES DE FUSION DE PARAMYXOVIRIDAE MODIFIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, that incorporate or are pseudotyped with a variant Nipah Virus F (NiV-F) envelope glycoprotein, and in some aspects also an attachment glycoprotein (G) protein such as a NiV-G protein or a biologically active portion or variant thereof. Also provided are polynucleotides encoding the variant NiV-F and producer cells for preparation of the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, containing the variant NiV-F proteins, as well as methods for preparing and using the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: Modified Nipah Virus (NiV) envelope glycoproteins (F and G proteins) incorporated into lentiviral particles for pseudotyping, enabling improved targeting and transduction efficiency for gene delivery. The variant NiV-F glycoproteins represent a novel envelope engineering approach that expands the tropism and safety profile of lentiviral vectors for in vivo CAR-T cell engineering applications, potentially offering superior performance to conventional VSV-G pseudotyped vectors.

patents.title: GLYCOPROTÉINES DE FIXATION DE PARAMYXOVIRIDAE MODIFIÉES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles, such as lenti viral particles, that incorporate or are pseudotyped with a variant Nipah Virus G (NiV-G) envelope glycoprotein, and in some aspects also a fusion (F) protein such as a NiV-F protein or a biologically active portion or variant thereof. Also provided are polynucleotides encoding the variant NiV-G and producer cells for preparation of the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, containing the variant NiV-G proteins, as well as methods for preparing and using the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents modified Nipah Virus G (NiV-G) envelope glycoproteins incorporated into lentiviral particles for pseudotyping, with potential inclusion of NiV-F fusion proteins. This represents a novel pseudotyping strategy using paramyxoviral glycoproteins that could enhance tropism and transduction efficiency of lentiviral vectors for therapeutic gene delivery, offering competitive advantages in targeted cell engineering applications.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS ET SYSTÈMES DE PRODUCTION DE PARTICULES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of producing lipid membrane bound particles, such as lentiviral vectors, that contain one or more Paramyxovirus envelope proteins in the lipid bilayer. Also provided are lipid membrane bound particles containing one or more Paramyxovirus envelope proteins in the lipid bilayer. In some embodiments, the one or more Parmyxovirus envelope protein is a Nipah virus (NiV) protein G or F or a biologically active portion or retargeted fusion thereof. In some embodiments, the lipid membrane bound particle is a lentiviral vector. Also provided are related compositions, kits and systems in connection with the provided methods.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes lipid membrane-bound particles (particularly lentiviral vectors) pseudotyped with Paramyxovirus envelope proteins, specifically Nipah virus G or F proteins, to enhance transduction efficiency and cellular targeting. This represents a significant innovation for in vivo CAR-T cell engineering by enabling improved viral vector-mediated gene delivery with enhanced tropism and reduced off-target transduction through pseudotyping with retargeted fusion proteins.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS ET RÉACTIFS POUR AMPLIFIER DES PRODUITS D'ACIDE NUCLÉIQUE DE VECTEUR VIRAL
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods to amplify reverse-transcriptase dependent viral vector nucleic acid products, methods for determining viral vector copy number, and reagents including primers and probes for use in the methods.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents methods and reagents (primers/probes) for amplifying and quantifying reverse-transcriptase-dependent viral vector nucleic acids, enabling improved viral vector copy number determination. This is significant for CAR-T and gene therapy manufacturing as accurate viral titer quantification is critical for product characterization, lot release testing, and ensuring consistent therapeutic dosing of viral vector-based therapeutics.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS DE MODIFICATION DE LYMPHOCYTES T ALLOGÉNIQUES AVEC UN TRANSGÈNE DANS UN LOCUS DE TCR ET COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of producing a composition comprising genetically engineered cells for cell therapy, the method comprising: selecting one or more genetically engineered cells from a population of cells, and formulating the composition comprising the selected one or more genetically engineered cells for use, wherein the one or more genetically engineered cells comprise one or more genetic modifications, and wherein the one or more genetically engineered cells are selected based on a level of one or more markers on the cell surface of the one or more genetically engineered cells, as well as compositions derived therefrom.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent addresses selection and formulation of genetically engineered allogeneic T cells bearing transgenes integrated at the TCR locus, with selection based on cell surface marker levels. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T as it describes a manufacturing approach that combines TCR disruption (enabling allogeneic use) with marker-based quality control to enrich therapeutically functional cells, potentially improving off-the-shelf CAR-T efficacy and consistency.

patents.title: MÉTODOS Y COMPOSICIONES PARA MODULAR LA ACTIVIDAD CAR-T
patents.abstract: La presente invención se refiere a células diseñadas y/o células hipoinmunogénicas que incluyen células madre diseñadas y/o hipoinmunogénicas, células diseñadas y/o hipoinmunogénicas diferenciadas de las mismas, células CAR-T diseñadas y/o hipoinmunogénicas (primarias o diferenciadas de células madre diseñadas y/o hipoinmunogénicas) y métodos relacionados para su uso y generación. La presente invención proporciona células diseñadas y/o hipoinmunogénicas que exhiben expresión reducida de los antígenos de leucocitos humanos MHC de clase I y/o MHC de clase II y receptores de células T. En algunas formas de realización, tales células también expresan exógenamente uno o más factores tolerogénicos tales como CD47 y uno o más receptores de antígenos quiméricos (CAR). patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered hypoimmunogenic cells derived from stem cells with reduced MHC Class I/II expression and T cell receptors, combined with exogenous CAR expression and tolerogenic factors (e.g., CD47). This addresses a key challenge in CAR-T therapy—immune rejection of allogeneic cells—by creating off-the-shelf, universally compatible CAR-T products with enhanced persistence through reduced immunogenicity and improved tolerability.

patents.title: CELLULES GÉNÉTIQUEMENT MODIFIÉES POUR UNE THÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE ALLOGÉNIQUE POUR RÉDUIRE LES RÉACTIONS INFLAMMATOIRES INDUITES PAR LE COMPLÉMENT
patents.abstract: Provided are engineered cells containing one or more modifications, such as genetic modifications, for use in allogeneic cell therapy. In some embodiments, the engineered cells are hypoimmunogenic cells. In some embodiments, the engineered cells comprise increased expression of CD46 and CD59.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses genetically engineered hypoimmunogenic cells with increased expression of complement regulatory proteins CD46 and CD59 to reduce complement-induced inflammatory reactions in allogeneic cell therapy. This addresses a key barrier to off-the-shelf allogeneic cell therapies by engineering immune evasion directly into therapeutic cells, providing competitive advantage for universal donor cell products.

patents.title: CELLULES GÉNÉTIQUEMENT MODIFIÉES POUR UNE THÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE ALLOGÉNIQUE
patents.abstract: Provided are engineered cells containing one or more modifications, such as genetic modifications, for use in allogeneic cell therapy. In some embodiments, the engineered cells are hypoimmunogenic cells.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims engineered, hypoimmunogenic cells with genetic modifications for allogeneic cell therapy, addressing a key challenge in off-the-shelf cellular immunotherapy by reducing host rejection. This is significant for CAR-T as it enables universal donor cell platforms that could eliminate patient-specific manufacturing timelines and costs, directly competing with autologous CAR-T approaches.

patents.title: CELLULES PRIMAIRES GENETIQUEMENT MODIFIEES POUR UNE THERAPIE CELLULAIRE ALLOGENIQUE
patents.abstract:
[0001]    Provided are engineered cells, such as engineered primary cells, containing one or more modifications, such as genetic modifications, for use in allogeneic cell therapy. In some embodiments, the engineered primary cells are hyopimmunogenic cells.

Dans certains modes de réalisation, les cellules primaires modifiées sont des cellules hyopimmunogènes.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered primary cells with genetic modifications designed for allogeneic cell therapy, with specific focus on hypoimmunogenic variants that reduce rejection risk. This is significant for CAR-T as it addresses a major clinical limitation—the ability to use off-the-shelf, allogeneic CAR-T products by engineering away immunogenicity barriers, potentially enabling universal donor cell therapies.

patents.title: CELLULES D'INGÉNIERIE POUR THÉRAPIES CELLULAIRES, ET COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: Provided are methods for genetically modifying cells to knock out or modify one or more genes associated with blood type, e.g., ABO, FUT1, RHD. Also provided are cells and compositions derived therefrom, as well as methods of using the same to treat various human diseases.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent covers genetic modification of cells to knock out or modify blood type-associated genes (ABO, FUT1, RHD), enabling generation of universal donor cells with reduced immunogenicity for allogeneic cell therapies. This is significant for CAR-T and other cellular therapies as it addresses a critical challenge in scaling off-the-shelf cell products by reducing HLA and blood group antigen-driven rejection.

patents.title: SYSTEMES INDUCTIBLES POUR MODIFIER L'EXPRESSION GENIQUE DANS DES CELLULES HYPOIMMUNOGENES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic cells including engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic stem cells, engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic cells differentiated therefrom, and/or engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic CAR-T cells (primary or differentiated from engineered and/or hypoimmunogenic stem cells) and related methods of their use and generation comprising regulatable reduced expression of one or more MHC class I and/or MHC class II human leukocyte antigen molecules and regulatable overexpression of CD47. Provided herein are cells further exhibiting reduced expression of T- cell receptors.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered hypoimmunogenic CAR-T cells with regulatable (inducible) suppression of MHC class I/II and upregulation of CD47, combined with optional TCR reduction. This represents a significant competitive advance for in vivo CAR-T by enabling dynamic immune evasion control, reducing host rejection while maintaining CAR-T persistence and efficacy, with particular value in allogeneic CAR-T applications where hypoimmunogenicity is critical.

patents.title: CELLULES GÉNÉTIQUEMENT MODIFIÉES POUR UNE THÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE ALLOGÉNIQUE PERMETTANT DE RÉDUIRE LES RÉACTIONS INFLAMMATOIRES À MÉDIATION PAR LE SANG INSTANTANÉE
patents.abstract: Provided are engineered cells containing one or more modifications, such as genetic modifications, for use in allogeneic cell therapy. In some embodiments, the engineered cells are hyopimmunogenic cells. In some embodiments, the engineered cells comprise reduced expression of CD 142 and/or are administered in combination with an anti-coagulant.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes hypoimmunogenic engineered cells with reduced CD142 expression for allogeneic cell therapy, designed to minimize inflammatory reactions and blood-mediated coagulation responses. The combination of CD142 downregulation with anticoagulant co-administration represents a strategy to improve safety and efficacy of allogeneic cell products by reducing thromboinflammatory complications, which is significant for clinical translation of off-the-shelf allogeneic cell therapies including CAR-T.

patents.title: UTILISATION DE VECTEURS VIRAUX CIBLANT CD4
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of transducing resting or non-activated T cells using CD4-targeted viral vectors.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.

This is competitively significant as it could improve CAR-T cell manufacturing efficiency, reduce costs, and preserve T cell phenotypes by avoiding activation-associated differentiation.

patents.title: EXPRESSION MODIFIEE D'ANTIGENES LIES AU CHROMOSOME Y DANS DES CELLULES HYPO-IMMUNOGENES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic cells including engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic stem cells, engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic cells differentiated therefrom, and engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic CAR-T cells (primary or differentiated from engineered and/or hypoimmunogenic stem cells) and related methods of their use and generation comprising reduced expression of one or more Y chromosome genes and reduced expression of MHC I and/or MHC II human leukocyte antigen molecules and overexpression of CD47. patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses hypoimmunogenic CAR-T cells engineered with triple modifications: reduced Y chromosome gene expression, reduced MHC I/II expression, and CD47 overexpression, designed to evade immune rejection in allogeneic settings. This combination addresses a critical challenge in off-the-shelf CAR-T therapy by reducing graft rejection and enhancing persistence, offering significant competitive advantage for universal donor CAR-T products.

patents.title: VECTEURS POLYCISTRONIQUES POUR THERAPIES CELLULAIRES
patents.abstract:
[0001]    Provided are polycistronic vectors for co-expression of one or more tolerogenic factors, one or more CARs, and optionally one or more safety switches, as well as compositions comprising the same, cells comprising the same and methods of generating those cells, and methods of using the disclosed vectors, compositions, and cells to treat diseases such as cancer, diabetes, and neurological diseases.
[0002]    L'invention concerne des vecteurs polycistroniques pour la co-expression d'un ou de plusieurs facteurs tolérogènes, d'un ou de plusieurs CAR, et éventuellement une ou plusieurs commutations de sécurité, ainsi que des compositions les comprenant, des cellules les comprenant et des procédés de génération de ces cellules, ainsi que des procédés d'utilisation des vecteurs, compositions et cellules de l'invention pour traiter des maladies telles que le cancer, le diabète et des maladies neurologiques.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes polycistronic vectors enabling simultaneous co-expression of multiple therapeutic components (tolerogenic factors, CAR proteins, and safety switches) in a single genetic construct, addressing the challenge of coordinated multi-gene delivery in cell therapy. This approach enhances therapeutic efficacy and safety profiles for CAR-T and allogeneic cell therapies by eliminating expression imbalances and enabling immune tolerance in allogeneic settings.

patents.title: PARTICULES LIPIDIQUES CONTENANT UNE GLYCOPROTEINE D'ENVELOPPE DE RETROVIRUS ENDOGENE DE BABOUIN (BAEV) TRONQUEE ET METHODES ET UTILISATIONS ASSOCIEES
patents.abstract: Provided herein are lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, that incorporate or are pseudotyped with a truncated Baboon Endogenous Retrovirus (BaEV) envelope glycoprotein that contains a cytoplasmic tail with a partial inhibitory R peptide that is less than the full length wildtype BaEV inhibitory R peptide. Also provided herein are polynucleotides encoding the truncated BaEV envelope glycoproteins and producer cells for preparation of the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles, containing the truncated BaEV envelope glycoproteins, as well as methods for preparing and using the lipid particles, such as lentiviral particles.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents lentiviral particles pseudotyped with truncated BaEV envelope glycoproteins containing partial inhibitory R peptides, representing a modification of the natural envelope protein to enhance particle production and transduction efficiency. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T cell engineering as improved lentiviral vectors with optimized envelope proteins can enable more efficient ex vivo T cell transduction and potentially reduce off-target immunogenicity compared to wildtype pseudotyped vectors.

patents.title: CELLULES HYPOIMMUNOGENES COMPRENANT HLA-E OU HLA-G GENETIQUEMENT MODIFIES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are engineered cells and/or hypoimmunogenic cells including hypoimmunogenic stem cells, hypoimmunogenic cells differentiated therefrom, and hypoimmunogenic CAR-T cells and related methods of their use and generation comprising one or more exogenous receptors selected from the group consisting of a human leukocyte antigen E (HLA-E) variant protein, a human leukocyte antigen G (HLA-G) variant protein, and an exogenous PD-L1 protein. patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.

This addresses a key challenge in off-the-shelf CAR-T therapy by enabling universal donor cells with enhanced persistence and reduced graft-versus-host disease risk.

patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.

patents.title: CONSTRUCTIONS D'ANTICORPS SPECIFIQUES DE CD8 ET COMPOSITIONS ASSOCIEES

patents.title: UTILISATION DE VECTEURS VIRAUX CIBLANT CD8

patents.title: METHODES DE DECLENCHEMENT DE MECANISMES DE DESTRUCTION DE SECURITE AU MOYEN D'UN AGENT DE BLOCAGE CD47-SIRP.ALPHA.

patents.title: METHODS OF TREATING SENSITIZED PATIENTS WITH HYPOIMMUNOGENIC CELLS, AND ASSOCIATED METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are hypoimmunogenic cells for administering to a sensitized patient. In some instances, the patient is sensitized from a previous pregnancy or a previous transplant. patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; Sana Biotechnology, Inc.

patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods of treating or reducing the likelihood of a virus infection, such as a coronavirus infection, by delivering to a subject in need a Chromosome 19 Open Reading Frame 66 (C19orf66) or a regulatory factor that increases expression of the gene encoding C19ord66 in a cell in a subject. Also provided are polynucleotides, proteins, and vehicles (e.g. viral and non-viral vector) and composition thereof, including for use in the methods.

patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.

patents.title: CELLULES NEURALES HYPOIMMUNOGENES POUR LE TRAITEMENT DE TROUBLES ET D'ETATS NEUROLOGIQUES
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are cells including neural cells that evade immune recognition such as microglial response and related methods of their use and generation. patents.title: INTERRUPTEURS DE SECURITE POUR LA REGULATION DE L'EXPRESSION GENIQUE

patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.

This is significant for allogeneic cell therapy as it enables a 'safety switch' mechanism to control immunogenicity dynamically, reducing graft rejection while maintaining therapeutic efficacy through controllable gene expression systems.

patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.

patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.

patents.title: VERFAHREN UND ZUSAMMENSETZUNGEN IM ZUSAMMENHANG MIT CHONDRISOMEN
patents.abstract: Therapeutic chondrisome compositions and related methods are described.
