The invention also provides an application of the antigen binding protein in detection of a chimeric antigen receptor.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS TECH CO LTD; 南京驯鹿医疗技术有限公司; 南京驯鹿生物技术股份有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes neutralizing monoclonal antibodies targeting single-chain antibodies, specifically those recognizing BCMA-targeting CAR constructs. The competitive significance lies in potential diagnostic/detection applications and possibly neutralization strategies for CAR-T therapeutics, though the patent focuses primarily on detection rather than therapeutic enhancement.

patents.title: ANTICORPS ENTIÈREMENT HUMANISÉ CIBLANT CD5
patents.abstract: Provided is a CD5-targeting fully humanized antibody or an antigen binding fragment thereof, which specifically binds to CD5 with a high affinity, has a lower immunogenicity compared with heterologous antibodies, and has a good application potential in the development of an antibody drug, a cell therapy drug detection reagent and the like.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 南京驯鹿医疗技术有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: A fully humanized anti-CD5 antibody or antigen-binding fragment with claimed high affinity binding and reduced immunogenicity compared to heterologous antibodies. Competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is limited as this is an antibody therapeutic rather than a CAR-T cell product, though anti-CD5 targeting could have utility in T-cell depletion or engineering contexts.

patents.title: ANTICORPS ENTIÈREMENT HUMAIN CIBLANT CD5, RÉCEPTEUR ANTIGÉNIQUE CHIMÉRIQUE ENTIÈREMENT HUMAIN (CAR) ET UTILISATION ASSOCIÉE
patents.abstract: Provided is a CD5 antibody. Also provided is a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) that can specifically bind to a CD5 protein, comprising a CD5 binding domain, a transmembrane domain, a costimulatory domain, and an intracellular signaling domain. Also provided is an engineered immune effector cell (such as a T cell) containing the CAR. Also provided is an application of the CAR and the engineered immune effector cell in the treatment of diseases or symptoms related to the expression of CD5.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 南京驯鹿医疗技术有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a fully human CD5-targeting CAR with defined structural domains (CD5 binding domain, transmembrane, costimulatory, and intracellular signaling domains) and its application in engineered T cells for CD5-expressing disease treatment. The competitive significance lies in targeting CD5+ malignancies (particularly T-cell lymphomas and chronic lymphocytic leukemia) with a fully human CAR design, which may reduce immunogenicity compared to chimeric or humanized approaches.

patents.title: ANTICORPS ET RÉCEPTEUR ANTIGÉNIQUE CHIMÉRIQUE (CAR) SE LIANT À CD70, ET APPLICATION ASSOCIÉE
patents.abstract: A CD70 antibody and a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) that can specifically bind to a CD70 protein. The CAR comprises a CD70 binding domain, a transmembrane domain, a costimulatory domain, and an intracellular signaling domain. Further disclosed is an application of the antibody and the CAR for treating diseases or conditions related to CD70 expression.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 南京驯鹿医疗技术有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: This patent discloses CD70-targeting CAR-T cells with a defined architecture (binding domain, transmembrane domain, costimulatory domain, intracellular signaling domain) and associated CD70 antibodies for treating CD70-expressing diseases. The competitive significance lies in expanding the CAR-T target repertoire beyond common hematologic malignancies (CD19, BCMA) to CD70+ malignancies including T-cell lymphomas and solid tumors, though CD70 targeting has been explored in prior literature.

patents.title: RECEPTEUR ANTIGENIQUE CHIMERIQUE BISPECIFIQUE ENTIEREMENT HUMANISE CIBLANT CD19 ET CD22 ET SES UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract:
[0001]    Provided is a bispecific chimeric antigen receptor targeting CD19 and CD22, which comprises extracellular antigen binding domains of heavy-chain variable regions and light-chain variable regions of anti-CD19 and anti-CD22 antibodies. Further provided is a bispecific CAR-T cell targeting CD19 and CD22.
[0002]    L'invention concerne un récepteur antigénique chimérique bispécifique ciblant CD19 et CD22, qui comprend des domaines de liaison à l'antigène extracellulaire de régions variables de chaîne lourde et de régions variables de chaîne légère d'anticorps anti-CD19 et anti-CD22. L'invention concerne en outre une cellule CAR-T bispécifique ciblant CD19 et CD22.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: A fully humanized bispecific CAR targeting both CD19 and CD22 using variable regions from anti-CD19 and anti-CD22 antibodies, enabling dual-antigen recognition in a single engineered receptor. This addresses tumor escape mechanisms in B-cell malignancies by simultaneously engaging two distinct surface antigens, potentially reducing relapse driven by antigen loss variants.

patents.title: VÉSICULES EXTRACELLULAIRES CIBLANT DES CELLULES CANCÉREUSES ET LEURS UTILISATIONS
patents.abstract: Provided are an extracellular vesicle (EV) and a method for producing the EV. The extracellular vesicle comprising a pharmaceutical composition inside the EV and a targeting polypeptide associated with the membrane of the EV for targeted delivery of the pharmaceutical composition.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses extracellular vesicles (EVs) engineered with membrane-associated targeting polypeptides to deliver pharmaceutical compositions to cancer cells. This represents a relevant delivery platform technology that could potentially complement or compete with viral vector and lipid nanoparticle delivery systems used in cell and gene therapy, particularly for in vivo therapeutic delivery.

patents.title: RECEPTEUR ANTIGENIQUE CHIMERIQUE ANTI-CD22 HUMAIN ENTIEREMENT HUMAIN ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract:
[0001]    The present invention provides an anti-CD22 antibody molecule and a CD22-targeted chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) constructed using the anti-CD22 antibody molecule. The present invention also provides an application of the anti-CD22 antibody molecule and the CAR in the preparation of drugs for treating CD22-related diseases.
[0002]    La présente invention concerne une molécule d'anticorps anti-CD22 et un récepteur antigénique chimérique (CAR) ciblant CD22 construit à l'aide de la molécule d'anticorps anti-CD22. La présente invention concerne également une utilisation de la molécule d'anticorps anti-CD22 et du CAR dans la préparation de médicaments pour le traitement de maladies liées à CD22.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a fully human anti-CD22 antibody molecule and a CD22-targeted CAR constructed from this antibody, along with their use in treating CD22-related diseases. The competitive significance lies in the development of a humanized anti-CD22 CAR-T approach, which could reduce immunogenicity compared to murine-derived counterparts and potentially address B-cell malignancies where CD22 is expressed.

patents.title: Fully human antibody targeting CD19 and application thereof
patents.abstract: Provided are a fully human antibody targeting CD19 or a single chain antibody or fragment thereof. Further provided is a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) constructed by using a single chain antibody (scFv) derived from the fully human antibody. The fully human antibody and the CAR can be used for the construction of CAR-T cells targeting CD19. Compared with CAR-T cells using murine antibodies, the CAR-T cells have better compatibility with the human body, which is beneficial to their long-term proliferation and survival in the body.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; NANJING IASO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents a fully human anti-CD19 antibody and its scFv derivative for constructing CD19-targeted CAR-T cells, with claimed advantages in human compatibility, long-term proliferation, and survival compared to murine antibody-based CAR-T cells. The use of fully human rather than chimeric or murine antibodies in the CAR construct addresses potential immunogenicity and rejection issues, offering competitive significance for improved therapeutic durability in in vivo CAR-T applications.

patents.title: T CELL EXPRESSING CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR, CHIMERIC ANTIGEN-RELATED EXPRESSION VECTOR AND USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: Provided is a T cell expressing a chimeric antigen receptor. The chimeric antigen receptor comprises an extracellular domain, and the extracellular domain recognizes a target antigen on the surface ofa target cell, thereby mediating the killing of the target cell by the T cell. The T cell itself also expresses the target antigen, and in order to prevent the T cells from killing each other, the expression of the target antigen in the T cell is down-regulated. An expression vector comprising a sequence coding the chimeric antigen receptor is also provided. The T cell provided can be used to treat diseases caused by abnormal proliferation of CS1 positive cells by targeting CS1 antigen, meanwhile, the T cells are prevented from killing each other due to down-regulation of CS1 expression of the T cell, facilitating expansion and survival of the T cell in vitro and in vivo.
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS TECH CO LTD; 南京驯鹿医疗技术有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents CAR-T cells engineered to target CS1-positive cells while incorporating a mechanism to prevent fratricide through downregulation of CS1 expression on the CAR-T cells themselves. This dual approach of combining CAR targeting with selective antigen downregulation addresses a clinically relevant problem in CAR-T manufacturing and efficacy, particularly for multiple myeloma applications where CS1 is a validated target.

patents.title: CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR (CAR) BINDING TO BCMA, AND APPLICATIONS THEREOF
patents.abstract: To provide a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) which can specifically bind to a B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA), and methods for application of the CAR to treatment of diseases or conditions linked to the expression of BCMA.SOLUTION: The present disclosure provides a CAR that comprises a BCMA-binding domain, a transmembrane domain, a costimulatory domain and an intracellular signal transduction domain, each domain comprising a sequence selected from specific sequences, an immune effector cell that comprises a vector comprising a nucleic acid molecule encoding the CAR, and a composition comprising the immune effector cell.SELECTED DRAWING: Figure 1
patents.assignee: NANJING IASO BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD; INNOVENT BIOLOGICS SUZHOU CO LTD; 南京馴鹿医療技術有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses CAR constructs with BCMA-targeting binding domains combined with specific transmembrane, costimulatory, and intracellular signaling domains, along with immune effector cells engineered to express these CARs. The competitive significance lies in optimizing BCMA-CAR architecture for hematologic malignancies (multiple myeloma, B-cell lymphomas), a clinically validated target with existing approved therapies, potentially differentiating through novel domain combinations or enhanced signaling properties.

patents.title: COMPOSITION ET MÉTHODE D'IMMUNOTHÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE
patents.abstract: The present application relates to a fusion protein having a function of resisting transplantation rejection, and an engineering cell for expressing the fusion protein, further relates to a method for resisting transplant immune rejection, and in particular to a method for resisting NK cell immune rejection. The present application relates to a cellular therapy.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO LTD [CN]; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a fusion protein designed to confer transplantation rejection resistance in engineered cells, particularly against NK cell-mediated immune rejection, combined with methods for cellular immunotherapy. This is significant for CAR-T applications as it addresses a critical challenge in allogeneic cell therapy: engineering cells to evade host NK cell recognition while maintaining therapeutic function.

patents.title: COMPOSITION ET MÉTHODE D'IMMUNOTHÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE
patents.abstract: This disclosure pertains to a nucleic acid encoding a fusion protein that specifically targets CD300A. It also provides pluralities of nucleic acids that further comprise a chimeric receptor-encoding nucleic acid, such as a nucleic acid encoding a NK-targeting CAR. Vectors, compositions, engineered cells, and populations of cells containing such nucleic acids are also provided herein. Uses of these fusion proteins, nucleic acids, vectors, engineered cells, or populations of engineered cells in promoting resistance to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in an allogeneic setting, preventing or treating transplant rejection, and preventing or treating diseases, such as cancers or autoimmune diseases, are also provided herein.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO LTD [CN]; CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO., LTD
patents.novelty_summary: This patent discloses engineered cells (likely CAR-T or NK cells) containing nucleic acids encoding fusion proteins targeting CD300A combined with NK-targeting CAR constructs. The novelty lies in using CD300A-targeting fusion proteins to confer resistance to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in allogeneic cell therapy settings, addressing a major hurdle in off-the-shelf cellular immunotherapy by protecting therapeutic cells from host NK cell rejection while maintaining anti-tumor CAR function.

patents.title: METHOD FOR TREATING TUMOR USING IMMUNE CELL
patents.abstract: The present application provides a new adjuvant treatment method for treating tumors, reducing tumor recurrence, inhibiting tumor growth, or inducing tumor necrosis, wherein the method comprises the following: after selecting patients with cancer (for example, liver cancer, pancreatic cancer, gastric cancer, or gastroesophageal junction tumor) in need thereof for tumor local treatment, a therapeutically effective amount of immune cells (for example, CAR-T cells) is administered as a new adjuvant treatment.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes an adjuvant treatment approach using CAR-T cells administered after local tumor treatment in solid tumors (liver, pancreatic, gastric cancers). The competitive significance lies in positioning CAR-T as a post-local therapy intervention to reduce recurrence and inhibit residual disease, though the specific mechanism of synergy and CAR construct details are not disclosed in the abstract.

patents.title: COMPOSITION POUR IMMUNOTHÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE ET MÉTHODE
patents.abstract: A chimeric receptor having an anti-transplant rejection function, an engineered cell expressing the chimeric receptor, an anti-tumor and anti-transplant immune rejection method, and in particular an anti-NK cell immune rejection method. Also provided is a cell therapy.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered cells expressing chimeric receptors with dual functionality targeting both anti-tumor and anti-transplant rejection responses, with specific focus on NK cell immune rejection. The competitive significance lies in addressing graft rejection in allogeneic cell therapy contexts, potentially enabling off-the-shelf CAR-T products by engineering resistance to host immune responses.

patents.title: CELLULE EFFECTRICE IMMUNITAIRE ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided are an immune effector cell targeting CD19 and CD20, and use thereof. The immune effector cell comprises a scFv targeting CD19 and CD20, a hinge region, a transmembrane region, and an intracellular signal domain. Further provided are a polynucleotide targeting CD19 and CD20, a corresponding expression vector, a CAR-T cell, and use thereof.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a dual-targeting CAR-T cell engineered to simultaneously recognize CD19 and CD20 antigens through a single scFv domain, potentially enabling broader B-cell malignancy coverage while reducing on-target off-tumor toxicity compared to single-antigen CAR-T approaches. This dual-specificity architecture represents a clinically relevant innovation for hematologic cancers where antigen escape and heterogeneous expression are significant treatment failures.

patents.title: Compositions and methods for cellular immunotherapy
patents.abstract: The invention relates to a fusion protein with an anti-transplant rejection function, an engineering cell for expressing the fusion protein, and a method for resisting transplant immunological rejection, in particular to a method for resisting NK (Natural Killer) cell immunological rejection. The invention relates to cell therapy.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered cells expressing a fusion protein designed to evade NK cell-mediated rejection, addressing a critical barrier in allogeneic cell therapy where host NK cells attack transplanted cells. This approach is significant for CAR-T and other cell therapies as it enables off-the-shelf allogeneic cellular products by reducing graft rejection, potentially expanding accessibility and manufacturing scalability compared to autologous approaches.

patents.title: Fusion protein and application thereof
patents.abstract: The invention provides a novel structure targeting FAP and tumor antigen fusion protein, and the application of the novel structure can improve the infiltration of immune effector cells in tumors, improve the tumor microenvironment and improve the killing effect on the tumors.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: A dual-targeting fusion protein that binds both fibroblast activation protein (FAP) and tumor-associated antigens, designed to enhance immune effector cell infiltration into the tumor microenvironment and improve anti-tumor killing efficacy. This approach is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T therapy as it addresses the critical barrier of poor T cell infiltration and hostile TME by creating a bridge between CAR-T cells and the immunosuppressive stroma.

patents.title: MÉTHODE ET COMPOSITION D'IMMUNOTHÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE
patents.abstract: Provided are a fusion protein having a function of preventing transplantation rejection and an engineering cell expressing the fusion protein. The present invention further relates to a method against transplantation immunological rejection, in particular to a method against NK cell immunological rejection.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTIC CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention discloses a fusion protein designed to prevent transplantation rejection when expressed in engineered cells, with specific focus on NK cell-mediated rejection. This is significant for CAR-T and cell therapy applications as it addresses a major clinical challenge of host immune rejection of adoptively transferred therapeutic cells, potentially enabling improved persistence and efficacy of engineered cell therapies in allogeneic settings.

patents.title: CELLULE MODIFIÉE NKG2D ET COMPOSITION ASSOCIÉE
patents.abstract: An engineered immune cell for use in immunotherapy and a preparation method therefor. The engineered immune cell is more persistent in a host organism and has a high transplantation survival rate.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered immune cells with NKG2D modifications designed to improve persistence and transplantation survival in vivo. This addresses a key limitation in adoptive cell therapy by enhancing cell durability post-infusion, which is competitive for CAR-T and NK cell therapies requiring sustained therapeutic activity.

patents.title: POLYPEPTIDE CHIMÉRIQUE ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: Provided are an antibody/T cell receptor chimera carrying different signal peptides and the use thereof. The provided chimeric polypeptide contains a chain A and a chain B, wherein the chain A contains a first antigen binding domain and a first constant region, and the chain B contains a second antigen binding domain and a second constant region: (i) the first and/or second antigen binding domain is a heavy chain or heavy chain variable region of an antibody, which is operably linked to a heavy chain signal peptide or a TCR subunit signal peptide; and (ii) the first and/or second antigen binding domain is a light chain or light chain variable region of an antibody, which is operably linked to a light chain signal peptide or a TCR subunit signal peptide.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO LTD [CN]; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a chimeric polypeptide combining antibody and T cell receptor (TCR) components with flexible signal peptide engineering (antibody-derived or TCR-derived signal sequences on heavy and light chains). The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T lies in optimizing protein expression and trafficking through rational signal peptide selection, potentially improving CAR-T cell manufacturing efficiency and in vivo persistence.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS ET PROCÉDÉS POUR IMMUNOLOGIE CELLULAIRE
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a bispecific molecule targeting NK cells, and relates to a method for resisting transplant immune rejection caused by NK cells, and particularly relates to a method for providing antibodies targeting NK cells or for providing cells which secrete antibodies targeting NK cells, so as to resist transplant immune rejection caused by NK cells of an individual receiving a transplant. The present invention also relates to CRISPR/Cas-related methods, compositions, and components for editing a target nucleic acid sequence or modulating the expression of a target nucleic acid sequence.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO LTD [CN]; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses bispecific molecules targeting NK cells to prevent transplant rejection, combined with CRISPR/Cas-based nucleic acid editing and expression modulation approaches. For CAR-T applications, this is potentially significant as NK cell antagonism could reduce allogeneic rejection of engineered T cell products, and the CRISPR methodology may enable T cell genetic modification as an alternative or complement to viral transduction.

patents.title: ANTICORPS GPRC5D ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present application relates to an antibody that binds to GPRC5D and use thereof. The present application further relates to a cell, a pharmaceutical composition, and a combination therapy comprising the antibody that binds to GPRC5D, and a method for preparing the antibody.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO LTD [CN]; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims anti-GPRC5D antibodies and their use in cellular and pharmaceutical compositions, likely for CAR-T cell engineering where GPRC5D serves as a tumor-associated antigen target. GPRC5D is highly expressed on multiple myeloma and other hematologic malignancies, positioning this as a competitive alternative to established CAR-T targets (BCMA, CD19), with potential advantages in tumors with heterogeneous antigen expression.

patents.title: ANTICORPS NKG2A ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to an antibody targeting NKG2A and an application thereof. Disclosed in the present invention is a novel fully human antibody capable of specifically recognizing NKG2A. The antibody of the present invention can effectively block the binding of HLA-E of tumor cells to NKG2A/CD94 of NK cells, reduces the inhibiting effect of the tumor cells expressing HLA-E on the NK cells by means of NKG2A/CD94 pathway, and enhances the killing effect of the NK cells on the tumor cells.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO LTD [CN]; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: A fully human monoclonal antibody targeting NKG2A that blocks HLA-E:NKG2A/CD94 immune checkpoint interaction on NK cells, thereby relieving NK cell exhaustion and enhancing tumor cytotoxicity. This represents a checkpoint blockade approach complementary to T cell therapies, with potential application in combination with CAR-NK or CAR-T platforms to overcome tumor immunosuppression.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ POUR INDUIRE UNE DIFFÉRENCIATION CELLULAIRE
patents.abstract: Provided are a culture platform, a cell culture medium, and a method for differentiating pluripotent stem cells into a hematopoietic lineage. A pluripotent stem cell-derived hematopoietic lineage produced by using the present culture platform and method can be produced by means of a monolayer culture without serum or trophoblasts, and without forming embryoid bodies. The pluripotent stem cell-derived hematopoietic lineage comprises hematopoietic endothelial cells, hematopoietic stem cells, hematopoietic pluripotent progenitor cells, hematopoietic progenitor cells, T progenitor cells, NK progenitor cells, T cells, and NK cells.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims a serum-free, monolayer culture platform and method for differentiating pluripotent stem cells into hematopoietic lineages including T cells and NK cells without embryoid body formation. This is significant for CAR-T manufacturing as it enables scalable, defined production of T cell progenitors from iPSCs, potentially providing an unlimited cell source for CAR-T cell engineering while reducing cost and variability associated with donor-derived T cells.

patents.title: POLYPEPTIDE CHIMÉRIQUE POUR LA RÉGULATION DE L'ACTIVITÉ PHYSIOLOGIQUE CELLULAIRE
patents.abstract: A chimeric polypeptide, containing a binding peptide that can specifically bind to a target molecule, a receptor regulatory domain containing one or more cleavage sites, and an intracellular domain. The receptor regulatory domain comprises an extracellular region and a transmembrane region, wherein the extracellular region and the transmembrane region are not both derived from a Notch protein. The binding of the binding peptide to the target molecule can induce the cleavage of the receptor regulatory domain, thereby releasing the intracellular domain.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: This patent discloses a chimeric polypeptide with a modular architecture comprising a binding peptide, a receptor regulatory domain (with extracellular and transmembrane regions not both derived from Notch), and an intracellular domain that is released upon ligand-induced cleavage. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is moderate: the design enables conditional activation of signaling through engineered cleavage sites, potentially improving safety and specificity of CAR-T cell therapies by providing additional layers of regulation beyond traditional CAR architectures.

patents.title: MÉTHODE ET COMPOSITION DE TRAITEMENT DE TUMEURS
patents.abstract: A treatment method for administration of immune effector cells to an individual suffering from or suspected of suffering from a CLD18 positive biliary tract tumor, comprising administrating immune effector cells that specifically recognize CLD18.2 to an individual. Pretreatment is performed and then the immune effector cells of the present application are administered, so that the tumor treatment efficacy of the immune effector cells can be remarkably improved.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes immune effector cells engineered to specifically recognize CLD18.2 antigen, applied to CLD18-positive biliary tract tumors with a pretreatment regimen that reportedly enhances efficacy. This represents a targeted CAR-T approach to a challenging solid tumor indication (biliary tract cancer) with a defined pretreatment optimization strategy that could provide competitive advantage in an underserved oncology space.

patents.title: CS1 engineered cells and compositions thereof
patents.abstract: The invention provides an antigen binding unit capable of targeting CS1 and application of the antigen binding unit. The present invention relates to a CS1-targeting antigen binding unit, a chimeric receptor, an immunoconjugate comprising the CS1-targeting antigen binding unit, a chimeric receptor, and nucleic acids encoding the CS1-targeting antigen binding unit, the immunoconjugate, and the chimeric receptor. The invention also relates to application of the CS1-targeting antigen binding unit, the immunoconjugate, the chimeric receptor and the host cell for treating diseases.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes CS1-targeting antigen binding units integrated into chimeric receptors (likely CAR constructs) with corresponding nucleic acid sequences and engineered host cells for therapeutic applications. The competitive significance lies in targeting CS1 (cell surface antigen), a marker expressed on multiple myeloma and other hematologic malignancies, positioning this as a potential alternative or complementary CAR-T approach to existing CD138 or BCMA-targeting therapies.

patents.title: TIGIT engineered cells and compositions thereof
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to engineered immune cells for use in immunotherapy, which are more persistent and/or have a high transplantation survival rate in a host organism, and a method for preparing the same. The invention relates to a genetically engineered cell, characterized in that said cell expresses a first protein that recognizes TIGIT, and to a method for increasing the persistence and/or transplant survival rate of a first immune cell in the presence of a host second immune cell.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes immune cells engineered to express TIGIT-targeting proteins, designed to enhance persistence and transplantation survival in host organisms. This addresses a critical challenge in adoptive cell therapy by improving engraftment and durability, potentially offering competitive advantages over standard CAR-T constructs by combining checkpoint modulation with cellular persistence mechanisms.

patents.title: Method for transduction of cells by viral vectors
patents.abstract: The present invention provides methods of making genetically engineered cells, as well as the obtained cells and compositions thereof transduced with recombinant or heterologous genes, and methods of use in adoptive immunotherapy.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent addresses methods for transducing cells with recombinant/heterologous genes and the resulting genetically engineered cells for adoptive immunotherapy applications. For in vivo CAR-T, the significance lies in potential innovations in viral transduction efficiency or cell engineering approaches that could improve CAR-T manufacturing and therapeutic efficacy, though the abstract lacks sufficient technical specificity to determine competitive differentiation.

patents.title: CELLS AND METHODS RESISTANT TO TRANSPLANTATION REJECTION
patents.abstract: To provide cells resistant to transplantation immunological rejection and methods for resisting inhibition or rejection.SOLUTION: The cell expresses a first protein capable of recognizing one or more immune effector cells of a host. Preferably, the cell has a function of inhibiting or killing the immune effector cells of the host. Also provided are a method for preventing or regulating transplantation immunological rejection, and a method for preventing or regulating attacks on exogenous cells by NK cells.SELECTED DRAWING: None
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD; ▲かい▼興生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered cells expressing proteins that recognize and inhibit/kill host immune effector cells (particularly NK cells) to confer transplantation resistance. This is relevant to allogeneic CAR-T therapy where preventing rejection of infused therapeutic T cells through immunoevasion or immune suppression represents a significant competitive advantage for off-the-shelf cell products.

patents.title: MÉTHODE DE TRANSDUCTION DE CELLULES AVEC UN VECTEUR VIRAL
patents.abstract: Provided is a method for transducing cells with a viral vector, and further provided are cells obtained through recombination or heterologous gene transduction and compositions thereof, and a method for using same in adoptive immunotherapy. Under the premise of not affecting the expression of recombinant nucleic acid, the method shortens the activation and transduction time during the preparation process of genetically engineered cells.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses an optimized viral transduction method that reduces activation and transduction time for genetically engineered cell preparation while maintaining recombinant nucleic acid expression. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T manufacturing by potentially reducing culture time, cost, and labor while improving cell quality and therapeutic efficacy through faster production cycles.

patents.title: Anti-Claudin18.2 antibody and application thereof
patents.abstract: Provided is an antibody or antigen binding fragment capable of recognizing an antigen peptide comprising SEQ ID NO: 7 (KNKKIYDGG); or an epitope containing SEQ ID NO: 7 in the claudin18.2 is identified; preferably, a peptide comprising SEQ ID NO: 6 (KNKKIYDGGART) is identified; or the epitope containing SEQ ID NO: 6 in the claudin18.2 is identified.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD; 佧珐药业有限公司; 上海恺兴诊断技术有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes antibodies or antigen-binding fragments targeting a specific epitope (SEQ ID NO: 7: KNKKIYDGG) within claudin18.2, a tumor-associated antigen. While claudin18.2 is a known target, the novelty lies in the specific epitope recognition and antibody characterization, with competitive significance for immunotherapy applications including potential CAR-T engineering where anti-claudin18.2 CAR-T cells are being developed for solid tumors.

patents.title: CELLULE EFFECTRICE IMMUNITAIRE EXPRIMANT IL-15
patents.abstract: Provided is an immune effector cell expressing IL-15; the cells express IL-15 and recognize receptors for specific target antigens, or the cells express IL-15R binding molecules and receptors that recognize specific target antigens. Also provided are a nucleic acid molecule, an IL-15R binding molecule or IL-15 or IL-15 and chemokine expressed by said nucleic acid molecule, a chemokine receptor, a cytokine other than IL-7, an siRNA which reduces PD-1 expression, a protein which blocks the binding of PD-L1 to PD-1, or a safety switch.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes immune effector cells engineered to express IL-15 and antigen-recognition receptors (likely CAR-T cells), with optional IL-15R signaling molecules and checkpoint inhibition (PD-1 reduction). The competitive significance lies in leveraging IL-15's known benefits for T cell proliferation, persistence, and anti-tumor activity without requiring exogenous cytokine administration, potentially improving CAR-T efficacy and manufacturing scalability in vivo.

patents.title: CELLULE EFFECTRICE IMMUNITAIRE DANS LAQUELLE L'EXPRESSION EST RÉGULÉE PAR DES CYTOKINES
patents.abstract: Provided is a genetically engineered immune effector cell, wherein the immune effector cell expresses a receptor specifically recognizing a target antigen and IL7, and the IL-7 performs an inducible expression and is regulated by the receptor. Further provided are a nucleic acid molecule expressing the immune effector cell and a method for preparing the immune effector cell.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a genetically engineered immune effector cell (likely CAR-T) with inducible IL-7 expression regulated by the target-recognition receptor itself, creating a feedback loop where cytokine production is triggered upon antigen engagement. This represents a novel approach to enhance CAR-T cell persistence and proliferation through receptor-controlled cytokine secretion, potentially improving efficacy and reducing systemic toxicity compared to constitutive IL-7 expression.

patents.title: CELLULE EFFECTRICE IMMUNITAIRE POUR CO-EXPRIMER UN RÉCEPTEUR DE CHIMIOKINE
patents.abstract: Provided are an immune effector cell for co-expressing a chemokine receptor, a pharmaceutical composition, a kit, and a method for treating a tumor. The immune effector cell comprises a receptor that specifically recognizes claudin 18.2 and a protein that recognizes SDF-1. Further provided are an expression construct, an expression vector, and a virus. The expression construct comprises an expression of a receptor that binds to a tumor-associated antigen and an expression of the protein that recognizes SDF-1, which are connected in sequence.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents immune effector cells (likely CAR-T cells) engineered to co-express a claudin 18.2-targeting receptor alongside an SDF-1-recognizing protein (CXCR4), designed to enhance tumor homing and infiltration. The novelty lies in the dual-receptor engineering strategy combining tumor-specific recognition with chemokine-axis engagement for improved trafficking to the tumor microenvironment, particularly relevant for gastric cancer and other claudin 18.2-expressing malignancies.

patents.title: TCR FUSION PROTEIN AND CELL EXPRESSING TCR FUSION PROTEIN
patents.abstract: Disclosed is a T cell receptor (TCR) fusion protein (TFP). The fusion protein comprises a TCR subunit (or referred to as a TCR unit) and an antigen recognition unit that recognizes an antigen. The antigen is GPC3 or claudin 18.2. Also disclosed is a T cell containing the fusion protein, a pharmaceutical composition and an application method of using the fusion protein or the T cell to treat diseases such as cancer. The use of TFP or T cells not only inhibits the growth of tumor cells, but also releases fewer cytokines, thereby effectively reducing the possibility of cytokine storms.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD; 佧珐药业有限公司; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a TCR fusion protein combining a TCR subunit with an antigen recognition unit targeting GPC3 or claudin 18.2, along with T cells expressing this fusion protein. The competitive significance lies in the claimed reduction of cytokine release compared to conventional CAR-T approaches, potentially mitigating cytokine release syndrome (CRS) — a major clinical limitation in adoptive T cell therapy. This represents a structural alternative to conventional CAR constructs for solid tumor targeting.

patents.title: CELLULAR IMMUNOTHERAPY COMBINATION
patents.abstract: Disclosed is a tumor treatment method, characterized in that immune effector cells and gemcitabine are administered to an individual with a tumor, and the immune effector cells express receptors having a tumor-specific antigen. Also disclosed is a tumor treatment kit, characterized in that the kit comprises 1) immune effector cells expressing receptors that recognize tumor antigens; 2) gemcitabine; 3) a container for for containing the substances of 1) and 2) described above; and 4) drug administration instructions for using the kit to treat a tumor.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; SHANGHAI CANCER INST; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a combination therapy approach pairing immune effector cells (CAR-T cells) with gemcitabine chemotherapy for tumor treatment. The novelty centers on the synergistic use of engineered T cells with a conventional chemotherapeutic agent, which addresses potential challenges in CAR-T monotherapy such as tumor microenvironment immunosuppression and antigen escape. This combination strategy is competitively significant as it may enhance efficacy and overcome resistance mechanisms in solid tumors.

patents.title: GEGEN GPC3 GERICHTETE IMMUNEFFEKTORZELLE UND ANWENDUNG DAVON
patents.abstract: [0001]    The present invention relates to an immune effector cell which expresses a chimeric antigen receptor targeting GPC3 and exogenous IL12. The present invention further provides a pharmaceutical composition containing the immune effector cell and a method for treating tumor, particularly GPC3 positive tumor by using the immune effector cell or the pharmaceutical composition. The immune effector cell in the present invention is effective to an entity tumor cell in vitro, and is outstanding in effect of extinguishing the entity tumor cell in vivo.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; CRAGE MEDICAL CO LTD [CN]
patents.novelty_summary: The invention combines a GPC3-targeting CAR-T cell with exogenous IL-12 expression to enhance anti-tumor efficacy against solid tumors, demonstrating improved in vivo tumor control compared to conventional CAR-T approaches. The dual engineering strategy addresses a key challenge in CAR-T therapy: insufficient infiltration and persistence in immunosuppressive solid tumor microenvironments through cytokine co-expression.

patents.title: TUMOR COMBINED IMMUNOTHERAPY
patents.abstract: Provided is a method for tumor treatment, comprising administering immune effector cells and a PARP inhibitor to an individual suffering from a tumor, the immune effector cells expressing a receptor for identifying a tumor antigen. Further provided is a kit for tumor treatment.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; SHANGHAI CANCER INST; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent combines CAR-T (or similar immune effector cells with tumor antigen receptors) with PARP inhibitor co-administration to enhance tumor treatment efficacy. This synergistic approach leverages immunotherapy with DNA repair inhibition, potentially increasing CAR-T cell penetration, tumor immunogenicity, or overcoming immunosuppressive microenvironments—a combination not commonly disclosed in standard CAR-T monotherapy patents.

patents.title: CLL1-TARGETING ANTIBODY AND APPLICATION THEREOF
patents.abstract: Provided are a CLL1-targeting antibody and an application thereof. The CLL1-specific antibody has high affinity for CLL1, and after being prepared into a chimeric antigen receptor-modified T cell, has a significant killing effect on cells expressing CLL1.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD; 佧珐药业有限公司; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a CLL1-targeting antibody with high affinity for CLL1 antigen and its application in generating CAR-T cells with enhanced cytotoxic activity against CLL1-expressing cells. The competitive significance lies in enabling improved CAR-T therapeutics for hematologic malignancies (particularly acute myeloid leukemia and chronic lymphocytic leukemia) by providing optimized single-chain variable fragment or antibody-derived recognition domains.

patents.title: CHEMOKINE EXPRESSING CELL AND USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a chemokine expressing cell. The cell expresses an exogenous IL-21R binding protein or an exogenous IL-21 and an exogenous chemokine. Further provided is a cell expressing an exogenous receptor, an exogenous IL-21R binding protein or an exogenous IL-21 and an exogenous chemokine. The cell involved is not only effective in solid tumor cells in vitro, but also has an excellent killing effect on solid tumor cells in vivo.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; SHANGHAI CANCER INST; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered cells expressing exogenous IL-21R binding proteins or IL-21 combined with exogenous chemokines to enhance infiltration and killing of solid tumors both in vitro and in vivo. This represents a multi-functional cell therapy approach combining immune stimulation (IL-21 signaling) with chemotactic recruitment, addressing a key challenge in CAR-T efficacy against solid tumors.

patents.title: T-CELL EXPRESSING CHIMERIC RECEPTOR
patents.abstract: Provided is a T-cell expressing a chimeric receptor, wherein the chimeric receptor specifically recognizes BCMA, and the endogenous TCR molecule and the endogenous MHC molecule are silenced. Also provided is the use of the T-cell in the preparation of a drug for treating BCMA positive tumors.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD; 佧珐药业有限公司; 克莱格医学有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims T-cells engineered with a BCMA-targeting chimeric receptor (CAR-T) where both endogenous TCR and MHC molecules are silenced to reduce off-target recognition and immunogenicity. This dual knockdown approach (TCR and MHC silencing combined with CAR expression) represents a strategy to enhance CAR-T specificity and reduce alloimmune rejection, offering potential competitive advantage in BCMA+ hematologic malignancies where allogeneic CAR-T applications are pursued.

patents.title: METHOD FOR TREATING TUMOR USING IMMUNE EFFECTOR CELL
patents.abstract: Provided are an immune effector cell expressing a chimeric antigen receptor that gives individual specific recognition BCMA, and a treatment method applying the immune effector cell. The method can improve the tumor treatment efficacy of the immune effector cell.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes immune effector cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) with individual-specific recognition of BCMA (B-cell maturation antigen), combined with methods for treating tumors using these cells. The claimed novelty appears to focus on improved tumor treatment efficacy, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific mechanistic or structural innovations that would distinguish this from existing BCMA-directed CAR-T therapies.

patents.title: GENETISCH VERÄNDERTE ZELLE UND IHRE VERWENDUNG
patents.abstract: [0001]    Disclosed in the present invention is a genetically engineered cell, expressing an exogenous receptor that specifically binds to a target antigen and exogenous CCL21, and capable of further expressing an IL-7R binding protein or exogenous IL-7 that promotes cell proliferation. Also disclosed are an expression construct comprising an exogenous CCL21 expression cassette, and a vector containing same, a virus, and a pharmaceutical composition comprising said cell. Also disclosed is an application for the cell, the expression construct, the vector, and the virus in the preparation of drugs for inhibiting tumours or inhibiting pathogens.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; CAFA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IE]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims genetically engineered cells expressing an exogenous antigen-specific receptor (CAR-T), CCL21, and IL-7/IL-7R signaling components to enhance T cell proliferation and persistence. The co-expression of chemokine (CCL21) and IL-7 signaling in CAR-T cells represents a novel approach to improve cell trafficking, expansion, and anti-tumor efficacy, with competitive significance for enhancing CAR-T cell manufacturing and in vivo performance.

patents.title: MANIPULIERTE IMMUNEFFEKTORZELLEN UND VERWENDUNG DAVON
patents.abstract: A geneticall engineered cell. The cell expresses an exogenous receptor binding to an antigen, and expresses increased RUNX3 or exogenous RUNX3. Also provided are a use of the cell and a method for treating tumors.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; CAFA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IE]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses genetically engineered immune effector cells with exogenous antigen-binding receptors (likely CAR constructs) combined with elevated or exogenous RUNX3 expression to enhance T cell function and anti-tumor efficacy. The co-expression strategy targeting RUNX3, a transcription factor regulating T cell differentiation and effector function, represents a potentially novel approach to improve CAR-T cell persistence, phenotype, and therapeutic potency in vivo.

patents.title: 종양 치료 방법 및 조성물
patents.abstract: 본 발명은 면역 효과기 세포의 조성물을 제공하고, 여기서, 상기 면역 효과기 세포의 조성물은 처음 사용량의 면역 효과기 세포 및 후속 사용량의 면역 효과기 세포, 및 이러한 면역 효과기 세포의 조성물을 포함하는 치료용 키트를 포함한다.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; 카르스젠 테라퓨틱스 리미티드
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes compositions of immune effector cells with sequential dosing regimens (initial and subsequent doses) and associated therapeutic kits for tumor treatment. The novelty centers on the dosing strategy and formulation approach for immune effector cell therapy, which could offer competitive advantages in optimizing CAR-T cell persistence, expansion, and anti-tumor efficacy through staged administration protocols.

patents.title: COMBINATION OF CELLULAR IMMUNOTHERAPY
patents.abstract: [0001]    Provided in the present invention is a method for treating tumor. An immune effector cell and a second treatment agent are applied to individual suffering from tumor, wherein the immune effector cell expresses a receptor for recognizing tumor antigen, and wherein the second treatment agent is a compound of formula I or a pharmaceutically acceptable salt thereof.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI CANCER INST [CN]; CRAGE MEDICAL CO LTD [HK]
patents.novelty_summary: The invention combines immune effector cells expressing tumor antigen-recognizing receptors (consistent with CAR-T architecture) with a defined small-molecule second treatment agent (formula I compound). The competitive significance lies in the combination strategy to enhance therapeutic efficacy and potentially overcome resistance mechanisms in solid tumors, though the specific identity and mechanism of formula I compounds are not disclosed in the abstract.

patents.title: ＳｙｎＮｏｔｃｈ受容体によるＩＬ１２の発現調節
patents.abstract: 本発明は、免疫治療分野に属し、具体的にバイナリーベクターおよびｓｙｎＮｏｔｃｈ技術を使用して標的抗原依存性調節サイトカインの発現の提供により、サイトカインを部分的に放出してＴ細胞の機能を増強し、同時にサイトカインの非特異的毒性副作用を低減する。合成ｎｏｔｃｈ受容体を使用して、プラスミドベクターを構築することにより、サイトカインの局所分泌を実現する。１つのプラスミドベクターは、標的抗原を認識するための特異的抗体を細胞外ドメインとして使用し、Ｎｏｔｃｈコアは膜貫通ドメインとｎｏｔｃｈ受容体上の特異的の酵素切断部位を含み、ＧＡＬ４ＶＰ６４は細胞内ドメインとして使用される。標的抗原が認識されると、ｎｏｔｃｈの酵素切断部位は対応する酵素によって認識され、細胞内転写因子ＧＡＬ４ＶＰ６４を加水分解および切断される。別のプラスミドベクターは、ＧＡＬ４転写因子のＤＮＡ認識結合領域ＧＡＬ４ＵＡＳおよび対応する標的遺伝子を活性化する最小プロモーターを有し、ＧＡＬ４ＶＰ６４が加水分解および切断された後、結合領域に結合して、後続の遺伝子の転写を活性化して、ＩＬ１２を発現しかつ細胞外に分泌する。
patents.assignee: カースゲン  セラピューティクス  カンパニー  リミテッドＣＡＲＳＧＥＮ  ＴＨＥＲＡＰＥＵＴＩＣＳ  ＣＯ．，  ＬＴＤ．; 上海市腫瘤研究所ＳＨＡＮＧＨＡＩ  ＣＡＮＣＥＲ  ＩＮＳＴＩＴＵＴＥ
patents.novelty_summary: The invention uses synthetic Notch receptor technology with binary plasmid vectors to enable antigen-dependent, localized IL-12 secretion from T cells, combining a recognition module (antibody-based extracellular domain) with a transcriptional activation module (GAL4-VP64 intracellular domain) to enhance T cell function while reducing off-target cytokine toxicity. This represents a novel approach to conditional cytokine expression in cell therapies by engineering synthetic receptor-driven gene circuits that decouple cytokine release from systemic exposure.

patents.title: 線維芽細胞活性化タンパク質αを標的とする結合ユニットとその応用
patents.abstract: 本発明は、ＦＡＰαに特異的に結合する結合ユニット、そのような結合ユニットをコードするポリヌクレオチド、そのようなポリヌクレオチドを含むベクターおよび宿主細胞に関する。本発明はさらに、前記抗原結合ユニットを生成する方法および本発明のＦＡＰα特異的に結合ユニットを使用して疾患を治療する方法に関する。本発明のＦＡＰαに特異的に結合する結合ユニットは、ＦＡＰαを発現する腫瘍細胞に効果的に結合でき、前記結合ユニットを含む免疫エフェクター細胞はＦＡＰを発現する腫瘍細胞に対して有意な殺傷能力を示す。【選択図】なし
patents.assignee: 科済生物医薬（上海）有限公司ＣＡＲＳＧＥＮ  ＴＨＥＲＡＰＥＵＴＩＣＳ  ＣＯ．，ＬＴＤ．; 上海市腫瘍研究所ＳＨＡＮＧＨＡＩ  ＣＡＮＣＥＲ  ＩＮＳＴＩＴＵＴＥ
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes binding units (likely CAR-T constructs) that specifically target FAP-α (fibroblast activation protein alpha), a tumor-associated antigen, along with polynucleotides encoding these units and methods for their generation and therapeutic use. The competitive significance lies in targeting the tumor microenvironment via FAP-α, enabling immune effector cells to achieve substantial cytotoxic activity against FAP-α-expressing tumor cells—a validated approach for addressing tumor heterogeneity and stromal components.

patents.title: Method for improving immune response cell function
patents.abstract: The invention relates to a method for improving the function of immune response cells. The invention discloses an immune response cell which expresses at least one receptor capable of binding to an antigen and type I interferon. The immune response cell is applied to treatment of tumors, infectious diseases and other diseases, and has remarkable and excellent capability of killing tumors or pathogens.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes immune response cells engineered to co-express antigen-binding receptors (likely CAR-T) with type I interferon, enhancing anti-tumor and anti-pathogen killing capacity. This represents a potentially significant advance for in vivo CAR-T by addressing immunosuppression through endogenous type I IFN production, improving both intrinsic T cell function and the tumor microenvironment.

patents.title: PARTICULE VIRALE PSEUDOTYPÉE ET SON UTILISATION
patents.abstract: A pseudotyped viral particle having a Maraba virus envelope glycoprotein or a variant thereof. The surface of the pseudotyped virus envelope comprises an immune cell targeting molecule and/or an immune cell activating molecule. A corresponding targeting molecule is designed according to a cell receptor to be targeted, and can target different types of cells, including immunotherapy cells such as CAR-T and CAR-NK.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI IMMUNOFOCO PHARMACEUTICAL RES CO LTD [CN]; CHENGDU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes pseudotyped viral particles with Maraba virus envelope glycoproteins engineered to display immune cell targeting and/or activating molecules on their surface. The novelty lies in the dual functionality of targeting specific cell receptors while simultaneously activating immune cells, with explicit application to CAR-T and CAR-NK cell engineering, offering a potentially improved delivery platform for immunotherapy cell generation or activation.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉDICTION D'UNE RÉPONSE DE TRAITEMENT À UNE THÉRAPIE CELLULAIRE IMMUNITAIRE DE TUMEUR SOLIDE
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a method for predicting a solid tumor immune cell therapy treatment response. The method comprises acquiring a tumor tissue section from a patient, and detecting the presence, number, proportion or density of one or more cell types in the tumor tissue section. A solid tumor immune cell therapy response is predicted by determining cell markers, such as α-SMA, CD3, CD4 or CD8, associated with the cell types. In addition, the present invention also relates to a kit used for predicting a solid tumor treatment response, including a reagent which detects expression levels of one or more cell types and cell markers in tumor tissue sections, and software and/or a user manual used for analyzing detection results. The method and kit provide an effective tool for clinical treatment, so as to optimize dosages and clinical regimens of immune cell therapy, thereby improving treatment response rates.
patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI IMMUNOFOCO PHARMACEUTICAL RES CO LTD [CN]; CHENGDU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents a predictive biomarker panel (α-SMA, CD3, CD4, CD8) for stratifying solid tumor patients likely to respond to cell-based immunotherapy, potentially enabling patient selection and treatment optimization. This addresses a significant clinical need in CAR-T therapy by providing pre-treatment tissue analysis to predict therapeutic response in solid tumors, where CAR-T efficacy remains limited.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉ DE CULTURE DE LYMPHOCYTES T
patents.abstract: A T-cell culture method. Micron-sized CD3/28 dual anti-magnetic beads and human platelet lysate are used to culture engineered T-cells, so that the viability of the engineered T-cells can be effectively improved. The present application has a large application prospect in the field of immune cell therapy.
patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI IMMUNOFOCO PHARMACEUTICAL RES CO LTD [CN]; CHENGDU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a T-cell culture method utilizing micron-sized CD3/CD28 dual anti-magnetic beads combined with human platelet lysate to enhance viability of engineered T-cells. This represents a targeted approach to improving ex vivo T-cell expansion conditions, potentially offering manufacturing advantages for CAR-T and other engineered T-cell therapies through optimized stimulation and culture media supplementation.

patents.title: IMMUNE CELLS TARGETING EPCAM AND MEDICAL USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present invention relates to the technical field of biomedicine, and specifically relates to immune cells targeting EpCAM and a medical use thereof. Provided is a use of immune cells in the preparation of a drug for preventing or treating a tumor; the immune cells are cells for adoptive immune cell therapy, which can target and kill EpCAM-expressing cells; and the tumor expresses EpCAM and is a metastatic tumor.
patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SUZHOU IMMUNOHEAD BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO., LTD
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims immune cells engineered to target EpCAM-expressing tumors for adoptive cell therapy, specifically applied to metastatic cancers. The competitive significance lies in addressing EpCAM as a tumor-associated antigen in metastatic disease, which is a common target in CAR-T development but the specific claims appear limited to use statements rather than novel engineering mechanisms or constructs.

patents.title: CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR CONTAINING CLDN18.2 SINGLE DOMAIN ANTIBODY AND APPLICATION THEREOF
patents.abstract: A chimeric antigen receptor containing a CLDN18.2 single domain antibody and an application thereof. The constructed chimeric antigen receptor is good in specificity, higher in safety in vivo use, and smaller in toxicity, and can provide a treatment solution for patients who suffer from advanced gastric cancer caused by high expression of a CLDN18.2 protein and currently undergo radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and surgery treatments.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHENZHEN IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a CAR-T construct using a CLDN18.2-targeting single domain antibody (sdAb) as the recognition domain, offering improved specificity and reduced in vivo toxicity compared to conventional full-length antibody-based CARs. This is competitively significant for gastric cancer treatment as CLDN18.2 is a validated tumor-associated antigen with high expression in gastric adenocarcinomas, and the smaller sdAb format may enhance tissue penetration and safety profiles in solid tumors.

patents.title: NOUVELLE COMPOSITION DE RÉCEPTEUR CHIMÉRIQUE, VECTEUR RECOMBINANT, CELLULE ET UTILISATION ASSOCIÉE
patents.abstract: A novel chimeric receptor composition, a recombinant vector, a cell, and an application thereof. The novel chimeric receptor composition comprises a conventional chimeric antigen receptor (CAR), and an NKG2D chimeric receptor comprising full-length sequences or truncated fragments of NKG2D, DAP10, and/or DAP12, referred to as a SNR-armed CAR. The chimeric receptor composition enables a conventional CAR-T cell to express an NKG2D extracellular region and an intracellular signal region, expands a CAR-T antigen recognition spectrum, solves the tumor heterogeneity, achieves a lower level of factor release while enhancing the killing capability of CAR-T on tumor cells expressing target antigens, reduces the possibility of factor storm occurrence, and improves the CAR-T security.
patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 苏州易慕峰生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a dual-receptor CAR-T architecture combining conventional CAR with an NKG2D chimeric receptor (SNR-armed CAR) to expand antigen recognition spectrum and address tumor heterogeneity. This represents a clinically significant advancement for in vivo CAR-T efficacy by reducing cytokine release while maintaining enhanced tumor-killing capability and improving safety profile.

patents.title: HUMANISIERTER ANTIKÖRPER, CHIMÄRER ANTIGENREZEPTOR, NUKLEINSÄURE, VEKTOR, ZELLE UND VERWENDUNG
patents.abstract: Provided are a humanized antibody specifically binding to EpCAM, and a chimeric antigen receptor, a nucleic acid, a vector, a cell, and the use associated with the humanized antibody. The humanized antibody comprises a heavy chain variable region and a light chain variable region. The sequence of the heavy chain variable region comprises a sequence shown in SEQ ID.1, a sequence shown in SEQ ID.2 and a sequence shown in SEQ ID.3. The sequence of the light chain variable region comprises a sequence shown in SEQ ID.4, a sequence shown in SEQ ID.5, and a sequence shown in SEQ ID.6. After the humanized antibody is constructed as a chimeric antigen receptor-T Cell, EpCAM-positive tumor cells can be specifically identified and killed, and tumors can be cleared in an animal bod
patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; Suzhou Immunofoco Biotechnology Co., Ltd.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a humanized anti-EpCAM antibody with defined variable region sequences (CDRs in SEQ ID.1-6) engineered into a CAR-T construct for targeting EpCAM-positive tumors. The novelty lies in the specific humanized antibody design and its application as a functional CAR-T therapeutic with demonstrated tumor cell killing capacity in vivo, providing a potentially less immunogenic alternative to murine-derived CAR-T constructs targeting this epithelial antigen.

patents.title: METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS FOR TRANSDUCING AND EXPANDING LYMPHOCYTES AND REGULATING THE ACTIVITY THEREOF
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present disclosure provides methods for genetically modifying lymphocytes and methods for performing adoptive cellular therapy that include transducing T cells and/or NK cells. The methods can include inhibitory RNA molecule(s) and/or engineered signaling polypeptides that can include a lymphoproliferative element, and/or a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR), for example a microenvironment restricted biologic CAR (MRB-CAR). Additional elements of such engineered signaling polypeptides are provided herein, such as those that drive proliferation and regulatory elements therefor, as well as replication incompetent recombinant retroviral particles and packaging cell lines and methods of making the same. Numerous elements and methods for regulating transduced and/or genetically modified T cells and/or NK cells are provided, such as, for example, those including riboswitches, MRB-CARs, recognition domains, and/or pH-modulating agents.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; Exuma Biotech Corp.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses microenvironment-restricted biologic CAR (MRB-CAR) constructs combined with methods for T/NK cell transduction and expansion using inhibitory RNA molecules and engineered signaling polypeptides. The competitive significance lies in the MRB-CAR technology platform, which appears designed to provide spatial/contextual control of CAR activity to reduce off-target toxicity in vivo, a critical unmet need in CAR-T therapy safety.

patents.title: ANTI-IDIOTYPE COMPOSITIONS AND METHODS OF USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions that include a polynucleotide that includes nucleic acids that encode an anti-idiotype polypeptide, as well as polypeptides that are encoded by the same, and cells that include and express the polypeptide. Disclosed methods include methods that utilize the anti-idiotype polypeptides as safety switches when they are used in combination with antibodies, include approved biologic antibodies, that include the recognized idiotype. Certain embodiments include anti-idiotype polypeptides and nucleotides encoding the same, that include an internal domain. This internal domain in some embodiments has functional domains that can induce proliferation or cell death upon binding of the anti-idiotype polypeptide by its target antibody.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; Exuma Biotech Corp.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses anti-idiotype polypeptides with internal functional domains that act as safety switches for antibody-based therapies, capable of inducing proliferation or cell death upon target binding. This is significant for CAR-T and cell therapy as it provides a controllable kill-switch or checkpoint mechanism that could be engineered into therapeutic cells to enhance safety and reduce off-target toxicity in vivo.

patents.title: PARTICULES VIRALES COMPRENANT DE L'HYALURONIDASE LIÉE À UNE MEMBRANE
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods, uses, compositions, and kits that include hyaluronidase polypeptides, including for example retroviral particles that include membrane bound hyaluronidase polypeptides, and novel, chimeric hyaluronidase polypeptides. Furthermore, provided herein are methods, uses, compositions, and kits that include hyaluronidase polypeptides, including for example retroviral particles that encode hyaluronidases and/or that include membrane bound hyaluronidases, which in some embodiments are novel, chimeric hyaluronidases provided herein. Accordingly, provided herein are replication incompetent recombinant retroviral particles (RIP), and methods using the same, that comprise a viral envelope, a nucleic acid encoding a packaging signal, Gag, and a membrane-bound hyaluronidase.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; EXUMA BIOTECH CORP.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses replication-incompetent retroviral particles with membrane-bound hyaluronidase, designed to enhance tissue penetration and transduction efficiency. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery as hyaluronidase degrades the extracellular matrix (hyaluronic acid), potentially improving viral vector penetration into solid tumors and tissues, addressing a key barrier to effective T cell gene therapy.

patents.title: METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS FOR THE DELIVERY OF MODIFIED LYMPHOCYTES AND/OR RETROVIRAL PARTICLES
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present disclosure provides methods and compositions for genetically modifying lymphocytes, for example T cells and/or NK cells. In some embodiments, the methods include reaction mixtures, and resulting cell formulations, that are created using whole blood, or a component thereof that is not a PBMC, and additionally comprise T cells and recombinant retroviral particles having polynucleotides that encode a CAR. In some embodiments, modified lymphocytes are reintroduced into a subject subcutaneously. In some embodiments, polynucleotides that provide T cells the ability to regulate cell survival and proliferation in response to binding to a CAR, are provided.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; Exuma Biotech Corp.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses methods for generating CAR-T cells using whole blood or non-PBMC blood components, combined with compositions of modified lymphocytes and retroviral particles encoding CAR constructs. Notably, it claims subcutaneous reintroduction of modified lymphocytes and incorporation of polynucleotides conferring CAR-regulated survival/proliferation signaling, which may offer advantages in manufacturing simplicity and cell control over standard leukapheresis-dependent approaches.

patents.title: PROCEDES ET COMPOSITIONS POUR L'ADMINISTRATION DE PARTICULES RETROVIRALES
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions for modifying lymphocytes, for example T cells and/or NK cells, for example in vivo. The disclosed compositions can include replication incompetent recombinant retroviral particles (RIPs), formulations thereof, and administration of RIP formulations to a subject. Furthermore, the compositions can include chemokines, including chemokines delivered and/or associated with RIPs.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; EXUMA BIOTECH CORP.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent discloses methods and compositions for in vivo modification of T cells and NK cells using replication-incompetent recombinant retroviral particles (RIPs), with novel integration of chemokines delivered alongside or associated with RIPs to enhance targeting and transduction efficiency. The competitive significance lies in enabling direct in vivo lymphocyte engineering without ex vivo manufacturing, potentially reducing manufacturing costs and time-to-therapy compared to conventional CAR-T approaches.

patents.title: PROCÉDÉS ET COMPOSITIONS POUR L'ADMINISTRATION DE PARTICULES RÉTROVIRALES
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions for modifying lymphocytes, for example T cells and/or NK cells, for example in vivo. The disclosed compositions can include replication incompetent recombinant retroviral particles (RIPs), formulations thereof, and administration of RIP formulations to a subject. Furthermore, the compositions can include chemokines, including chemokines delivered and/or associated with RIPs.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; EXUMA BIOTECH CORP.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents in vivo lymphocyte modification using replication-incompetent retroviral particles (RIPs) combined with chemokine co-delivery/association to enhance targeting and transduction efficiency of T cells and NK cells. This addresses a significant competitive advantage in in vivo CAR-T by potentially improving transduction kinetics and homing without requiring ex vivo cell manipulation, potentially reducing manufacturing complexity and time-to-treatment.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS ANTI-IDIOTYPE ET PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION ASSOCIÉS
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions that include a polynucleotide that includes nucleic acids that encode an anti-idiotype polypeptide, as well as polypeptides that are encoded by the same, and cells that include and express the polypeptide. Disclosed methods include methods that utilize the anti-idiotype polypeptides as safety switches when they are used in combination with antibodies, include approved biologic antibodies, that include the recognized idiotype. Certain embodiments include anti-idiotype polypeptides and nucleotides encoding the same, that include an internal domain. This internal domain in some embodiments has functional domains that can induce proliferation or cell death upon binding of the anti-idiotype polypeptide by its target antibody.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; EXUMA BIOTECH CORP.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses anti-idiotype polypeptides encoded by polynucleotides with internal functional domains that can act as safety switches for therapeutic antibodies, inducing proliferation or cell death upon target binding. This represents a novel approach to controlling antibody therapeutics through encoded anti-idiotype mechanisms, with potential application as a kill-switch or control mechanism in cell therapy contexts.

patents.title: MÉTHODES ET COMPOSITIONS POUR L'ADMINISTRATION D'AGRÉGATS DE LYMPHOCYTES MODIFIÉS
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions for genetically modifying lymphocytes, for example T cells and/or NK cells. In some embodiments, the methods include reaction mixtures, and resulting cell formulations, that are created using whole blood, or a component thereof that is not a PBMC, and additionally comprise T cells and recombinant retroviral particles having polynucleotides that encode a CAR. In some embodiments, modified lymphocytes are reintroduced into a subject subcutaneously. In some embodiments, polynucleotides that provide T cells the ability to regulate cell survival and proliferation in response to binding to a CAR, are provided.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; EXUMA BIOTECH CORP.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims novel methods for generating CAR-T cells directly from whole blood or non-PBMC blood components using retroviral transduction, combined with compositions of modified lymphocyte aggregates. The competitive significance lies in potentially simplified manufacturing by circumventing traditional PBMC isolation steps, and in subcutaneous reintroduction routes that may reduce manufacturing complexity and costs for in vivo CAR-T therapy.

patents.title: RECEPTEURS ANTIGENIQUES CHIMERIQUES DIRIGES VERS HER2 ET LEURS PROCEDES D'UTILISATION
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), and nucleic acids comprising nucleotide sequences encoding the CARs, that bind to HER2, and conditionally active biologic (CAB) CARs that bind to HER2. The present disclosure provides cells genetically modified to produce the CARs, delivery suspensions comprising these genetically modified cells, and methods for making such cells. The CARs of the present disclosure can be used in various methods, which are also provided, including methods for activating immune cells under certain conditions, and methods for performing adoptive cell therapy such as CAR therapy, for example CAR therapy against cancer.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; BIOATLA LLC [US]; EXUMA BIOTECH CORP.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses HER2-targeting chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) with conditional activation capability (CAB-CARs), along with genetically modified T cells expressing these CARs and methods for their manufacture and therapeutic use. The conditional activation feature represents a potentially significant advance for in vivo CAR-T by enabling spatially or temporally controlled T cell activation, potentially reducing off-target toxicity and improving therapeutic index in HER2-positive cancers.

patents.title: METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS FOR GENETICALLY MODIFYING LYMPHOCYTES TO EXPRESS POLYPEPTIDES COMPRISING THE INTRACELLULAR DOMAIN OF MPL
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions for genetically modifying lymphocytes, for example T cells and/or NK cells, in shorter times than previously and/or in whole blood or a component thereof. In some embodiments a lymphodepletion filter assembly is used before or after forming a reaction mixture where lymphocytes are contacted with recombinant retroviral particles in a closed system, to genetically modify the lymphocytes.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; Exuma Biotech Corp.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents methods for rapid genetic modification of lymphocytes (T cells and NK cells) using recombinant retroviral particles in closed systems, with optional lymphodepletion filtration to enhance transduction efficiency. The competitive significance lies in accelerated manufacturing timelines and integration of lymphodepletion within a closed-system bioprocess, reducing handling steps and improving scalability for CAR-T cell manufacturing.

patents.title: METHODES ET COMPOSITIONS POUR LA MODIFICATION ET L'ADMINISTRATION DE LYMPHOCYTES
patents.abstract:

In some embodiments, the methods include reaction mixtures, and resulting cell formulations, that are created using whole blood, or a component thereof that is not a PBMC, and additionally comprise T cells and recombinant retroviral particles having polynucleotides that encode a CAR. In some embodiments, modified lymphocytes are reintroduced into a subject subcutaneously. In some embodiments, polynucleotides that provide T cells the ability to regulate cell survival and proliferation in response to binding to a CAR, are provided.
